texts.luk.1.79: To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shades of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
texts.luk.1.80: And the child grew, and became strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of his showing to Israel.
texts.luk.2.1: And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Cesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.
texts.luk.2.2: (And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.)
texts.luk.2.3: And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city.
texts.luk.2.4: And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David)
texts.luk.2.5: To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.
texts.luk.2.6: And so it was, that while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered.
texts.luk.2.7: And she brought forth her first-born son, and wrapped him in swaddling-clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
texts.luk.2.8: And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.
texts.luk.2.9: And lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them; and they were in great fear.
texts.luk.2.10: And the angel said to them, Fear not: for behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy which shall be to all people.
texts.luk.2.11: For to you is born this day, in the city of David, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
texts.luk.2.12: And this shall be a sign to you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling-clothes, lying in a manger.
texts.luk.2.13: And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying,
texts.luk.2.14: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will towards men.
texts.luk.2.15: And it came to pass, when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another, Let us now go even to Bethlehem, and see this thing which is come to pass, which the Lord hath made known to us.
texts.luk.2.16: And they came with haste, and found Mary and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.
texts.luk.2.17: And when they had seen it, they made known abroad the saying which was told them concerning this child.
texts.luk.2.18: And all they that heard it, wondered at those things which were told them by the shepherds.
texts.luk.2.19: But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
texts.luk.2.20: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told to them.
texts.luk.2.21: And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, who was so named by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
texts.luk.2.22: And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord;
texts.luk.2.23: (As it is written in the law of the Lord, Every male that is the first born of his mother shall be called holy to the Lord)
texts.luk.2.24: And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtle-doves, or two young pigeons.
texts.luk.2.25: And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
texts.luk.2.26: And it was revealed to him by the Holy Spirit, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ.
texts.luk.2.27: And he came by the spirit into the temple; and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law,
texts.luk.2.28: Then he took him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said,
texts.luk.2.29: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word:
texts.luk.2.30: For my eyes have seen thy salvation,
texts.luk.2.31: Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people;
texts.luk.2.32: A light to enlighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.
texts.luk.2.33: And Joseph and his mother marveled at those things which were spoken concerning him.
texts.luk.2.34: And Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary his mother, Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel; and for a sign which shall be spoken against;
texts.luk.2.35: (And a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.
texts.luk.2.36: And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher: she was of a great age, and had lived with a husband seven years from her virginity;
texts.luk.2.37: And she was a widow of about eighty four years, who departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
texts.luk.2.38: And she coming in that instant, gave thanks likewise to the Lord, and spoke of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.
texts.luk.2.39: And when they had performed all things according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
texts.luk.2.40: And the child grew, and became strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.
texts.luk.2.41: Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.
texts.luk.2.42: And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast.
texts.luk.2.43: And when they had fulfilled the days, as they returned, the child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem; and Joseph and his mother knew not of it.
texts.luk.2.44: But they, supposing him to be in the company, went a day's journey; and they sought him among their relations and acquaintance.
texts.luk.2.45: And when they found him not, they returned to Jerusalem, seeking him.
texts.luk.2.46: And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
texts.luk.2.47: And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.
texts.luk.2.48: And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said to him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.
texts.luk.2.49: And he said to them, How is it that ye sought me? knew ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
texts.luk.2.50: And they understood not the saying which he spoke to them.
texts.luk.2.51: And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them: but his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
texts.luk.2.52: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.
texts.luk.3.1: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Cesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Iturea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanius the tetrarch of Abilene,
texts.luk.3.2: Annas and Caiaphas being the high priests, the word of God came to John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness.
texts.luk.3.3: And he came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance, for the remission of sins;
texts.luk.3.4: As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
texts.luk.3.5: Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth;
texts.luk.3.6: And all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
texts.luk.3.7: Then said he to the multitude that came forth to be baptized by him, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
texts.luk.3.8: Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham for our father: for I say to you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children to Abraham.
texts.luk.3.9: And now also the ax is laid to the root of the trees: every tree therefore which bringeth not forth good fruit, is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
texts.luk.3.10: And the people asked him, saying, What shall we do then?
texts.luk.3.11: He answereth and saith to them, He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath provisions, let him do likewise.
texts.luk.3.12: Then came also publicans to be baptized, and said to him, Master, what shall we do?
texts.luk.3.13: And he said to them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you.
texts.luk.3.14: And the soldiers likewise asked him, saying, And what shall we do? And he said to them, Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely, and be content with your wages.
texts.luk.3.15: And as the people were in expectation, and all men mused in their hearts concerning John, whether he was the Christ, or not;
texts.luk.3.16: John answered, saying to them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit, and with fire:
texts.luk.3.17: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor, and will gather the wheat into his granary; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.
texts.luk.3.18: And many other things in his exhortation he preached to the people.
texts.luk.3.19: But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him on account of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done,
texts.luk.3.20: Added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.
texts.luk.3.21: Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened,
texts.luk.3.22: And the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.
texts.luk.3.23: And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, who was the son of Heli,
texts.luk.3.24: Who was the son of Matthat, who was the son of Levi, who was the son of Melchi, who was the son of Janna, who was the son of Joseph,
texts.luk.3.25: Who was the son of Mattathias, who was the son of Amos, who was the son of Naum, who was the son of Esli, who was the son of Nagge,
texts.luk.3.26: Who was the son of Maath, who was the son of Mattathias, who was the son of Semei, who was the son of Joseph, who was the son of Juda,
texts.luk.3.27: Who was the son of Joanna, who was the son of Rhesa, who was the son of Zorobabel, who was the son of Salathiel, who was the son of Neri,
texts.luk.3.28: Who was the son of Melchi, who was the son of Addi, who was the son of Cosam, who was the son of Elmodam, who was the son of Er,
texts.luk.3.29: Who was the son of Jose, who was the son of Eliezer, who was the son of Jorim, who was the son of Matthat, who was the son of Levi,
texts.luk.3.30: Who was the son of Simeon, who was the son of Judah, who was the son of Joseph, who was the son of Jonan, who was the son of Eliakim,
texts.luk.3.31: Who was the son of Melea, who was the son of Menan, who was the son of Mattatha, who was the son of Nathan, who was the son of David,
texts.luk.3.32: Who was the son of Jesse, who was the son of Obed, who was the son of Booz, who was the son of Salmon, who was the son of Naasson,
texts.luk.3.33: Who was the son of Aminadab, who was the son of Aram, who was the son of Esrom, who was the son of Phares, who was the son of Judah,
texts.luk.3.34: Who was the son of Jacob, who was the son of Isaac, who was the son of Abraham, who was the son of Terah, who was the son of Nahor,
texts.luk.3.35: Who was the son of Serug, who was the son of Reu, who was the son of Peleg, who was the son of Heber, who was the son of Sala,
texts.luk.3.36: Who was the son of Cainan, who was the son of Arphaxad, who was the son of Shem, who was the son of Noah, who was the son of Lamech,
texts.luk.3.37: Who was the son of Methuselah, who was the son of Enoch, who was the son of Jared, who was the son of Maleleel, who was the son of Cainan,
texts.luk.3.38: Who was the son of Enos, who was the son of Seth, who was the son of Adam, who was the son of God.
texts.luk.4.1: And Jesus being full of the Holy Spirit, returned from Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,
texts.luk.4.2: Being forty days tempted by the devil. And in those days he ate nothing; and when they were ended, he was afterward hungry.
texts.luk.4.3: And the devil said to him, If thou art the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.
texts.luk.4.4: And Jesus answered him, saying, It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.
texts.luk.4.5: And the devil taking him up upon a high mountain, showed to him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
texts.luk.4.6: And the devil said to him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered to me, and to whomsoever I will, I give it.
texts.luk.4.7: If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.
texts.luk.4.8: And Jesus answered and said to him, Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
texts.luk.4.9: And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, If thou art the son of God, cast thyself down from hence.
texts.luk.4.10: For it is written, He will give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee:
texts.luk.4.11: And in their hands they will bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.
texts.luk.4.12: And Jesus answering, said to him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
texts.luk.4.13: And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.
texts.luk.4.14: And Jesus returned in the power of the spirit into Galilee: and there went out a fame of him through all the surrounding region.
texts.luk.4.15: And he taught in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
texts.luk.4.16: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath, and stood up to read.
texts.luk.4.17: And there was delivered to him the book of the prophet Isaiah. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,
texts.luk.4.18: The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the broken-hearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,
texts.luk.4.19: To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.
texts.luk.4.20: And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on him.
texts.luk.4.21: And he began to say to them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
texts.luk.4.22: And all bore him testimony, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph's son?
texts.luk.4.23: And he said to them, Ye will surely say to me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.
texts.luk.4.24: And he said, Verily I say to you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.
texts.luk.4.25: But I tell you in truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut three years and six months when great famine was throughout all the land:
texts.luk.4.26: But to none of them was Elijah sent, save to Sarepta, a city of Sidon, to a woman that was a widow.
texts.luk.4.27: And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.
texts.luk.4.28: And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,
texts.luk.4.29: And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
texts.luk.4.30: But he passing through the midst of them, went away,
texts.luk.4.31: And came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath-days.
texts.luk.4.32: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.
texts.luk.4.33: And in the synagogue there was a man who had a spirit of an unclean demon; and he cried out with a loud voice,
texts.luk.4.34: Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.
texts.luk.4.35: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. And when the demon had thrown him in the midst, he came out of him, and hurt him not.
texts.luk.4.36: And they were all amazed, and spoke among themselves, saying, What a word is this! for with authority and power he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they come out.
texts.luk.4.37: And the fame of him went out into every place of the surrounding country.
texts.luk.4.38: And he arose out of the synagogue, and entered into Simon's house. And the mother of Simon's wife was taken with a violent fever; and they besought him for her.
texts.luk.4.39: And he stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her: and immediately she arose and ministered to them.
texts.luk.4.40: Now when the sun was setting, all they that had any sick with divers diseases, brought them to him: and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
texts.luk.4.41: And demons also came out of many, crying out, and saying, Thou art Christ the Son of God. And he rebuking them, suffered them not to speak: for they knew that he was Christ.
texts.luk.4.42: And when it was day, he departed, and went into a desert place; and the people sought him, and came to him, and stayed him, that he should not depart from them.
texts.luk.4.43: And he said to them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also, for therefore am I sent.
texts.luk.4.44: And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee.
texts.luk.5.1: And it came to pass, that as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret.
texts.luk.5.2: And saw two boats standing by the lake: but the fishermen had gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
texts.luk.5.3: And he entered into one of the boats, which was Simon's, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the boat.
texts.luk.5.4: Now when he had left speaking, he said to Simon, Lanch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.
texts.luk.5.5: And Simon answering said to him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing; nevertheless, at thy word I will let down the net.
texts.luk.5.6: And when they had done this, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net broke.
texts.luk.5.7: And they beckoned to their partners, who were in the other boat, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the boats, so that they began to sink.
texts.luk.5.8: When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
texts.luk.5.9: For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken:
texts.luk.5.10: And so was also James and John the sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, Fear not: from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
texts.luk.5.11: And when they had brought their boats to land, they forsook all, and followed him.
texts.luk.5.12: And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold, a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus, fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
texts.luk.5.13: And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: Be thou clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.
texts.luk.5.14: And he charged him to tell no man: but go, and show thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded for a testimony to them.
texts.luk.5.15: But so much the more a fame of him went abroad: and great multitudes came together to hear and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
texts.luk.5.16: And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.
texts.luk.5.17: And it came to pass on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, who had come out of every town of Galilee, and Judea, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
texts.luk.5.18: And behold, men brought in a bed a man who was taken with the palsy: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
texts.luk.5.19: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in, because of the multitude, they went upon the house-top, and let him down through the tiling with his couch, into the midst before Jesus.
texts.luk.5.20: And when he saw their faith, he said to him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.
texts.luk.5.21: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this who speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone?
texts.luk.5.22: But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering, said to them, What reason ye in your hearts?
texts.luk.5.23: Which is easier, to say, Thy sins are forgiven thee; or to say, Rise and walk?
texts.luk.5.24: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, He said to the sick with the palsy, I say to thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thy house.
texts.luk.5.25: And immediately he arose before them, and took up that on which he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.
texts.luk.5.26: And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to-day.
texts.luk.5.27: And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said to him, Follow me.
texts.luk.5.28: And he left all, arose, and followed him.
texts.luk.5.29: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house; and there was a great company of publicans, and of others that sat down with them.
texts.luk.5.30: But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners?
texts.luk.5.31: And Jesus answering, said to them, They that are well need not a physician; but they that are sick.
texts.luk.5.32: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
texts.luk.5.33: And they said to him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink?
texts.luk.5.34: And he said to them, Can ye make the children of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
texts.luk.5.35: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then they will fast in those days.
texts.luk.5.36: And he spoke also a parable to them: No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old: if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new, agreeth not with the old.
texts.luk.5.37: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles will perish.
texts.luk.5.38: But new wine must be put into new bottles, and both are preserved.
texts.luk.5.39: No man also having drank old wine, immediately desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.
texts.luk.6.1: And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through corn-fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and ate, rubbing them in their hands.
texts.luk.6.2: And certain of the Pharisees said to them, Why do ye that which it is not lawful to do on the sabbath-days?
texts.luk.6.3: And Jesus answering them, said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was hungry, and they who were with him;
texts.luk.6.4: How he went into the house of God, and took and ate the show-bread, and gave also to them that were with him, which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?
texts.luk.6.5: And he said to them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
texts.luk.6.6: And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue, and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered:
texts.luk.6.7: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, to see whether he would heal on the sabbath; that they might find an accusation against him.
texts.luk.6.8: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man who had the withered hand, Rise, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose, and stood forth.
texts.luk.6.9: Then said Jesus to them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath-days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it?
texts.luk.6.10: And looking around upon them all, he said to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
texts.luk.6.11: And they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.
texts.luk.6.12: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out to a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
texts.luk.6.13: And when it was day, he called to him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named Apostles;
texts.luk.6.14: Simon (whom he also named Peter) and Andrew his brother, James and John, and Philip and Bartholomew,
texts.luk.6.15: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alpheus, and Simon called Zelotes,
texts.luk.6.16: And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, who also was the traitor.
texts.luk.6.17: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain; and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judea and Jerusalem, and from the sea-coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;
texts.luk.6.18: And they that were afflicted with unclean spirits: and they were healed.
texts.luk.6.19: And the whole multitude sought to touch him; for there went virtue out of him, and healed them all.
texts.luk.6.20: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed are ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.6.21: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.
texts.luk.6.22: Blessed are ye when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, on account of the son of man.
texts.luk.6.23: Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers to the prophets.
texts.luk.6.24: But woe to you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.
texts.luk.6.25: Woe to you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe to you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.
texts.luk.6.26: Woe to you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
texts.luk.6.27: But I say to you who hear, Love your enemies, do good to them who hate you,
texts.luk.6.28: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them who despitefully use you.
texts.luk.6.29: And to him that smiteth thee on the one cheek, offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloke, forbid not to take thy coat also.
texts.luk.6.30: Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods, ask them not again.
texts.luk.6.31: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.
texts.luk.6.32: For if ye love them who love you, what thanks have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.
texts.luk.6.33: And if ye do good to them who do good to you, what thanks have ye? for sinners also do even the same.
texts.luk.6.34: And if ye lend to them from whom ye hope to receive, what thanks have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much in return.
texts.luk.6.35: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind to the unthankful and to the evil.
texts.luk.6.36: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
texts.luk.6.37: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:
texts.luk.6.38: Give, and it shall be given to you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye give to others, it shall be measured to you again.
texts.luk.6.39: And he spoke a parable to them; Can the blind lead the blind? will they not both fall into the ditch?
texts.luk.6.40: The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect, shall be as his master.
texts.luk.6.41: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but perceivest not the beam that is in thy own eye?
texts.luk.6.42: Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thy eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thy own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thy own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother's eye.
texts.luk.6.43: For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
texts.luk.6.44: For every tree is known by its own fruit: for from thorns men do not gather figs, nor from a bramble bush do they gather grapes.
texts.luk.6.45: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart, bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart, bringeth forth that which is evil: for from the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.
texts.luk.6.46: And why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?
texts.luk.6.47: Whoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will show you to whom he is like.
texts.luk.6.48: He is like a man who built a house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.
texts.luk.6.49: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that, without a foundation, built a house on the earth, against which the stream beat vehemently, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great.
texts.luk.7.1: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
texts.luk.7.2: And a certain centurion's servant, who was dear to him, was sick, and ready to die.
texts.luk.7.3: And when he heard of Jesus, he sent to him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.
texts.luk.7.4: And when they came to Jesus, they besought him earnestly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:
texts.luk.7.5: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.
texts.luk.7.6: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof;
texts.luk.7.7: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come to thee; but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.
texts.luk.7.8: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say to one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
texts.luk.7.9: When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turned himself about and said to the people that followed him, I say to you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
texts.luk.7.10: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant well that had been sick.
texts.luk.7.11: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain: and many of his disciples went with him, and many people.
texts.luk.7.12: Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and many people of the city were with her.
texts.luk.7.13: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said to her, Weep not.
texts.luk.7.14: And he came and touched the bier: And they that bore him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say to thee, Arise.
texts.luk.7.15: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak, and he delivered him to his mother.
texts.luk.7.16: And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet hath risen among us; and, That God hath visited his people.
texts.luk.7.17: And this rumor of him went forth throughout all Judea, and throughout all the neighboring region.
texts.luk.7.18: And the disciples of John informed him of all these things.
texts.luk.7.19: And John calling two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
texts.luk.7.20: When the men had come to him, they said, John the Baptist hath sent us to thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
texts.luk.7.21: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities, and diseases, and of evil spirits; and to many that were blind he gave sight.
texts.luk.7.22: Then Jesus answering, said to them, Go, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; that the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.
texts.luk.7.23: And blessed is he, to whom I shall not be a stumbling block.
texts.luk.7.24: And when the messengers of John had departed, he began to speak to the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
texts.luk.7.25: But what went ye out to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they who are gorgeously appareled, and live delicately, are in kings' courts.
texts.luk.7.26: But what went ye out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and much more than a prophet.
texts.luk.7.27: This is he, concerning whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, who shall prepare thy way before thee.
texts.luk.7.28: For I say to you, Among those that are born of women, there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God, is greater than he.
texts.luk.7.29: And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
texts.luk.7.30: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized by him.
texts.luk.7.31: And the Lord said, To what then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?
texts.luk.7.32: They are like children sitting in the market-place, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped to you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.
texts.luk.7.33: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread, nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a demon.
texts.luk.7.34: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold, a gluttonous man, and a wine-bibber, a friend of publicans and sinners.
texts.luk.7.35: But wisdom is justified by all her children.
texts.luk.7.36: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee's house, and sat down at table.
texts.luk.7.37: And behold, a woman in the city, who was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at table in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster-box of ointment,
texts.luk.7.38: And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
texts.luk.7.39: Now when the Pharisee who had invited him, saw it, he spoke within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who, and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him, for she is a sinner.
texts.luk.7.40: And Jesus answering, said to him, Simon, I have somewhat to say to thee. And he saith, Master, speak.
texts.luk.7.41: There was a certain creditor, who had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.
texts.luk.7.42: And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?
texts.luk.7.43: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said to him, Thou hast rightly judged.
texts.luk.7.44: And he turned to the woman, and said to Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thy house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.
texts.luk.7.45: Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman, since the time I came in, hath not ceased to kiss my feet.
texts.luk.7.46: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment.
texts.luk.7.47: Wherefore I say to thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
texts.luk.7.48: And he said to her, Thy sins are forgiven.
texts.luk.7.49: And they that sat at table with him, began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgiveth sins also?
texts.luk.7.50: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.
texts.luk.8.1: And it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and showing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God: and the twelve were with him,
texts.luk.8.2: And certain women, who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven demons.
texts.luk.8.3: And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, who ministered to him of their substance.
texts.luk.8.4: And when many people were collected, and had come to him out of every city, he spoke by a parable:
texts.luk.8.5: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.
texts.luk.8.6: And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered, because it lacked moisture.
texts.luk.8.7: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.
texts.luk.8.8: And other fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bore fruit a hundred-fold. And when he had said these things, he cried, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.luk.8.9: And his disciples asked him, saying, What doth this parable mean?
texts.luk.8.10: And he said, To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to others in parables; that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
texts.luk.8.11: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
texts.luk.8.12: Those by the way side, are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.
texts.luk.8.13: They on the rock are they, who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, who for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.
texts.luk.8.14: And that which fell among thorns are they, who, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.
texts.luk.8.15: But that on the good ground are they, who in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
texts.luk.8.16: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but setteth it on a candlestick, that they who enter in may see the light.
texts.luk.8.17: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known, and come abroad.
texts.luk.8.18: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whoever hath, to him shall be given; and whoever hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he seemeth to have.
texts.luk.8.19: Then came to him his mother and his brethren, and could not come near to him for the crowd.
texts.luk.8.20: And it was told to him by certain, who said, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.
texts.luk.8.21: And he answered and said to them, My mother and my brethren are these who hear the word of God, and do it.
texts.luk.8.22: Now it came to pass on a certain day, that he went into a boat with his disciples: and he said to them, Let us go over to the other side of the lake. And they lanched forth.
texts.luk.8.23: But as they sailed, he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filled with water, and were in jeopardy.
texts.luk.8.24: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he arose, and rebuked the wind, and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm.
texts.luk.8.25: And he said to them, Where is your faith? And they being afraid, wondered, saying one to another, What manner of man is this! for he commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey him.
texts.luk.8.26: And they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is over against Galilee.
texts.luk.8.27: And when he went forth to land, there met him out of the city a certain man, who had demons a long time, and wore no clothes, neither abode in any house, but in the tombs.
texts.luk.8.28: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God most high? I beseech thee torment me not.
texts.luk.8.29: (For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For often it had caught him, and he was kept bound with chains, and in fetters: and he broke the bands, and was driven by the demon into the wilderness.)
texts.luk.8.30: And Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many demons had entered into him.
texts.luk.8.31: And they besought him, that he would not command them to go out into the deep.
texts.luk.8.32: And there was there a herd of many swine feeding on the mountain: and they besought him that he would suffer them to enter into them. And he suffered them.
texts.luk.8.33: Then the demons went out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked.
texts.luk.8.34: When they that fed them saw what was done, they fled, and went and told it in the city and in the country.
texts.luk.8.35: Then they went out to see what was done; and came to Jesus, and found the man out of whom the demons had departed, sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
texts.luk.8.36: They also who saw it, told them by what means he that was possessed by the demons was healed.
texts.luk.8.37: Then the whole multitude of the surrounding country of the Gadarenes, besought him to depart from them: for they were taken with great fear. And he went into the boat, and returned.
texts.luk.8.38: Now the man out of whom the demons had departed, besought him that he might be with him. But Jesus sent him away, saying,
texts.luk.8.39: Return to thy own house, and show how great things God hath done to thee. And he went away and published throughout the whole city, how great things Jesus had done to him.
texts.luk.8.40: And it came to pass, that, when Jesus had returned, the people gladly received him: for they were all waiting for him.
texts.luk.8.41: And behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue: and he fell down at the feet of Jesus, and besought him that he would come into his house:
texts.luk.8.42: For he had one daughter only, about twelve years of age, and she lay dying. (But as he was going, the people thronged him.
texts.luk.8.43: And a woman having an issue of blood twelve years, who had spent all her living upon physicians, neither could be healed by any,
texts.luk.8.44: Came behind him, and touched the border of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched.
texts.luk.8.45: And Jesus said, Who touched me? When all denied, Peter, and they that were with him, said, Master, the multitude throng thee, and press thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
texts.luk.8.46: And Jesus said, Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue hath gone out of me.
texts.luk.8.47: And when the woman saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him, she declared to him before all the people for what cause she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
texts.luk.8.48: And he said to her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.
texts.luk.8.49: While he was yet speaking, there cometh one from the house of the ruler of the synagogue, saying to him, Thy daughter is dead: trouble not the Master.
texts.luk.8.50: But when Jesus heard it, he answered him, saying, Fear not: believe only, and she shall be healed.
texts.luk.8.51: And when he came into the house, he suffered no man to go in, save Peter, and James, and John, and the father and the mother of the maiden.
texts.luk.8.52: And all wept and bewailed her: but he said, Weep not: she is not dead, but sleepeth.
texts.luk.8.53: And they derided him, knowing that she was dead.
texts.luk.8.54: And he put them all out, and took her by the hand, and called, saying, Maid, arise.
texts.luk.8.55: And her spirit came again, and she arose immediately: and he commanded to give her food.
texts.luk.8.56: And her parents were astonished: but he charged them that they should tell no man what was done.
texts.luk.9.1: Then he called his twelve disciples together, and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.
texts.luk.9.2: And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.
texts.luk.9.3: And he said to them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staffs, nor bag, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece.
texts.luk.9.4: And into whatever house ye enter, there abide, and thence depart.
texts.luk.9.5: And whoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
texts.luk.9.6: And they departed, and went through the towns, preaching the gospel, and healing every where.
texts.luk.9.7: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him: and he was perplexed, because that it was said by some, that John had risen from the dead;
texts.luk.9.8: And by some, that Elijah had appeared; and by others, that one of the ancient prophets had risen again.
texts.luk.9.9: And Herod said, John have I beheaded; but who is this of whom I hear such things? And he desired to see him.
texts.luk.9.10: And the apostles, when they had returned, told him all that they had done. And he took them, and went aside privately into a desert place, belonging to the city called Bethsaida.
texts.luk.9.11: And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spoke to them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.
texts.luk.9.12: And when the day began to decline, then came the twelve, and said to him, Send the multitude away, that they may go into the towns and country around, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place.
texts.luk.9.13: But he said to them, Give ye them to eat. And they said, We have no more than five loaves and two fishes; except we should go and buy provisions for all this people.
texts.luk.9.14: For they were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit down by fifties in a company.
texts.luk.9.15: And they did so, and made them all sit down.
texts.luk.9.16: Then he took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed them, and broke, and gave to the disciples to set before the multitude.
texts.luk.9.17: And they ate, and were all satisfied: and there was taken up of fragments that remained to them, twelve baskets.
texts.luk.9.18: And it came to pass, as he was in retirement praying, his disciples were with him; and he asked them, saying, Who say the people that I am?
texts.luk.9.19: They answering, said, John the Baptist; but some say, Elijah; and others say, that one of the ancient prophets is risen again.
texts.luk.9.20: He said to them, But who say ye that I am? Peter answering, said, Christ of God.
texts.luk.9.21: And he strictly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing,
texts.luk.9.22: Saying, The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and be put to death, and be raised the third day.
texts.luk.9.23: And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.
texts.luk.9.24: For whoever will save his life, shall lose it: but whoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.
texts.luk.9.25: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?
texts.luk.9.26: For whoever shall be ashamed of me, and of my words, of him will the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory, and in that of his Father, and of the holy angels.
texts.luk.9.27: But I tell you in truth, there are some standing here who shall not taste death till they see the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.9.28: And it came to pass, about eight days after these sayings, he took Peter, and John, and James, and went up upon a mountain to pray.
texts.luk.9.29: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistening.
texts.luk.9.30: And behold, there talked with him two men, who were Moses and Elijah.
texts.luk.9.31: Who appeared in glory, and spoke of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
texts.luk.9.32: But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.
texts.luk.9.33: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah: not knowing what he said.
texts.luk.9.34: While he was thus speaking, there came a cloud and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.
texts.luk.9.35: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
texts.luk.9.36: And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.
texts.luk.9.37: And it came to pass, that on the next day, when they had come down from the hill, many people met him.
texts.luk.9.38: And behold, a man of the company cried out, saying, Master, I beseech thee look upon my son: for he is my only child.
texts.luk.9.39: And lo, a spirit taketh him, and he suddenly crieth out; and it teareth him that he foameth, and bruising him, hardly departeth from him.
texts.luk.9.40: And I besought thy disciples to cast him out, and they could not.
texts.luk.9.41: And Jesus answering, said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and suffer you? Bring thy son hither.
texts.luk.9.42: And as he was yet coming, the demon threw him down, and tore him. And Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the child, and delivered him again to his father.
texts.luk.9.43: And they were all amazed at the mighty power of God. But while they were all wondering at all things which Jesus did, he said to his disciples,
texts.luk.9.44: Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man will be delivered into the hands of men.
texts.luk.9.45: But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not: and they feared to ask him concerning that saying.
texts.luk.9.46: Then there arose a reasoning among them, which of them should be greatest.
texts.luk.9.47: And Jesus perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him,
texts.luk.9.48: And said to them, Whoever shall receive this child in my name, receiveth me; and whoever shall receive me, receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great.
texts.luk.9.49: And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out demons in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us.
texts.luk.9.50: And Jesus said to him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us, is for us.
texts.luk.9.51: And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he steadfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,
texts.luk.9.52: And sent messengers before his face: and they went and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.
texts.luk.9.53: And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.
texts.luk.9.54: And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elijah did?
texts.luk.9.55: But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.
texts.luk.9.56: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. And they went to another village.
texts.luk.9.57: And it came to pass, that as they were going in the way, a certain man said to him, Lord, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
texts.luk.9.58: And Jesus said to him, Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
texts.luk.9.59: And he said to another, Follow me. But he said, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.
texts.luk.9.60: Jesus said to him, Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.9.61: And another also said, Lord, I will follow thee; but let me first go and bid them farewell who are at my house.
texts.luk.9.62: And Jesus said to him, No man having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.10.1: After these things, the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city, and place, whither he himself would come.
texts.luk.10.2: Therefore said he to them, The harvest truly is great, but the laborers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth laborers into his harvest.
texts.luk.10.3: Go: behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves.
texts.luk.10.4: Carry neither purse, nor sack, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.
texts.luk.10.5: And into whatever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house.
texts.luk.10.6: And if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it: if not, it shall turn to you again.
texts.luk.10.7: And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the laborer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.
texts.luk.10.8: And into whatever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you.
texts.luk.10.9: And heal the sick that are therein, and say to them, The kingdom of God is come nigh to you.
texts.luk.10.10: But into whatever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go out into the streets of the same, and say,
texts.luk.10.11: Even the very dust of your city which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding, be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh to you.
texts.luk.10.12: But I say to you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.
texts.luk.10.13: Woe to thee, Chorazin! woe to thee Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
texts.luk.10.14: But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.
texts.luk.10.15: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shall be thrust down to hell.
texts.luk.10.16: He that heareth you, heareth me; and he that despiseth you, despiseth me; and he that despiseth me, despiseth him that sent me.
texts.luk.10.17: And the seventy returned with joy, saying, Lord, even the demons are subject to us through thy name.
texts.luk.10.18: And he said to them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.
texts.luk.10.19: Behold, I give to you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
texts.luk.10.20: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject to you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.
texts.luk.10.21: In that hour Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to babes: even so, Father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.
texts.luk.10.22: All things are delivered to me by my Father: and no man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him.
texts.luk.10.23: And he turned himself to his disciples, and said privately, Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see.
texts.luk.10.24: For I tell you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see the things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear the things which ye hear, and have not heard them.
texts.luk.10.25: And behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
texts.luk.10.26: He said to him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?
texts.luk.10.27: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbor as thyself.
texts.luk.10.28: And he said to him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.
texts.luk.10.29: But he, willing to justify himself, said to Jesus, And who is my neighbor?
texts.luk.10.30: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among robbers, who stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
texts.luk.10.31: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way; and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
texts.luk.10.32: And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.
texts.luk.10.33: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came were he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,
texts.luk.10.34: And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
texts.luk.10.35: And on the morrow, when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said to him, Take care of him: and whatever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
texts.luk.10.36: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbor to him that fell among the robbers?
texts.luk.10.37: And he said, He that showed mercy on him. Then said Jesus to him, Go, and do thou likewise.
texts.luk.10.38: Now it came to pass, as they were going, he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman, named Martha, received him into her house.
texts.luk.10.39: And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word.
texts.luk.10.40: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.
texts.luk.10.41: And Jesus answered, and said to her, Martha, Martha, thou art anxious, and troubled about many things:
texts.luk.10.42: But one thing is needful; and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
texts.luk.11.1: And it came to pass, that as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said to him, Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.
texts.luk.11.2: And he said to them, When ye pray, say, Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
texts.luk.11.3: Give us day by day our daily bread.
texts.luk.11.4: And forgive us our sins; for we also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil.
texts.luk.11.5: And he said to them, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go to him at midnight, and say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves:
texts.luk.11.6: For a friend of mine in his journey is come to me, and I have nothing to set before him?
texts.luk.11.7: And he from within shall answer and say, Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give thee.
texts.luk.11.8: I say to you, Though he will not rise and give him, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth.
texts.luk.11.9: And I say to you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and the door shall be opened to you.
texts.luk.11.10: For every one that asketh, receiveth; and he that seeketh, findeth; and to him that knocketh, the door shall be opened.
texts.luk.11.11: If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone? or if he shall ask a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent?
texts.luk.11.12: Or if he shall ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion?
texts.luk.11.13: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children: how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
texts.luk.11.14: And he was casting out a demon, and it was dumb. And it came to pass when the demon was gone out, the dumb spoke; and the people wondered.
texts.luk.11.15: But some of them said, He casteth out demons through Beelzebub, the chief of the demons.
texts.luk.11.16: And others tempting him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
texts.luk.11.17: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house divided against a house falleth.
texts.luk.11.18: If Satan also is divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? because ye say that I cast out demons through Beelzebub.
texts.luk.11.19: And if I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.
texts.luk.11.20: But if I with the finger of God cast out demons, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.
texts.luk.11.21: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace:
texts.luk.11.22: But when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armor in which he trusted, and divideth his spoils.
texts.luk.11.23: He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.
texts.luk.11.24: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest: and finding none, he saith, I will return to my house whence I came out.
texts.luk.11.25: And when he cometh, he findeth it swept and garnished.
texts.luk.11.26: Then he goeth and taketh to him seven other spirits more wicked than himself; and they enter in, and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first.
texts.luk.11.27: And it came to pass, as he was speaking these things, a certain woman of the company lifted up her voice, and said to him, Blessed is the womb that bore thee, and the paps which nourished thee.
texts.luk.11.28: But he said, Yes, rather blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.
texts.luk.11.29: And when the people were assembled in crowds, he began to say, This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
texts.luk.11.30: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so also shall the Son of man be to this generation.
texts.luk.11.31: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth, to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
texts.luk.11.32: The men of Nineveh shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, a greater than Jonah is here.
texts.luk.11.33: No man when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, neither under a close vessel, but on a candlestick, that they who come in may see the light.
texts.luk.11.34: The light of the body is the eye: therefore when thy eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thy eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.
texts.luk.11.35: Take heed therefore, that the light which is in thee be not darkness.
texts.luk.11.36: If thy whole body therefore be full of light, having no part dark, the whole shall be full of light; as when the bright shining of a candle doth give thee light.
texts.luk.11.37: And as he was speaking, a certain Pharisee besought him to dine with him: and he went in, and sat down to eat.
texts.luk.11.38: And when the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that he had not first washed before dinner.
texts.luk.11.39: And the Lord said to him, Now do ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness.
texts.luk.11.40: Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without, make that which is within also?
texts.luk.11.41: But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and behold, all things are clean to you.
texts.luk.11.42: But woe to you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint, and rue, and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the others undone.
texts.luk.11.43: Woe to you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.
texts.luk.11.44: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are as graves which appear not, and the men that walk over them are not aware of them.
texts.luk.11.45: Then answered one of the lawyers, and said to him, Master, thus saying, thou reproachest us also.
texts.luk.11.46: And he said, Woe to you also, ye lawyers, for ye load men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.
texts.luk.11.47: Woe to you! for ye build the sepulchers of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
texts.luk.11.48: Truly ye bear testimony, that ye allow the deeds of your fathers: for they indeed killed them, and ye build their sepulchers.
texts.luk.11.49: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will slay and persecute:
texts.luk.11.50: That the blood of all the prophets, which hath been shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
texts.luk.11.51: From the blood of Abel to the blood of Zacharias, who perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say to you, It shall be required of this generation.
texts.luk.11.52: Woe to you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye have not entered in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
texts.luk.11.53: And as he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, and to solicit him to speak of many things;
texts.luk.11.54: Laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something from his mouth, that they might accuse him.
texts.luk.12.1: In the mean time, when there was gathered an innumerable multitude of people, so that they trod one upon another, he began to say to his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
texts.luk.12.2: For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.
texts.luk.12.3: Therefore, whatever ye have spoken in darkness, shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets, shall be proclaimed upon the house-tops.
texts.luk.12.4: And I say to you, my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
texts.luk.12.5: But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, who after he hath killed, hath power to cast into hell; yes, I say to you, Fear him.
texts.luk.12.6: Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?
texts.luk.12.7: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.
texts.luk.12.8: Also I say to you, Whoever shall confess me before men, him will the Son of man also confess before the angels of God.
texts.luk.12.9: But he that denieth me before men, shall be denied before the angels of God.
texts.luk.12.10: And whoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but to him that blasphemeth against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven.
texts.luk.12.11: And when they bring you to the synagogues, and before magistrates, and powers, be not solicitous how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:
texts.luk.12.12: For the Holy Spirit will teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.
texts.luk.12.13: And one of the company said to him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.
texts.luk.12.14: And he said to him, Man, who made me a judge, or a divider over you?
texts.luk.12.15: And he said to them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
texts.luk.12.16: And he spoke a parable to them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:
texts.luk.12.17: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to deposit my fruits?
texts.luk.12.18: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I deposit all my fruits and my goods.
texts.luk.12.19: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast abundance of goods laid up for many years; take thy ease, eat, drink, and be merry.
texts.luk.12.20: But God said to him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?
texts.luk.12.21: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich towards God.
texts.luk.12.22: And he said to his disciples, Therefore I say to you, Be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on.
texts.luk.12.23: The life is more than food, and the body is more than raiment.
texts.luk.12.24: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap: which neither have store-house, nor barn; and God feedeth them: How much more are ye better than the fowls?
texts.luk.12.25: And which of you by solicitude can add to his stature one cubit?
texts.luk.12.26: If ye then are not able to do that thing which is least, why are ye anxious for the rest?
texts.luk.12.27: Consider the lilies how they grow: They toil not, they spin not; and yet I say to you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
texts.luk.12.28: If then God so clothe the grass, which is to-day in the field, and to-morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith?
texts.luk.12.29: And seek ye not what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.
texts.luk.12.30: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.
texts.luk.12.31: But rather seek ye the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added to you.
texts.luk.12.32: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
texts.luk.12.33: Sell what ye have, and give alms: provide yourselves bags which become not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
texts.luk.12.34: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
texts.luk.12.35: Let your loins be girt, and your lights burning;
texts.luk.12.36: And ye yourselves like men that wait for their lord, when he shall return from the wedding; that, when he cometh and knocketh, they may open to him immediately.
texts.luk.12.37: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say to you, that he will gird himself, and make them to sit down to eat, and will come forth and serve them.
texts.luk.12.38: And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants.
texts.luk.12.39: And this know, that if the master of the house knew at what hour the thief would come, he would watch, and not suffer his house to be broken through.
texts.luk.12.40: Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.
texts.luk.12.41: Then Peter said to him, Lord, speakest thou this parable to us, or even to all?
texts.luk.12.42: And the Lord said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of provisions in due season?
texts.luk.12.43: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.
texts.luk.12.44: In truth I say to you, that he will make him ruler over all that he hath.
texts.luk.12.45: But if that servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the men-servants, and maidens, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken?
texts.luk.12.46: The lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him asunder, and will appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.
texts.luk.12.47: And that servant who knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.
texts.luk.12.48: But he that knew not, and committed things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For to whomsoever much is given, of him shall much be required: and to whom men have committed much, from him they will ask the more.
texts.luk.12.49: I am come to send fire on the earth, and what will I, if it is already kindled?
texts.luk.12.50: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it shall be accomplished!
texts.luk.12.51: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, No; but rather division:
texts.luk.12.52: For from henceforth there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
texts.luk.12.53: The father will be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
texts.luk.12.54: And he said also to the people, When ye see a cloud rising in the west, immediately ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it is.
texts.luk.12.55: And when ye perceive the south wind blowing, ye say, There will be heat; and it cometh to pass.
texts.luk.12.56: Ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky, and of the earth; but how is it, that ye do not discern this time?
texts.luk.12.57: And why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?
texts.luk.12.58: When thou goest with thy adversary to the magistrate, as thou art in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he draw thee before the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.
texts.luk.12.59: I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.
texts.luk.13.1: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
texts.luk.13.2: And Jesus answering, said to them, Suppose ye that these Galileans were sinners above all the Galileans, because they suffered such things?
texts.luk.13.3: I tell you, No; but except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
texts.luk.13.4: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?
texts.luk.13.5: I tell you, No; but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
texts.luk.13.6: He spoke also this parable: A certain man had a fig-tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit on it, and found none.
texts.luk.13.7: Then said he to the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig-tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?
texts.luk.13.8: And he answering, said to him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:
texts.luk.13.9: And if it shall bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.
texts.luk.13.10: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
texts.luk.13.11: And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise raise herself.
texts.luk.13.12: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him, and said to her, Woman, thou art loosed from thy infirmity.
texts.luk.13.13: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.
texts.luk.13.14: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because Jesus had healed on the sabbath, and said to the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath.
texts.luk.13.15: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
texts.luk.13.16: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, to be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath?
texts.luk.13.17: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
texts.luk.13.18: Then said he, To what is the kingdom of God like? and to what shall I resemble it?
texts.luk.13.19: It is like a grain of mustard-seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden, and it grew, and became a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.
texts.luk.13.20: And again he said, To what shall I liken the kingdom of God?
texts.luk.13.21: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
texts.luk.13.22: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying towards Jerusalem.
texts.luk.13.23: Then said one to him, Lord, are there few that are saved? And he said to them,
texts.luk.13.24: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say to you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.
texts.luk.13.25: When once the master of the house hath risen, and hath shut the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us; and he will answer and say to you, I know you not whence ye are:
texts.luk.13.26: Then ye will begin to say, We have eaten and drank in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.
texts.luk.13.27: But he will say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are: depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.
