texts.luk.13.28: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves excluded.
texts.luk.13.29: And they will come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and will sit down in the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.13.30: And behold, there are last, who shall be first; and there are first who shall be last.
texts.luk.13.31: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying to him, Go out, and depart hence; for Herod will kill thee.
texts.luk.13.32: And he said to them, Go ye and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out demons, and I do cures to-day and to-morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.
texts.luk.13.33: Nevertheless, I must walk to-day and to-morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet should perish out of Jerusalem.
texts.luk.13.34: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent to thee; how often would I have gathered thy children, as a hen gathereth her brood under her wings, and ye would not!
texts.luk.13.35: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. And verily I say to you, ye shall not see me, until the time shall come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
texts.luk.14.1: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath, that they watched him.
texts.luk.14.2: And behold, there was a certain man before him who had the dropsy.
texts.luk.14.3: And Jesus answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath?
texts.luk.14.4: And they held their peace. And he took him and healed him, and let him go;
texts.luk.14.5: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not forthwith pull him out on the sabbath?
texts.luk.14.6: And they could not answer him again to these things.
texts.luk.14.7: And he put forth a parable to those who were invited, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying to them,
texts.luk.14.8: When thou art invited by any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room, lest a more honorable man than thou be invited by him;
texts.luk.14.9: And he that invited thee and him, shall come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.
texts.luk.14.10: But when thou art invited, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that invited thee cometh, he may say to thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have honor in the presence of them that sit at table with thee.
texts.luk.14.11: For whoever exalteth himself shall be abased, and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
texts.luk.14.12: Then said he also to him that invited him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbors; lest they also invite thee again, and a recompense be made thee.
texts.luk.14.13: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:
texts.luk.14.14: And thou shalt be blessed: for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.
texts.luk.14.15: And when one of them that sat at table with him heard these things, he said to him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.14.16: Then said he to him, A certain man made a great supper, and invited many:
texts.luk.14.17: And sent his servant at supper-time, to say to them that were invited, Come, for all things are now ready.
texts.luk.14.18: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said to him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.
texts.luk.14.19: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.
texts.luk.14.20: And another said, I have married a wife: and therefore I cannot come.
texts.luk.14.21: So that servant came, and showed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry, said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.
texts.luk.14.22: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.
texts.luk.14.23: And the lord said to the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
texts.luk.14.24: For I say to you, that none of those men who were invited, shall taste my supper.
texts.luk.14.25: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said to them,
texts.luk.14.26: If any man cometh to me, and hateth not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.
texts.luk.14.27: And whoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.
texts.luk.14.28: For which of you intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he hath sufficient to finish it?
texts.luk.14.29: Lest perhaps after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,
texts.luk.14.30: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
texts.luk.14.31: Or what king going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?
texts.luk.14.32: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an embassy, and desireth conditions of peace.
texts.luk.14.33: So likewise, whoever he is of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.
texts.luk.14.34: Salt is good: but if the salt hath lost its savor, with what shall it be seasoned?
texts.luk.14.35: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill, but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.luk.15.1: Then drew near to him all the publicans and sinners to hear him.
texts.luk.15.2: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.
texts.luk.15.3: And he spoke this parable to them, saying,
texts.luk.15.4: What man of you having a hundred sheep, if he loseth one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he findeth it?
texts.luk.15.5: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
texts.luk.15.6: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.
texts.luk.15.7: I say to you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, who need no repentance.
texts.luk.15.8: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she loseth one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she findeth it?
texts.luk.15.9: And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbors together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.
texts.luk.15.10: Likewise, I say to you, There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
texts.luk.15.11: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
texts.luk.15.12: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided to them his living.
texts.luk.15.13: And not many days after, the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
texts.luk.15.14: And when he had spent all, there arose a severe famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
texts.luk.15.15: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
texts.luk.15.16: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat; and no man gave to him.
texts.luk.15.17: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father have bread enough and to spare, and I am perishing with hunger!
texts.luk.15.18: I will arise and go to my father, and will say to him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,
texts.luk.15.19: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
texts.luk.15.20: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
texts.luk.15.21: And the son said to him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.
texts.luk.15.22: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
texts.luk.15.23: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
texts.luk.15.24: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
texts.luk.15.25: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.
texts.luk.15.26: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
texts.luk.15.27: And he said to him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him in health.
texts.luk.15.28: And he was angry, and would not go in; therefore his father came out, and entreated him.
texts.luk.15.29: And he answering, said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither have I at any time transgressed thy commandment; and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:
texts.luk.15.30: But as soon as this thy son had come, who hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.
texts.luk.15.31: And he said to him, Son, thou art ever with me: and all that I have is thine.
texts.luk.15.32: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
texts.luk.16.1: And he said also to his disciples, There was a certain rich man who had a steward; and the same was accused to him that he had wasted his goods.
texts.luk.16.2: And he called him, and said to him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship: for thou mayest be no longer steward.
texts.luk.16.3: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; I am ashamed to beg.
texts.luk.16.4: I am resolved what to do, that when I am removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
texts.luk.16.5: So he called every one of his lord's debtors, and said to the first, How much owest thou to my lord?
texts.luk.16.6: And he said, A hundred measures of oil. And he said to him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.
texts.luk.16.7: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, A hundred measures of wheat. And he said to him, Take thy bill, and write eighty.
texts.luk.16.8: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.
texts.luk.16.9: And I say to you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.
texts.luk.16.10: He that is faithful in that which is least, is faithful also in much; and he that is unjust in the least, is unjust also in much.
texts.luk.16.11: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
texts.luk.16.12: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man's, who will give you that which is your own?
texts.luk.16.13: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
texts.luk.16.14: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things, and they derided him.
texts.luk.16.15: And he said to them, Ye are they who justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men, is abomination in the sight of God.
texts.luk.16.16: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.
texts.luk.16.17: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than one tittle of the law to fail.
texts.luk.16.18: Whoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery; and whoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband, committeth adultery.
texts.luk.16.19: There was a certain rich man, who was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:
texts.luk.16.20: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, who was laid at his gate, full of sores,
texts.luk.16.21: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table: moreover, the dogs came and licked his sores.
texts.luk.16.22: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by angels into Abraham's bosom. The rich man also died, and was buried:
texts.luk.16.23: And in hell he lifted up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
texts.luk.16.24: And he cried, and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue: for I am tormented in this flame.
texts.luk.16.25: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy life-time receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.
texts.luk.16.26: And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they who would pass from hence to you, cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.
texts.luk.16.27: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldst send him to my father's house:
texts.luk.16.28: For I have five brethren; that he may testify to them, lest they also come into this place of torment.
texts.luk.16.29: Abraham saith to him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
texts.luk.16.30: And he said, No, father Abraham: but if one shall go to them from the dead, they will repent.
texts.luk.16.31: And he said to him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one shall rise from the dead.
texts.luk.17.1: Then he said to the disciples, It is impossible but that causes of sin will come: but woe to him by whom they come!
texts.luk.17.2: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to fall into sin.
texts.luk.17.3: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother shall trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he shall repent forgive him.
texts.luk.17.4: And if he shall trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day shall turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.
texts.luk.17.5: And the apostles said to the Lord, Increase our faith.
texts.luk.17.6: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard-seed, ye might say to this sycamine-tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it would obey you.
texts.luk.17.7: But which of you having a servant plowing, or feeding cattle, will say to him immediately, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to eat?
texts.luk.17.8: And will not rather say to him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drank; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?
texts.luk.17.9: Doth he thank that servant, because he did the things that were commanded him? I suppose not.
texts.luk.17.10: So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all the things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which it was our duty to do.
texts.luk.17.11: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
texts.luk.17.12: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, who stood at a distance.
texts.luk.17.13: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
texts.luk.17.14: And when he saw them, he said to them, Go, show yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass, that as they were going, they were cleansed.
texts.luk.17.15: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,
texts.luk.17.16: And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
texts.luk.17.17: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
texts.luk.17.18: There are not found returning to give glory to God, save this stranger.
texts.luk.17.19: And he said to him, Arise, depart: thy faith hath made thee whole.
texts.luk.17.20: And when he was asked by the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation.
texts.luk.17.21: Neither will they say, Lo here! or lo there! for behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
texts.luk.17.22: And he said to his disciples, The days will come, when ye will desire to see one of the days of the son of man, and ye shall not see it.
texts.luk.17.23: And they will say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.
texts.luk.17.24: For as the lightning that lighteneth from the one part under heaven, shineth to the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of man be in his day.
texts.luk.17.25: But first he must suffer many things, and be rejected by this generation.
texts.luk.17.26: And as it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.
texts.luk.17.27: They ate, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark; and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
texts.luk.17.28: Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
texts.luk.17.29: But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all:
texts.luk.17.30: Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.
texts.luk.17.31: In that day, he who shall be upon the house-top, and his furniture in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.
texts.luk.17.33: Whoever shall seek to save his life, shall lose it; and whoever shall lose his life, shall preserve it.
texts.luk.17.34: I tell you, in that night there will be two men in one bed; the one will be taken, and the other will be left.
texts.luk.17.35: Two women will be grinding together; the one will be taken, and the other left.
texts.luk.17.36: Two men will be in the field; the one will be taken, and the other left.
texts.luk.17.37: And they answered and said to him, Where Lord? And he said to them, Wherever the body is, thither will the eagles be collected.
texts.luk.18.1: And he spoke a parable to them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;
texts.luk.18.2: Saying, There was in a city a judge, who feared not God, neither regarded man.
texts.luk.18.3: And there was a widow in that city; and she came to him, saying, Avenge me of my adversary.
texts.luk.18.4: And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;
texts.luk.18.5: Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.
texts.luk.18.6: And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith.
texts.luk.18.7: And will not God avenge his own elect, who cry day and night to him, though he beareth long with them?
texts.luk.18.8: I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of man cometh, will he find faith on the earth?
texts.luk.18.9: And he spoke this parable to certain who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others:
texts.luk.18.10: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.
texts.luk.18.11: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.
texts.luk.18.12: I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.
texts.luk.18.13: And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes to heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.
texts.luk.18.14: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
texts.luk.18.15: And they brought to him also infants, that he would touch them: but when his disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
texts.luk.18.16: But Jesus called them to him, and said, Suffer little children to come to me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.18.17: Verily I say to you, Whoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, shall in no wise enter into it.
texts.luk.18.18: And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
texts.luk.18.19: And Jesus said to him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is God.
texts.luk.18.20: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honor thy father and thy mother.
texts.luk.18.21: And he said, All these have I kept from my youth.
texts.luk.18.22: Now when Jesus heard these things, he said to him, Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.
texts.luk.18.23: And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful: for he was very rich.
texts.luk.18.24: And when Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful, he said, How hardly will they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
texts.luk.18.25: For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.18.26: And they that heard it, said, Who then can be saved?
texts.luk.18.27: Then he said, The things which are impossible with men, are possible with God.
texts.luk.18.28: Then Peter said, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee.
texts.luk.18.29: And he said to them, Verily I say to you, there is no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
texts.luk.18.30: Who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting.
texts.luk.18.31: Then he took the twelve, and said to them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished.
texts.luk.18.32: For he will be delivered to the Gentiles, and will be mocked, and spitefully treated, and spitted on;
texts.luk.18.33: And they will scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he will rise again.
texts.luk.18.34: And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken.
texts.luk.18.35: And it came to pass, that as he had come nigh to Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging;
texts.luk.18.36: And hearing the multitude passing by, he asked what it meant.
texts.luk.18.37: And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
texts.luk.18.38: And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.
texts.luk.18.39: And they who went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried so much the more, Thou son of David, have mercy on me.
texts.luk.18.40: And Jesus stood and commanded him to be brought to him: and when he had come near, he asked him,
texts.luk.18.41: Saying, What wilt thou that I shall do to thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight.
texts.luk.18.42: And Jesus said to him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee.
texts.luk.18.43: And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.
texts.luk.19.1: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
texts.luk.19.2: And behold, there was a man named Zaccheus, who was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
texts.luk.19.3: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the crowd, because he was little of stature.
texts.luk.19.4: And he ran before, and climbed up upon a sycamore-tree to see him; for he was to pass that way.
texts.luk.19.5: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said to him, Zaccheus, make haste, and come down: for to-day I must abide at thy house.
texts.luk.19.6: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
texts.luk.19.7: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
texts.luk.19.8: And Zaccheus stood, and said to the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him four-fold.
texts.luk.19.9: And Jesus said to him, This day is salvation come to this house, forasmuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
texts.luk.19.10: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
texts.luk.19.11: And as they heard these things, he added and spoke a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God would immediately appear.
texts.luk.19.12: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
texts.luk.19.13: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said to them, Occupy till I come.
texts.luk.19.14: But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.
texts.luk.19.15: And it came to pass, that when he had returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called to him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.
texts.luk.19.16: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.
texts.luk.19.17: And he said to him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.
texts.luk.19.18: And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.
texts.luk.19.19: And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.
texts.luk.19.20: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:
texts.luk.19.21: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up what thou layedst not down, and reapest what thou didst not sow.
texts.luk.19.22: And he saith to him, Out of thy own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest me to be an austere man, taking up what I laid not down, and reaping what I did not sow:
texts.luk.19.23: Why then gavest thou not my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required my own with interest?
texts.luk.19.24: And he said to them that stood by, Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.
texts.luk.19.25: (And they said to him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.)
texts.luk.19.26: For I say to you, That to every one who hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even what he hath shall be taken away from him.
texts.luk.19.27: But those my enemies, who would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.
texts.luk.19.28: And when he had thus spoken, he went before, ascending towards Jerusalem.
texts.luk.19.29: And it came to pass, when he had come nigh to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
texts.luk.19.30: Saying, Go ye into the village over against you; in which at your entering ye will find a colt tied, on which yet never man sat: loose him, and bring him hither.
texts.luk.19.31: And if any man shall ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say to him, Because the Lord hath need of him.
texts.luk.19.32: And they that were sent, went and found even as he had said to them.
texts.luk.19.33: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners of it said to them, Why loose ye the colt?
texts.luk.19.34: And they said, The Lord hath need of him.
texts.luk.19.35: And they brought him to Jesus: and they cast their garments upon the colt, and they set Jesus upon him.
texts.luk.19.36: And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way.
texts.luk.19.37: And when he had come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice, for all the mighty works that they had seen.
texts.luk.19.38: Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
texts.luk.19.39: And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said to him, Master, rebuke thy disciples.
texts.luk.19.40: And he answered and said to them, I tell you, that if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.
texts.luk.19.41: And when he had come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,
texts.luk.19.42: Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong to thy peace! but now they are hid from thy eyes.
texts.luk.19.43: For the days shall come upon thee, that thy enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and encompass thee, and keep thee in on every side,
texts.luk.19.44: And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee: and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another: because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
texts.luk.19.45: And he went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold in it, and them that bought,
texts.luk.19.46: Saying to them, It is written, My house is the house of prayer, but ye have made it a den of thieves.
texts.luk.19.47: And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests, and the scribes, and the chief of the people sought to destroy him,
texts.luk.19.48: And could not find what they might do: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.
texts.luk.20.1: And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he was teaching the people in the temple, and preaching the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him, with the elders,
texts.luk.20.2: And spoke to him, saying, Tell us, By what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?
texts.luk.20.3: And he answered and said to them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me:
texts.luk.20.4: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?
texts.luk.20.5: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not?
texts.luk.20.6: But if we say, From men; all the people will stone us: for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.
texts.luk.20.7: And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was.
texts.luk.20.8: And Jesus said to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.luk.20.9: Then he began to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.
texts.luk.20.10: And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.
texts.luk.20.11: And again he sent another servant: and they beat him also, and treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
texts.luk.20.12: And again he sent the third: and they wounded him also, and cast him out.
texts.luk.20.13: Then said the lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be when they see him they will reverence him.
texts.luk.20.14: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.
texts.luk.20.15: So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
texts.luk.20.16: He will come and destroy these husbandmen, and will give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, may that never be.
texts.luk.20.17: And he beheld them, and said, What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?
texts.luk.20.18: Whoever shall fall upon that stone, shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
texts.luk.20.19: And the chief priests and the scribes the same hour sought to lay hands on him; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them.
texts.luk.20.20: And they watched him, and sent forth spies, who should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him to the power and authority of the governor.
texts.luk.20.21: And they asked him, saying, Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, neither acceptest thou the person of any, but teachest the way of God truly:
texts.luk.20.22: Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Cesar, or not?
texts.luk.20.23: But he perceived their craftiness, and said to them, Why tempt ye me?
texts.luk.20.24: Show me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said, Cesar's.
texts.luk.20.25: And he said to them, Render therefore to Cesar the things which are Cesar's, and to God the things which are God's.
texts.luk.20.26: And they could not take hold of his words before the people: and they marveled at his answer, and held their peace.
texts.luk.20.27: Then came to him certain of the Sadducees (who deny that there is any resurrection) and they asked him,
texts.luk.20.28: Saying, Master, Moses wrote to us, If any man's brother should die, having a wife, and he should die without children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed to his brother.
texts.luk.20.29: There were therefore seven brothers: and the first took a wife, and died without children.
texts.luk.20.30: And the second took her for a wife, and he died childless.
texts.luk.20.31: And the third took her; and in like manner the seven also: And they left no children, and died.
texts.luk.20.32: Last of all the woman died also.
texts.luk.20.33: Therefore in the resurrection, whose wife of them is she? for seven had her to wife.
texts.luk.20.34: And Jesus answering, said to them, The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:
texts.luk.20.35: But they who shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage.
texts.luk.20.36: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal to the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.
texts.luk.20.37: Now that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
texts.luk.20.38: For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live to him.
texts.luk.20.39: Then certain of the scribes answering, said, Master, thou hast well said.
texts.luk.20.40: And after that, they durst not ask him any question at all.
texts.luk.20.41: And he said to them, How say they that Christ is David's son?
texts.luk.20.42: And David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The LORD said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,
texts.luk.20.43: Till I make thy enemies thy footstool.
texts.luk.20.44: David therefore calleth him Lord, how is he then his son?
texts.luk.20.45: Then in the audience of all the people, he said to his disciples,
texts.luk.20.46: Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts;
texts.luk.20.47: Who devour widows' houses, and for a show make long prayers: the same shall receive greater damnation.
texts.luk.21.1: And he looked up, and saw rich men casting their gifts into the treasury.
texts.luk.21.2: And he saw also a certain poor widow, casting in thither two mites.
texts.luk.21.3: And he said, Of a truth I say to you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all.
texts.luk.21.4: For all these have of their abundance cast in to the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.
texts.luk.21.5: And as some spoke of the temple, that it was adorned with goodly stones, and gifts, he said,
texts.luk.21.6: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that will not be thrown down.
texts.luk.21.7: And they asked him, saying, Master, but when will these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?
texts.luk.21.8: And he said, Take heed that ye be not deceived: for many will come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: therefore go ye not after them.
texts.luk.21.9: But when ye shall hear of wars, and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass: but the end is not immediately.
texts.luk.21.10: Then said he to them, Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:
texts.luk.21.11: And great earthquakes will be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences: and fearful sights, and great signs will there be from heaven.
texts.luk.21.12: But before all these they will lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name's sake.
texts.luk.21.13: And it shall turn to you for a testimony.
texts.luk.21.14: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall answer.
texts.luk.21.15: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.
texts.luk.21.16: And ye will be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsmen, and friends; and some of you will they cause to be put to death.
texts.luk.21.17: And ye will be hated by all men for my name's sake.
texts.luk.21.18: But there shall not a hair of your head perish.
texts.luk.21.19: In your patience possess ye your souls.
texts.luk.21.20: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that its desolation is nigh.
texts.luk.21.21: Then let them who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let them who are in the midst of it depart from it; and let not them that are in the countries enter into it.
texts.luk.21.22: For these are the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
texts.luk.21.23: But woe to them that are with child, and to them that nurse infants in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.
texts.luk.21.24: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles shall be fulfilled.
texts.luk.21.25: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;
texts.luk.21.26: Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for apprehension of those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.
texts.luk.21.27: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud, with power and great glory.
texts.luk.21.28: And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads: for your redemption draweth nigh.
texts.luk.21.29: And he spoke to them a parable; Behold the fig-tree, and all the trees;
texts.luk.21.30: When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your ownselves that summer is now nigh at hand.
texts.luk.21.31: So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.
texts.luk.21.32: Verily I say to you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.
texts.luk.21.33: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my word shall not pass away.
texts.luk.21.34: And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.
texts.luk.21.35: For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.
texts.luk.21.36: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.
texts.luk.21.37: And in the day-time he was teaching in the temple; and at night he went out, and abode in the mount that is called the mount of Olives.
texts.luk.21.38: And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, to hear him.
texts.luk.22.1: Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.
texts.luk.22.2: And the chief priests and scribes sought how they might kill him: for they feared the people.
texts.luk.22.3: Then Satan entered into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.
texts.luk.22.4: And he went, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him to them.
texts.luk.22.5: And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.
texts.luk.22.6: And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him to them in the absence of the multitude.
texts.luk.22.7: Then came the day of unleavened bread, when the passover must be killed.
texts.luk.22.8: And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare for us the passover, that we may eat.
texts.luk.22.9: And they said to him, Where wilt thou that we prepare?
texts.luk.22.10: And he said to them, Behold, when ye have entered into the city, there shall a man meet you, bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he entereth.
texts.luk.22.11: And ye shall say to the master of the house, The Master saith to thee, Where is the guest-chamber, where I may eat the passover with my disciples?
texts.luk.22.12: And he will show you a large upper room furnished: there make ready.
texts.luk.22.13: And they went and found as he had said to them: and they made ready the passover.
texts.luk.22.14: And when the hour was come, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him.
texts.luk.22.15: And he said to them, I have earnestly desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer.
texts.luk.22.16: For I say to you, I will not any more eat of it until it shall be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.22.17: And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and said, Take this, and divide it among yourselves.
texts.luk.22.18: For I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come.
texts.luk.22.19: And he took bread, and gave thanks, and broke it, and gave to them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.
texts.luk.22.20: Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.
texts.luk.22.21: But behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table.
texts.luk.22.22: And truly the Son of man goeth as it was determined: but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!
texts.luk.22.23: And they began to inquire among themselves, which of them it was that should do this thing.
texts.luk.22.24: And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest.
texts.luk.22.25: And he said to them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them, are called benefactors.
texts.luk.22.26: But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.
texts.luk.22.27: For which is greater, he that sitteth at table, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at table? but I am among you as he that serveth.
texts.luk.22.28: Ye are they who have continued with me in my temptations.
texts.luk.22.29: And I appoint to you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed to me;
texts.luk.22.30: That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
texts.luk.22.31: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:
texts.luk.22.32: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not; and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
texts.luk.22.33: And he said to him, Lord, I am ready to go with thee both into prison, and to death.
texts.luk.22.34: And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock will not crow this day, before thou wilt thrice deny that thou knowest me.
texts.luk.22.35: And he said to them, When I sent you without purse, and sack, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing.
texts.luk.22.36: Then said he to them, But now he that hath a purse, let him take it, and likewise his sack: and he that hath no sword, let him sell his garment, and buy one.
texts.luk.22.37: For I say to you, that this which is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors: for the things concerning me have an end.
texts.luk.22.38: And they said, Lord, behold, here are two swords. And he said to them, It is enough.
texts.luk.22.39: And he came out, and went, as he was wont, to the mount of Olives; and his disciples also followed him.
texts.luk.22.40: And when he was at the place, he said to them, Pray, that ye enter not into temptation.
texts.luk.22.41: And he was withdrawn from them about a stone's cast, and kneeled down, and prayed.
texts.luk.22.42: Saying, Father, if thou art willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine be done.
texts.luk.22.43: And there appeared to him an angel from heaven, strengthening him.
texts.luk.22.44: And being in an agony, he prayed more earnestly: and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling to the ground.
texts.luk.22.45: And when he arose from prayer, and had come to his disciples, he found them sleeping for sorrow:
texts.luk.22.46: And said to them, Why sleep ye? rise and pray, lest ye enter into temptation.
texts.luk.22.47: And while he was yet speaking, behold a multitude, and he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and drew near to Jesus to kiss him.
texts.luk.22.48: But Jesus said to him, Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?
texts.luk.22.49: When they who were about him, saw what would follow, they said to him, Lord, shall we smite with the sword?
texts.luk.22.50: And one of them smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
texts.luk.22.51: And Jesus answered and said, Suffer ye thus far. And he touched his ear, and healed him.
texts.luk.22.52: Then Jesus said to the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and the elders who had come to him, Are ye come out as against a thief, with swords and staffs?
texts.luk.22.53: When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
texts.luk.22.54: Then they took him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest's house. And Peter followed at a distance.
texts.luk.22.55: And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.
texts.luk.22.56: But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.
texts.luk.22.57: And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.
texts.luk.22.58: And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.
texts.luk.22.59: And about the space of one hour after, another confidently affirmed, saying, In truth this man also was with him; for he is a Galilean.
texts.luk.22.60: And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he was yet speaking, the cock crowed.
texts.luk.22.61: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said to him, Before the cock shall crow, thou wilt deny me thrice.
texts.luk.22.62: And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
texts.luk.22.63: And the men that held Jesus, mocked him, and smote him.
texts.luk.22.64: And when they had blindfolded him, they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?
texts.luk.22.65: And many other things blasphemously they spoke against him.
texts.luk.22.66: And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people, and the chief priests, and the scribes came together, and led him into their council,
texts.luk.22.67: Saying, Art thou the Christ? tell us. And he said to them, If I tell you, ye will not believe.
texts.luk.22.68: And if I also ask you, ye will not answer me, nor let me go.
texts.luk.22.69: Hereafter will the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God.
texts.luk.22.70: Then said they all, Art thou then the Son of God? And he said to them, Ye say that I am.
texts.luk.22.71: And they said, What need have we of any further testimony? for we ourselves have heard from his own mouth.
texts.luk.23.1: And the whole multitude of them arose, and led him to Pilate.
texts.luk.23.2: And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this man perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Cesar, saying, that he himself is Christ a king.
texts.luk.23.3: And Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answered him and said, Thou sayest it.
texts.luk.23.4: Then said Pilate to the chief priests, and to the people, I find no fault in this man.
texts.luk.23.5: And they were the more fierce, saying, He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee to this place.
texts.luk.23.6: When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
texts.luk.23.7: And as soon as he knew that he belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who himself was also at Jerusalem at that time.
texts.luk.23.8: And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he had been for a long time, desirous to see him, because he had heard many things of him; and he hoped to see some miracle done by him.
texts.luk.23.9: Then he questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.
texts.luk.23.10: And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him.
texts.luk.23.11: And Herod with his troops set him at naught, and mocked him, and arrayed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him again to Pilate.
texts.luk.23.12: And the same day Pilate and Herod were made friends together; for before they were at enmity between themselves.
texts.luk.23.13: And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests, and the rulers, and the people,
texts.luk.23.14: Said to them, Ye have brought this man to me, as one that perverteth the people: and behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man, touching those things of which ye accuse him;
texts.luk.23.15: No, nor yet Herod: for I sent you to him; and lo, nothing worthy of death is done to him:
texts.luk.23.16: I will therefore chastise him, and release him.
texts.luk.23.17: (For of necessity he must release one to them at the feast.)
texts.luk.23.18: And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man, and release to us Barabbas:
texts.luk.23.19: (Who, for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.)
texts.luk.23.20: Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spoke again to them.
texts.luk.23.21: But they cried, saying, Crucify, crucify him.
texts.luk.23.22: And he said to them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him; I will therefore chastise him, and let him go.
texts.luk.23.23: And they were urgent with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified: and the voices of them, and of the chief priests prevailed.
texts.luk.23.24: And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.
texts.luk.23.25: And he released to them him that for sedition and murder had been cast into prison, whom they had desired; but he delivered Jesus to their will.
texts.luk.23.26: And as they led him away, they laid hold upon one Simon a Cyrenian, coming out of the country, and on him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.
texts.luk.23.27: And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, who also bewailed and lamented him.
texts.luk.23.28: But Jesus turning to them, said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.
texts.luk.23.29: For behold, the days are coming, in which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bore, and the breasts which never nourished infants.
texts.luk.23.30: Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.
texts.luk.23.31: For if they do these things in a green tree, what will be done in the dry?
texts.luk.23.32: And two others, who were malefactors, were led with him to be put to death.
texts.luk.23.33: And when they had come to the place which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors; one on the right hand, and the other on the left.
texts.luk.23.34: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them: for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.
texts.luk.23.35: And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he is Christ the chosen of God.
texts.luk.23.36: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, and offering him vinegar,
texts.luk.23.37: And saying, If thou art the King of the Jews, save thyself.
texts.luk.23.38: And a superscription also was written over him, in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
texts.luk.23.39: And one of the malefactors, who were hanged, railed on him, saying, If thou art Christ, save thyself and us.
texts.luk.23.40: But the other answering, rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?
texts.luk.23.41: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.
texts.luk.23.42: And he said to Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
texts.luk.23.43: And Jesus said to him, Verily I say to thee, This day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
texts.luk.23.44: And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
texts.luk.23.45: And the sun was darkened, and the vail of the temple was rent in the midst.
texts.luk.23.46: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he expired.
texts.luk.23.47: Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.
texts.luk.23.48: And all the people that came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts, and returned.
texts.luk.23.49: And all his acquaintance, and the women that followed him from Galilee, stood afar off beholding these things.
texts.luk.23.50: And behold, there was a man named Joseph, a counselor: and he was a good man, and a just:
texts.luk.23.51: (The same had not consented to the counsel and deed of them) he was of Arimathea, a city of the Jews; who also himself waited for the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.23.52: This man went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus.
texts.luk.23.53: And he took it down, and wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a sepulcher that was hewn in stone, in which man was never before laid.
texts.luk.23.54: And that day was the preparation, and the sabbath drew on.
texts.luk.23.55: And the women also, who came with him from Galilee, followed after, and beheld the sepulcher, and how his body was laid.
texts.luk.23.56: And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested on the sabbath, according to the commandment.
texts.luk.24.1: Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came to the sepulcher, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.
texts.luk.24.2: And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulcher.
texts.luk.24.3: And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.
texts.luk.24.4: And it came to pass, as they were much perplexed at this, behold, two men stood by them in shining garments.
texts.luk.24.5: And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said to them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?
texts.luk.24.6: He is not here, but is risen. Remember how he spoke to you when he was yet in Galilee,
texts.luk.24.7: Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.
texts.luk.24.9: And returned from the sepulcher, and told all these things to the eleven, and to all the rest.
texts.luk.24.10: It was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women that were with them, who told these things to the apostles.
texts.luk.24.11: And their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not.
texts.luk.24.12: Then Peter arose, and ran to the sepulcher, and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which had come to pass.
texts.luk.24.13: And behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about sixty furlongs.
texts.luk.24.14: And they talked together of all these things which had happened.
texts.luk.24.15: And it came to pass, that, while they communed together, and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.
texts.luk.24.16: But their eyes were held, that they should not know him.
texts.luk.24.17: And he said to them, What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad?
texts.luk.24.18: And one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering, said to him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which have come to pass there in these days?
texts.luk.24.19: And he said to them, What things? And they said to him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God, and all the people:
texts.luk.24.20: And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and crucified him.
texts.luk.24.21: But we trusted that it had been he who would have redeemed Israel: and besides all this, to-day is the third day since these things were done.
texts.luk.24.22: Yes, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, who were early at the sepulcher.
texts.luk.24.23: And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.
texts.luk.24.24: And certain of them who were with us, went to the sepulcher, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not.
texts.luk.24.25: Then he said to them, O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
texts.luk.24.26: Ought not Christ to suffer these things, and to enter into his glory?
texts.luk.24.27: And beginning at Moses, and all the prophets, he expounded to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
texts.luk.24.28: And they drew nigh to the village whither they were going: and he made as though he would go further.
texts.luk.24.29: But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is towards evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them.
texts.luk.24.30: And it came to pass, as he sat at table with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and broke, and gave to them.
texts.luk.24.31: And their eyes were opened, and they knew him: and he vanished out of their sight.
texts.luk.24.32: And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?
texts.luk.24.33: And they rose the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven assembled, and them that were with them,
texts.luk.24.34: Saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon.
texts.luk.24.35: And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known to them in breaking of bread.
texts.luk.24.36: And as they were thus speaking, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them, and saith to them, Peace be to you.
texts.luk.24.37: But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.
texts.luk.24.38: And he said to them, Why are ye troubled? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?
texts.luk.24.39: Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.
texts.luk.24.40: And when he had thus spoken, he showed them his hands and his feet.
texts.luk.24.41: And while they yet believed not for joy, and wondered, he said to them, Have ye here any thing for food?
texts.luk.24.42: And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and a honey-comb.
texts.luk.24.43: And he took it, and ate before them.
texts.luk.24.44: And he said to them, These are the words which I spoke to you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.
texts.luk.24.45: Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures,
texts.luk.24.46: And said to them, Thus it is written, and thus it behooved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day:
texts.luk.24.47: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
texts.luk.24.48: And ye are witnesses of these things.
texts.luk.24.49: And behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye are endued with power from on high.
texts.luk.24.50: And he led them out as far as to Bethany: and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.
texts.luk.24.51: And it came to pass, while he was blessing them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.
texts.luk.24.52: And they worshiped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy:
texts.luk.24.53: And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

texts.luk.1.1: Forasmuch as many have undertaken to draw up a relation concerning the matters fully believed among us,
texts.luk.1.2: as those who from the beginning were eye-witnesses of and attendants on the Word have delivered them to us,
texts.luk.1.3: it has seemed good to *me* also, accurately acquainted from the origin with all things, to write to thee with method, most excellent Theophilus,
texts.luk.1.4: that thou mightest know the certainty of those things in which thou hast been instructed.
texts.luk.1.5: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judaea, a certain priest, by name Zacharias, of the course of Abia, and his wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elizabeth.
texts.luk.1.6: And they were both just before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
texts.luk.1.7: And they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and they were both advanced in years.
texts.luk.1.8: And it came to pass, as he fulfilled his priestly service before God in the order of his course,
texts.luk.1.9: it fell to him by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter into the temple of the Lord to burn incense.
texts.luk.1.10: And all the multitude of the people were praying without at the hour of incense.
texts.luk.1.11: And an angel of [the] Lord appeared to him, standing on the right of the altar of incense.
texts.luk.1.12: And Zacharias was troubled, seeing [him], and fear fell upon him.
texts.luk.1.13: But the angel said to him, Fear not, Zacharias, because thy supplication has been heard, and thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
texts.luk.1.14: And he shall be to thee joy and rejoicing, and many shall rejoice at his birth.
texts.luk.1.15: For he shall be great before [the] Lord, and he shall drink no wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with [the] Holy Spirit, even from his mother's womb.
texts.luk.1.16: And many of the sons of Israel shall he turn to [the] Lord their God.
texts.luk.1.17: And *he* shall go before him in [the] spirit and power of Elias, to turn hearts of fathers to children, and disobedient ones to [the] thoughts of just [men], to make ready for [the] Lord a prepared people.
texts.luk.1.18: And Zacharias said to the angel, How shall I know this, for *I* am an old man, and my wife advanced in years?
texts.luk.1.19: And the angel answering, said to him, *I* am Gabriel, who stand before God, and I have been sent to speak to thee, and to bring these glad tidings to thee;
texts.luk.1.20: and behold, thou shalt be silent and not able to speak, till the day in which these things shall take place, because thou hast not believed my words, the which shall be fulfilled in their time.
texts.luk.1.21: And the people were awaiting Zacharias, and they wondered at his delaying in the temple.
texts.luk.1.22: But when he came out he could not speak to them, and they recognised that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he was making signs to them, and continued dumb.
texts.luk.1.23: And it came to pass, when the days of his service were completed, he departed to his house.
texts.luk.1.24: Now after these days, Elizabeth his wife conceived, and hid herself five months, saying,
texts.luk.1.25: Thus has [the] Lord done to me in [these] days in which he looked upon [me] to take away my reproach among men.
texts.luk.1.26: But in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent of God to a city of Galilee, of which [the] name [was] Nazareth,
texts.luk.1.27: to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name [was] Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary.
texts.luk.1.28: And the angel came in to her, and said, Hail, [thou] favoured one! the Lord [is] with thee: [blessed art *thou* amongst women].
texts.luk.1.29: But she, [seeing] [the angel], was troubled at his word, and reasoned in her mind what this salutation might be.
texts.luk.1.30: And the angel said to her, Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found favour with God;
texts.luk.1.31: and behold, thou shalt conceive in the womb and bear a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus.
texts.luk.1.32: *He* shall be great, and shall be called Son of [the] Highest; and [the] Lord God shall give him the throne of David his father;
texts.luk.1.33: and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for the ages, and of his kingdom there shall not be an end.
texts.luk.1.34: But Mary said to the angel, How shall this be, since I know not a man?
texts.luk.1.35: And the angel answering said to her, [The] Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, and power of [the] Highest overshadow thee, wherefore the holy thing also which shall be born shall be called Son of God.
texts.luk.1.36: And behold, Elizabeth, thy kinswoman, she also has conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month to her that was called barren:
texts.luk.1.37: for nothing shall be impossible with God.
texts.luk.1.38: And Mary said, Behold the bondmaid of [the] Lord; be it to me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.
texts.luk.1.39: And Mary, rising up in those days, went into the hill country with haste, to a city of Judah,
texts.luk.1.40: and entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elizabeth.
texts.luk.1.41: And it came to pass, as Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with [the] Holy Spirit,
texts.luk.1.42: and cried out with a loud voice and said, Blessed [art] *thou* amongst women, and blessed the fruit of thy womb.
texts.luk.1.43: And whence [is] this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
texts.luk.1.44: For behold, as the voice of thy salutation sounded in my ears, the babe leaped with joy in my womb.
texts.luk.1.45: And blessed [is] she that has believed, for there shall be a fulfilment of the things spoken to her from [the] Lord.
texts.luk.1.46: And Mary said, My soul magnifies the Lord,
texts.luk.1.47: and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Saviour.
texts.luk.1.48: For he has looked upon the low estate of his bondmaid; for behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.
texts.luk.1.49: For the Mighty One has done to me great things, and holy [is] his name;
texts.luk.1.50: and his mercy [is] to generations and generations to them that fear him.
texts.luk.1.51: He has wrought strength with his arm; he has scattered haughty [ones] in the thought of their heart.
texts.luk.1.52: He has put down rulers from thrones, and exalted the lowly.
texts.luk.1.53: He has filled the hungry with good things, and sent away the rich empty.
texts.luk.1.54: He has helped Israel his servant, in order to remember mercy,
texts.luk.1.55: (as he spoke to our fathers,) to Abraham and to his seed for ever.
texts.luk.1.56: And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned to her house.
texts.luk.1.57: But the time was fulfilled for Elizabeth that she should bring forth, and she gave birth to a son.
texts.luk.1.58: And her neighbours and kinsfolk heard that [the] Lord had magnified his mercy with her, and they rejoiced with her.
texts.luk.1.59: And it came to pass on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they called it after the name of his father, Zacharias.
texts.luk.1.60: And his mother answering said, No; but he shall be called John.
texts.luk.1.61: And they said to her, There is no one among thy kinsfolk who is called by this name.
texts.luk.1.62: And they made signs to his father as to what he might wish it to be called.
texts.luk.1.63: And having asked for a writing-table, he wrote saying, John is his name. And they all wondered.
texts.luk.1.64: And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue, and he spake, blessing God.
texts.luk.1.65: And fear came upon all who dwelt round about them; and in the whole hill-country of Judaea all these things were the subject of conversation.
texts.luk.1.66: And all who heard them laid them up in their heart, saying, What then will this child be? And [the] Lord's hand was with him.
texts.luk.1.67: And Zacharias his father was filled with [the] Holy Spirit, and prophesied, saying,
texts.luk.1.68: Blessed be [the] Lord the God of Israel, because he has visited and wrought redemption for his people,
texts.luk.1.69: and raised up a horn of deliverance for us in the house of David his servant;
texts.luk.1.70: as he spoke by [the] mouth of his holy prophets, who have been since the world began;
texts.luk.1.71: deliverance from our enemies and out of the hand of all who hate us;
texts.luk.1.72: to fulfil mercy with our fathers and remember his holy covenant,
texts.luk.1.73: [the] oath which he swore to Abraham our father,
texts.luk.1.74: to give us, that, saved out of the hand of our enemies, we should serve him without fear
texts.luk.1.75: in piety and righteousness before him all our days.
texts.luk.1.76: And *thou*, child, shalt be called [the] prophet of [the] Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of [the] Lord to make ready his ways;
texts.luk.1.77: to give knowledge of deliverance to his people by [the] remission of their sins
texts.luk.1.78: on account of [the] bowels of mercy of our God; wherein [the] dayspring from on high has visited us,
texts.luk.1.79: to shine upon them who were sitting in darkness and in [the] shadow of death, to guide our feet into [the] way of peace.
texts.luk.1.80: -- And the child grew and was strengthened in spirit; and he was in the deserts until the day of his shewing to Israel.
texts.luk.2.1: But it came to pass in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus, that a census should be made of all the habitable world.
texts.luk.2.2: The census itself first took place when Cyrenius had the government of Syria.
texts.luk.2.3: And all went to be inscribed in the census roll, each to his own city:
texts.luk.2.4: and Joseph also went up from Galilee out of the city Nazareth to Judaea, to David's city, the which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
texts.luk.2.5: to be inscribed in the census roll with Mary who was betrothed to him [as his] wife, she being great with child.
texts.luk.2.6: And it came to pass, while they were there, the days of her giving birth [to her child] were fulfilled,
texts.luk.2.7: and she brought forth her first-born son, and wrapped him up in swaddling-clothes and laid him in the manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
texts.luk.2.8: And there were shepherds in that country abiding without, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
texts.luk.2.9: And lo, an angel of [the] Lord was there by them, and [the] glory of [the] Lord shone around them, and they feared [with] great fear.
texts.luk.2.10: And the angel said to them, Fear not, for behold, I announce to you glad tidings of great joy, which shall be to all the people;
texts.luk.2.11: for to-day a Saviour has been born to you in David's city, who is Christ [the] Lord.
texts.luk.2.12: And this is the sign to you: ye shall find a babe wrapped in swaddling-clothes, and lying in a manger.
texts.luk.2.13: And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying,
texts.luk.2.14: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good pleasure in men.
texts.luk.2.15: And it came to pass, as the angels departed from them into heaven, that the shepherds said to one another, Let us make our way then now as far as Bethlehem, and let us see this thing that is come to pass, which the Lord has made known to us.
texts.luk.2.16: And they came with haste, and found both Mary and Joseph, and the babe lying in the manger;
texts.luk.2.17: and having seen [it] they made known about the country the thing which had been said to them concerning this child.
texts.luk.2.18: And all who heard [it] wondered at the things said to them by the shepherds.
texts.luk.2.19: But Mary kept all these things [in her mind], pondering [them] in her heart.
texts.luk.2.20: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all things which they had heard and seen, as it had been said to them.
texts.luk.2.21: And when eight days were fulfilled for circumcising him, his name was called Jesus, which was the name given by the angel before he had been conceived in the womb.
texts.luk.2.22: And when the days were fulfilled for their purifying according to the law of Moses, they brought him to Jerusalem to present [him] to the Lord
texts.luk.2.23: (as it is written in the law of [the] Lord: Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord),
texts.luk.2.24: and to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of [the] Lord: A pair of turtle doves, or two young pigeons.
texts.luk.2.25: And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon; and this man was just and pious, awaiting the consolation of Israel, and [the] Holy Spirit was upon him.
texts.luk.2.26: And it was divinely communicated to him by the Holy Spirit, that he should not see death before he should see [the] Lord's Christ.
texts.luk.2.27: And he came in the Spirit into the temple; and as the parents brought in the child Jesus that they might do for him according to the custom of the law,
texts.luk.2.28: *he* received him into his arms, and blessed God, and said,
texts.luk.2.29: Lord, now thou lettest thy bondman go, according to thy word, in peace;
texts.luk.2.30: for mine eyes have seen thy salvation,
texts.luk.2.31: which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples;
texts.luk.2.32: a light for revelation of [the] Gentiles and [the] glory of thy people Israel.
texts.luk.2.33: And his father and mother wondered at the things which were said concerning him.
texts.luk.2.34: And Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary his mother, Lo, this [child] is set for the fall and rising up of many in Israel, and for a sign spoken against;
texts.luk.2.35: (and even a sword shall go through thine own soul;) so that [the] thoughts may be revealed from many hearts.
texts.luk.2.36: And there was a prophetess, Anna, daughter of Phanuel, of [the] tribe of Asher, who was far advanced in years, having lived with [her] husband seven years from her virginity,
texts.luk.2.37: and herself a widow up to eighty-four years; who did not depart from the temple, serving night and day with fastings and prayers;
texts.luk.2.38: and she coming up the same hour gave praise to the Lord, and spoke of him to all those who waited for redemption in Jerusalem.
texts.luk.2.39: And when they had completed all things according to the law of [the] Lord, they returned to Galilee to their own city Nazareth.
texts.luk.2.40: And the child grew and waxed strong [in spirit], filled with wisdom, and God's grace was upon him.
texts.luk.2.41: And his parents went yearly to Jerusalem at the feast of the passover.
texts.luk.2.42: And when he was twelve years old, and they went up [to Jerusalem] according to the custom of the feast
texts.luk.2.43: and had completed the days, as they returned, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and his parents knew not [of it];
texts.luk.2.44: but, supposing him to be in the company that journeyed together, they went a day's journey, and sought him among their relations and acquaintances:
texts.luk.2.45: and not having found him they returned to Jerusalem seeking him.
texts.luk.2.46: And it came to pass, after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers and hearing them and asking them questions.
texts.luk.2.47: And all who heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.
texts.luk.2.48: And when they saw him they were amazed: and his mother said to him, Child, why hast thou dealt thus with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee distressed.
texts.luk.2.49: And he said to them, Why [is it] that ye have sought me? did ye not know that I ought to be [occupied] in my Father's business?
texts.luk.2.50: And they understood not the thing that he said to them.
texts.luk.2.51: And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was in subjection to them. And his mother kept all these things in her heart.
texts.luk.2.52: And Jesus advanced in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and men.
texts.luk.3.1: Now in the fifteenth year of the government of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea, and Herod tetrarch of Galilee, and Philip his brother tetrarch of Ituraea and the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
texts.luk.3.2: in the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, [the] word of God came upon John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness.
texts.luk.3.3: And he came into all the district round the Jordan, preaching [the] baptism of repentance for [the] remission of sins,
texts.luk.3.4: as it is written in [the] book of [the] words of Esaias the prophet: Voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare ye the way of [the] Lord, make straight his paths.
