texts.luk.15.20: And he rose up and went to his own father. But while he was yet a long way off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell upon his neck, and covered him with kisses.
texts.luk.15.21: And the son said to him, Father, I have sinned against heaven and before thee; I am no longer worthy to be called thy son.
texts.luk.15.22: But the father said to his bondmen, Bring out the best robe and clothe him in [it], and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet;
texts.luk.15.23: and bring the fatted calf and kill it, and let us eat and make merry:
texts.luk.15.24: for this my son was dead and has come to life, was lost and has been found. And they began to make merry.
texts.luk.15.25: And his elder son was in the field; and as, coming [up], he drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.
texts.luk.15.26: And having called one of the servants, he inquired what these things might be.
texts.luk.15.27: And he said to him, Thy brother is come, and thy father has killed the fatted calf because he has received him safe and well.
texts.luk.15.28: But he became angry and would not go in. And his father went out and besought him.
texts.luk.15.29: But he answering said to his father, Behold, so many years I serve thee, and never have I transgressed a commandment of thine; and to me hast thou never given a kid that I might make merry with my friends:
texts.luk.15.30: but when this thy son, who has devoured thy substance with harlots, is come, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.
texts.luk.15.31: But he said to him, Child, *thou* art ever with me, and all that is mine is thine.
texts.luk.15.32: But it was right to make merry and rejoice, because this thy brother was dead and has come to life again, and was lost and has been found.
texts.luk.16.1: And he said also to [his] disciples, There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and *he* was accused to him as wasting his goods.
texts.luk.16.2: And having called him, he said to him, What [is] this that I hear of thee? give the reckoning of thy stewardship, for thou canst be no longer steward.
texts.luk.16.3: And the steward said within himself, What shall I do; for my lord is taking the stewardship from me? I am not able to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
texts.luk.16.4: I know what I will do, that when I shall have been removed from the stewardship I may be received into their houses.
texts.luk.16.5: And having called to [him] each one of the debtors of his own lord, he said to the first, How much owest thou to my lord?
texts.luk.16.6: And he said, A hundred baths of oil. And he said to him, Take thy writing and sit down quickly and write fifty.
texts.luk.16.7: Then he said to another, And thou, how much dost thou owe? And he said, A hundred cors of wheat. And he says to him, Take thy writing and write eighty.
texts.luk.16.8: And the lord praised the unrighteous steward because he had done prudently. For the sons of this world are, for their own generation, more prudent than the sons of light.
texts.luk.16.9: And *I* say to you, Make to yourselves friends with the mammon of unrighteousness, that when it fails ye may be received into the eternal tabernacles.
texts.luk.16.10: He that is faithful in the least is faithful also in much; and he that is unrighteous in the least is unrighteous also in much.
texts.luk.16.11: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who shall entrust to you the true?
texts.luk.16.12: and if ye have not been faithful in that which is another's, who shall give to you your own?
texts.luk.16.13: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and will love the other, or he will cleave to the one and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
texts.luk.16.14: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things, and mocked him.
texts.luk.16.15: And he said to them, *Ye* are they who justify themselves before men, but God knows your hearts; for what amongst men is highly thought of is an abomination before God.
texts.luk.16.16: The law and the prophets [were] until John: from that time the glad tidings of the kingdom of God are announced, and every one forces his way into it.
texts.luk.16.17: But it is easier that the heaven and the earth should pass away than that one tittle of the law should fail.
texts.luk.16.18: Every one who puts away his wife and marries another commits adultery; and every one that marries one put away from a husband commits adultery.
texts.luk.16.19: Now there was a rich man and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, making good cheer in splendour every day.
texts.luk.16.20: And [there was] a poor man, by name Lazarus, [who] was laid at his gateway full of sores,
texts.luk.16.21: and desiring to be filled with the crumbs which fell from the table of the rich man; but the dogs also coming licked his sores.
texts.luk.16.22: And it came to pass that the poor man died, and that he was carried away by the angels into the bosom of Abraham. And the rich man also died and was buried.
texts.luk.16.23: And in hades lifting up his eyes, being in torments, he sees Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
texts.luk.16.24: And he crying out said, Father Abraham, have compassion on me, and send Lazarus that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am suffering in this flame.
texts.luk.16.25: But Abraham said, Child, recollect that *thou* hast fully received thy good things in thy lifetime, and likewise Lazarus evil things. But now he is comforted here, and *thou* art in suffering.
texts.luk.16.26: And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm is fixed, so that those who desire to pass hence to you cannot, nor do they who [desire to cross] from there pass over unto us.
texts.luk.16.27: And he said, I beseech thee then, father, that thou wouldest send him to the house of my father,
texts.luk.16.28: for I have five brothers, so that he may earnestly testify to them, that they also may not come to this place of torment.
texts.luk.16.29: But Abraham says to him, They have Moses and the prophets: let them hear them.
texts.luk.16.30: But he said, Nay, father Abraham, but if one from the dead should go to them, they will repent.
texts.luk.16.31: And he said to him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, not even if one rise from among [the] dead will they be persuaded.
texts.luk.17.1: And he said to his disciples, It cannot be but that offences come, but woe [to him] by whom they come!
texts.luk.17.2: It would be [more] profitable for him if a millstone were hanged about his neck and he cast into the sea, than that he should be a snare to one of these little ones.
texts.luk.17.3: Take heed to yourselves: if thy brother should sin, rebuke him; and if he should repent, forgive him.
texts.luk.17.4: And if he should sin against thee seven times in the day, and seven times should return to thee, saying, I repent, thou shalt forgive him.
texts.luk.17.5: And the apostles said to the Lord, Give more faith to us.
texts.luk.17.6: But the Lord said, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard [seed], ye had said to this sycamine tree, Be thou rooted up, and be thou planted in the sea, and it would have obeyed you.
texts.luk.17.7: But which of you [is there] who, having a bondman ploughing or shepherding, when he comes in out of the field, will say, Come and lie down immediately to table?
texts.luk.17.8: But will he not say to him, Prepare what I shall sup on, and gird thyself and serve me that I may eat and drink; and after that *thou* shalt eat and drink?
texts.luk.17.9: Is he thankful to the bondman because he has done what was ordered? I judge not.
texts.luk.17.10: Thus *ye* also, when ye shall have done all things that have been ordered you, say, We are unprofitable bondmen; we have done what it was our duty to do.
texts.luk.17.11: And it came to pass as he was going up to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
texts.luk.17.12: And as he entered into a certain village ten leprous men met him, who stood afar off.
texts.luk.17.13: And they lifted up [their] voice saying, Jesus, Master, have compassion on us.
texts.luk.17.14: And seeing [them] he said to them, Go, shew yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass as they were going they were cleansed.
texts.luk.17.15: And one of them, seeing that he was cured, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice,
texts.luk.17.16: and fell on [his] face at his feet giving him thanks: and *he* was a Samaritan.
texts.luk.17.17: And Jesus answering said, Were not the ten cleansed? but the nine, where [are they]?
texts.luk.17.18: There have not been found to return and give glory to God save this stranger.
texts.luk.17.19: And he said to him, Rise up and go thy way: thy faith has made thee well.
texts.luk.17.20: And having been asked by the Pharisees, When is the kingdom of God coming? he answered them and said, The kingdom of God does not come with observation;
texts.luk.17.21: nor shall they say, Lo here, or, Lo there; for behold, the kingdom of God is in the midst of you.
texts.luk.17.22: And he said to the disciples, Days are coming, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and shall not see [it].
texts.luk.17.23: And they will say to you, Lo here, or Lo there; go not, nor follow [them].
texts.luk.17.24: For as the lightning shines which lightens from [one end] under heaven to [the other end] under heaven, thus shall the Son of man be in his day.
texts.luk.17.25: But first he must suffer many things and be rejected of this generation.
texts.luk.17.26: And as it took place in the days of Noe, thus also shall it be in the days of the Son of man:
texts.luk.17.27: they ate, they drank, they married, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed all [of them];
texts.luk.17.28: and in like manner as took place in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
texts.luk.17.29: but on the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulphur from heaven, and destroyed all [of them]:
texts.luk.17.30: after this [manner] shall it be in the day that the Son of man is revealed.
texts.luk.17.31: In that day, he who shall be on the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not go down to take it away; and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.
texts.luk.17.33: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it, and whosoever shall lose it shall preserve it.
texts.luk.17.34: I say to you, In that night there shall be two [men] upon one bed; one shall be seized and the other shall be let go.
texts.luk.17.35: Two [women] shall be grinding together; the one shall be seized and the other shall be let go.
texts.luk.17.36: [Two men shall be in the field; the one shall be seized and the other let go.]
texts.luk.17.37: And answering they say to him, Where, Lord? And he said to them, Where the body [is], there the eagles will be gathered together.
texts.luk.18.1: And he spoke also a parable to them to the purport that they should always pray and not faint,
texts.luk.18.2: saying, There was a judge in a city, not fearing God and not respecting man:
texts.luk.18.3: and there was a widow in that city, and she came to him, saying, Avenge me of mine adverse party.
texts.luk.18.4: And he would not for a time; but afterwards he said within himself, If even I fear not God and respect not man,
texts.luk.18.5: at any rate because this widow annoys me I will avenge her, that she may not by perpetually coming completely harass me.
texts.luk.18.6: And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge says.
texts.luk.18.7: And shall not God at all avenge his elect, who cry to him day and night, and he bears long as to them?
texts.luk.18.8: I say unto you that he will avenge them speedily. But when the Son of man comes, shall he indeed find faith on the earth?
texts.luk.18.9: And he spoke also to some, who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and made nothing of all the rest [of men], this parable:
texts.luk.18.10: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a tax-gatherer.
texts.luk.18.11: The Pharisee, standing, prayed thus to himself: God, I thank thee that I am not as the rest of men, rapacious, unjust, adulterers, or even as this tax-gatherer.
texts.luk.18.12: I fast twice in the week, I tithe everything I gain.
texts.luk.18.13: And the tax-gatherer, standing afar off, would not lift up even his eyes to heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, O God, have compassion on me, the sinner.
texts.luk.18.14: I say unto you, This [man] went down to his house justified rather than that [other]. For every one who exalts himself shall be humbled, and he that humbles himself shall be exalted.
texts.luk.18.15: And they brought to him also infants that he might touch them, but the disciples when they saw [it] rebuked them.
texts.luk.18.16: But Jesus calling them to [him] said, Suffer little children to come to me, and do not forbid them, for of such is the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.18.17: Verily I say to you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.
texts.luk.18.18: And a certain ruler asked him saying, Good teacher, having done what, shall I inherit eternal life?
texts.luk.18.19: But Jesus said to him, Why callest thou me good? There is none good but one, God.
texts.luk.18.20: Thou knowest the commandments: Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother.
texts.luk.18.21: And he said, All these things have I kept from my youth.
texts.luk.18.22: And when Jesus had heard this, he said to him, One thing is lacking to thee yet: Sell all that thou hast and distribute to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in the heavens, and come, follow me.
texts.luk.18.23: But when he heard this he became very sorrowful, for he was very rich.
texts.luk.18.24: But when Jesus saw that he became very sorrowful, he said, How difficultly shall those who have riches enter into the kingdom of God;
texts.luk.18.25: for it is easier for a camel to enter through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.18.26: And those who heard it said, And who can be saved?
texts.luk.18.27: But he said, The things that are impossible with men are possible with God.
texts.luk.18.28: And Peter said, Behold, *we* have left all things and have followed thee.
texts.luk.18.29: And he said to them, Verily I say to you, There is no one who has left home, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God's sake,
texts.luk.18.30: who shall not receive manifold more at this time, and in the coming age life eternal.
texts.luk.18.31: And he took the twelve to [him] and said to them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written of the Son of man by the prophets shall be accomplished;
texts.luk.18.32: for he shall be delivered up to the nations, and shall be mocked, and insulted, and spit upon.
texts.luk.18.33: And when they have scourged [him] they will kill him; and on the third day he will rise again.
texts.luk.18.34: And they understood nothing of these things. And this word was hidden from them, and they did not know what was said.
texts.luk.18.35: And it came to pass when he came into the neighbourhood of Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the wayside begging.
texts.luk.18.36: And when he heard the crowd passing, he inquired what this might be.
texts.luk.18.37: And they told him that Jesus the Nazaraean was passing by.
texts.luk.18.38: And he called out saying, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.
texts.luk.18.39: And those [who were] going before rebuked him that he might be silent; but *he* cried out so much the more, Son of David, have mercy on me.
texts.luk.18.40: And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be led to him. And when he drew nigh he asked him [saying],
texts.luk.18.41: What wilt thou that I shall do to thee? And he said, Lord, that I may see.
texts.luk.18.42: And Jesus said to him, See: thy faith has healed thee.
texts.luk.18.43: And immediately he saw, and followed him, glorifying God. And all the people when they saw [it] gave praise to God.
texts.luk.19.1: And he entered and passed through Jericho.
texts.luk.19.2: And behold, [there was] a man by name called Zacchaeus, and he was chief tax-gatherer, and he was rich.
texts.luk.19.3: And he sought to see Jesus who he was: and he could not for the crowd, because he was little in stature.
texts.luk.19.4: And running on before, he got up into a sycamore that he might see him, for he was going to pass that [way].
texts.luk.19.5: And when he came up to the place, Jesus looked up and saw him, and said to him, Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for to-day I must remain in thy house.
texts.luk.19.6: And he made haste and came down, and received him with joy.
texts.luk.19.7: And all murmured when they saw [it], saying, He has turned in to lodge with a sinful man.
texts.luk.19.8: But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from any man by false accusation, I return [him] fourfold.
texts.luk.19.9: And Jesus said to him, To-day salvation is come to this house, inasmuch as he also is a son of Abraham;
texts.luk.19.10: for the Son of man has come to seek and to save that which is lost.
texts.luk.19.11: But as they were listening to these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was near to Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was about to be immediately manifested.
texts.luk.19.12: He said therefore, A certain high-born man went to a distant country to receive for himself a kingdom and return.
texts.luk.19.13: And having called his own ten bondmen, he gave to them ten minas, and said to them, Trade while I am coming.
texts.luk.19.14: But his citizens hated him, and sent an embassy after him, saying, We will not that this [man] should reign over us.
texts.luk.19.15: And it came to pass on his arrival back again, having received the kingdom, that he desired these bondmen to whom he gave the money to be called to him, in order that he might know what every one had gained by trading.
texts.luk.19.16: And the first came up, saying, [My] Lord, thy mina has produced ten minas.
texts.luk.19.17: And he said to him, Well [done], thou good bondman; because thou hast been faithful in that which is least, be thou in authority over ten cities.
texts.luk.19.18: And the second came, saying, [My] Lord, thy mina has made five minas.
texts.luk.19.19: And he said also to this one, And *thou*, be over five cities.
texts.luk.19.20: And another came, saying, [My] Lord, lo, [there is] thy mina, which I have kept laid up in a towel.
texts.luk.19.21: For I feared thee because thou art a harsh man: thou takest up what thou hast not laid down, and thou reapest what thou hast not sowed.
texts.luk.19.22: He says to him, Out of thy mouth will I judge thee, wicked bondman: thou knewest that *I* am a harsh man, taking up what I have not laid down and reaping what I have not sowed.
texts.luk.19.23: And why didst thou not give my money to [the] bank; and *I* should have received it, at my coming, with interest?
texts.luk.19.24: And he said to those that stood by, Take from him the mina and give [it] to him who has the ten minas.
texts.luk.19.25: And they said to him, Lord, he has ten minas.
texts.luk.19.26: For I say unto you, that to every one that has shall be given; but from him that has not, that even which he has shall be taken from him.
texts.luk.19.27: Moreover those mine enemies, who would not [have] me to reign over them, bring them here and slay [them] before me.
texts.luk.19.28: And having said these things, he went on before, going up to Jerusalem.
texts.luk.19.29: And it came to pass as he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany at the mountain called [the mount] of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
texts.luk.19.30: saying, Go into the village over against [you], in which ye will find, on entering it, a colt tied up, on which no [child] of man ever sat at any time: loose it and lead it [here].
texts.luk.19.31: And if any one ask you, Why do ye loose [it]? thus shall ye say to him, Because the Lord has need of it.
texts.luk.19.32: And they that were sent, having gone their way, found as he had said to them.
texts.luk.19.33: And as they were loosing the colt, its masters said to them, Why loose ye the colt?
texts.luk.19.34: And they said, Because the Lord has need of it.
texts.luk.19.35: And they led it to Jesus; and having cast their own garments on the colt, they put Jesus on [it].
texts.luk.19.36: And as he went, they strewed their clothes in the way.
texts.luk.19.37: And as he drew near, already at the descent of the mount of Olives, all the multitude of the disciples began, rejoicing, to praise God with a loud voice for all the works of power which they had seen,
texts.luk.19.38: saying, Blessed the King that comes in the name of [the] Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
texts.luk.19.39: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him, Teacher, rebuke thy disciples.
texts.luk.19.40: And he answering said to them, I say unto you, If these shall be silent, the stones will cry out.
texts.luk.19.41: And as he drew near, seeing the city, he wept over it,
texts.luk.19.42: saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, even at least in this thy day, the things that are for thy peace: but now they are hid from thine eyes;
texts.luk.19.43: for days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall make a palisaded mound about thee, and shall close thee around, and keep thee in on every side,
texts.luk.19.44: and shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children in thee; and shall not leave in thee a stone upon a stone: because thou knewest not the season of thy visitation.
texts.luk.19.45: And entering into the temple, he began to cast out those that sold and bought in it,
texts.luk.19.46: saying to them, It is written, My house is a house of prayer, but *ye* have made it a den of robbers.
texts.luk.19.47: And he was teaching day by day in the temple: and the chief priests and the scribes and the chief of the people sought to destroy him,
texts.luk.19.48: and did not find what they could do, for all the people hung on him to hear.
texts.luk.20.1: And it came to pass on one of the days, as he was teaching the people in the temple, and announcing the glad tidings, the chief priests and the scribes with the elders came up,
texts.luk.20.2: and spoke to him saying, Tell us by what authority thou doest these things, or who is it who has given thee this authority?
texts.luk.20.3: And he answering said to them, *I* also will ask you [one] thing, and tell me:
texts.luk.20.4: The baptism of John, was it of heaven or of men?
texts.luk.20.5: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, If we should say, Of heaven, he will say, Why have ye not believed him?
texts.luk.20.6: but if we should say, Of men, the whole people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.
texts.luk.20.7: And they answered, they did not know whence.
texts.luk.20.8: And Jesus said to them, Neither do *I* tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.luk.20.9: And he began to speak to the people this parable: A man planted a vineyard and let it out to husbandmen, and left the country for a long time.
texts.luk.20.10: And in the season he sent to the husbandmen a bondman, that they might give to him of the fruit of the vineyard; but the husbandmen, having beaten him, sent [him] away empty.
texts.luk.20.11: And again he sent another bondman; but they, having beaten him also, and cast insult upon him, sent [him] away empty.
texts.luk.20.12: And again he sent a third; and they, having wounded him also, cast [him] out.
texts.luk.20.13: And the lord of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: perhaps when they see him they will respect [him].
texts.luk.20.14: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir; [come,] let us kill him, that the inheritance may become ours.
texts.luk.20.15: And having cast him forth out of the vineyard, they killed [him]. What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do to them?
texts.luk.20.16: He will come and destroy those husbandmen, and will give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it they said, May it never be!
texts.luk.20.17: But he looking at them said, What then is this that is written, The stone which they that builded rejected, this has become the corner-stone?
texts.luk.20.18: Every one falling on this stone shall be broken, but on whomsoever it shall fall, it shall grind him to powder.
texts.luk.20.19: And the chief priests and the scribes sought the same hour to lay hands on him, and they feared the people; for they knew that he had spoken this parable of them.
texts.luk.20.20: And having watched [him], they sent out suborned persons, pretending to be just men, that they might take hold of him in [his] language, so that they might deliver him up to the power and authority of the governor.
texts.luk.20.21: And they asked him saying, Teacher, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, and acceptest no [man's] person, but teachest with truth the way of God:
texts.luk.20.22: Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Caesar, or not?
texts.luk.20.23: But perceiving their deceit he said to them, Why do ye tempt me?
texts.luk.20.24: Shew me a denarius. Whose image and superscription has it? And answering they said, Caesar's.
texts.luk.20.25: And he said to them, Pay therefore what is Caesar's to Caesar, and what is God's to God.
texts.luk.20.26: And they were not able to take hold of him in [his] expressions before the people, and, wondering at his answer, they were silent.
texts.luk.20.27: And some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is any resurrection, coming up [to him],
texts.luk.20.28: demanded of him saying, Teacher, Moses wrote to us, If any one's brother, who has a wife, die, and he die childless, his brother shall take the wife and raise up seed to his brother.
texts.luk.20.29: There were then seven brethren: and the first, having taken a wife, died childless;
texts.luk.20.30: and the second [took the woman, and *he* died childless];
texts.luk.20.31: and the third took her: and in like manner also the seven left no children and died;
texts.luk.20.32: and last of all the woman also died.
texts.luk.20.33: In the resurrection therefore of which of them does she become wife, for the seven had her as wife?
texts.luk.20.34: And Jesus said to them, The sons of this world marry and are given in marriage,
texts.luk.20.35: but they who are counted worthy to have part in that world, and the resurrection from among [the] dead, neither marry nor are given in marriage;
texts.luk.20.36: for neither can they die any more, for they are equal to angels, and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
texts.luk.20.37: But that the dead rise, even Moses shewed in [the section of] the bush, when he called [the] Lord the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob;
texts.luk.20.38: but he is not God of [the] dead but of [the] living; for all live for him.
texts.luk.20.39: And some of the scribes answering said, Teacher, thou hast well spoken.
texts.luk.20.40: For they did not dare any more to ask him anything.
texts.luk.20.41: And he said to them, How do they say that the Christ is David's son,
texts.luk.20.42: and David himself says in the book of Psalms, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand
texts.luk.20.43: until I put thine enemies [as] footstool of thy feet?
texts.luk.20.44: David therefore calls him Lord, and how is he his son?
texts.luk.20.45: And, as all the people were listening, he said to his disciples,
texts.luk.20.46: Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes, and who love salutations in the market-places, and first seats in the synagogues, and first places at suppers;
texts.luk.20.47: who devour the houses of widows, and as a pretext make long prayers. These shall receive a severer judgment.
texts.luk.21.1: And he looked up and saw the rich casting their gifts into the treasury;
texts.luk.21.2: but he saw also a certain poor widow casting therein two mites.
texts.luk.21.3: And he said, Verily I say unto you, that this poor widow has cast in more than all;
texts.luk.21.4: for all these out of their abundance have cast into the gifts [of God]; but she out of her need has cast in all the living which she had.
texts.luk.21.5: And as some spoke of the temple, that it was adorned with goodly stones and consecrated offerings, he said,
texts.luk.21.6: [As to] these things which ye are beholding, days are coming in which there shall not be left stone upon stone which shall not be thrown down.
texts.luk.21.7: And they asked him saying, Teacher, when then shall these things be; and what [is] the sign when these things are going to take place?
texts.luk.21.8: And he said, See that ye be not led astray, for many shall come in my name, saying, *I* am [he], and the time is drawn nigh: go ye not [therefore] after them.
texts.luk.21.9: And when ye shall hear of wars and tumults, be not terrified, for these things must first take place, but the end is not immediately.
texts.luk.21.10: Then he said to them, Nation shall rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;
texts.luk.21.11: there shall be both great earthquakes in different places, and famines and pestilences; and there shall be fearful sights and great signs from heaven.
texts.luk.21.12: But before all these things they shall lay their hands upon you and persecute you, delivering [you] up to synagogues and prisons, bringing [you] before kings and governors on account of my name;
texts.luk.21.13: but it shall turn out to you for a testimony.
texts.luk.21.14: Settle therefore in your hearts not to meditate beforehand [your] defence,
texts.luk.21.15: for *I* will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your opposers shall not be able to reply to or resist.
texts.luk.21.16: But ye will be delivered up even by parents and brethren and relations and friends, and they shall put to death [some] from among you,
texts.luk.21.17: and ye will be hated of all for my name's sake.
texts.luk.21.18: And a hair of your head shall in no wise perish.
texts.luk.21.19: By your patient endurance gain your souls.
texts.luk.21.20: But when ye see Jerusalem encompassed with armies, then know that its desolation is drawn nigh.
texts.luk.21.21: Then let those who are in Judaea flee to the mountains, and those who are in the midst of it depart out, and those who are in the country not enter into it;
texts.luk.21.22: for these are days of avenging, that all the things that are written may be accomplished.
texts.luk.21.23: But woe to them that are with child and to them who give suck in those days, for there shall be great distress upon the land and wrath upon this people.
texts.luk.21.24: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and be led captive into all the nations; and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of [the] nations until [the] times of [the] nations be fulfilled.
texts.luk.21.25: And there shall be signs in sun and moon and stars, and upon the earth distress of nations in perplexity [at] the roar of the sea and rolling waves,
texts.luk.21.26: men ready to die through fear and expectation of what is coming on the habitable earth, for the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.
texts.luk.21.27: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
texts.luk.21.28: But when these things begin to come to pass, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption draws nigh.
texts.luk.21.29: And he spoke a parable to them: Behold the fig-tree and all the trees;
texts.luk.21.30: when they already sprout, ye know of your own selves, [on] looking [at them], that already the summer is near.
texts.luk.21.31: So also *ye*, when ye see these things take place, know that the kingdom of God is near.
texts.luk.21.32: Verily I say unto you, that this generation shall in no wise pass away until all come to pass.
texts.luk.21.33: The heaven and the earth shall pass away, but my words shall in no wise pass away.
texts.luk.21.34: But take heed to yourselves lest possibly your hearts be laden with surfeiting and drinking and cares of life, and that day come upon you suddenly unawares;
texts.luk.21.35: for as a snare shall it come upon all them that dwell upon the face of the whole earth.
texts.luk.21.36: Watch therefore, praying at every season, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things which are about to come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.
texts.luk.21.37: And by day he was teaching in the temple, and by night, going out, he remained abroad on the mountain called [the mount] of Olives;
texts.luk.21.38: and all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.
texts.luk.22.1: Now the feast of unleavened bread, which [is] called the passover, drew nigh,
texts.luk.22.2: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might kill him; for they feared the people.
texts.luk.22.3: And Satan entered into Judas, who was surnamed Iscariote, being of the number of the twelve.
texts.luk.22.4: And he went away and spoke with the chief priests and captains as to how he should deliver him up to them.
texts.luk.22.5: And they were rejoiced, and agreed to give him money.
texts.luk.22.6: And he came to an agreement to do it, and sought an opportunity to deliver him up to them away from the crowd.
texts.luk.22.7: And the day of unleavened bread came, in which the passover was to be killed.
texts.luk.22.8: And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare the passover for us, that we may eat [it].
texts.luk.22.9: But they said to him, Where wilt thou that we prepare [it]?
texts.luk.22.10: And he said to them, Behold, as ye enter into the city a man will meet you, carrying an earthen pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he goes in;
texts.luk.22.11: and ye shall say to the master of the house, The Teacher says to thee, Where is the guest-chamber where I may eat the passover with my disciples?
texts.luk.22.12: And *he* will shew you a large upper room furnished: there make ready.
texts.luk.22.13: And having gone they found it as he had said to them; and they prepared the passover.
texts.luk.22.14: And when the hour was come, he placed himself at table, and the [twelve] apostles with him.
texts.luk.22.15: And he said to them, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer.
texts.luk.22.16: For I say unto you, that I will not eat any more at all of it until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.22.17: And having received a cup, when he had given thanks he said, Take this and divide it among yourselves.
texts.luk.22.18: For I say unto you, that I will not drink at all of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God come.
texts.luk.22.19: And having taken a loaf, when he had given thanks, he broke [it], and gave [it] to them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.
texts.luk.22.20: In like manner also the cup, after having supped, saying, This cup [is] the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
texts.luk.22.21: Moreover, behold, the hand of him that delivers me up [is] with me on the table;
texts.luk.22.22: and the Son of man indeed goes as it is determined, but woe unto that man by whom he is delivered up.
texts.luk.22.23: And *they* began to question together among themselves who then it could be of them who was about to do this.
texts.luk.22.24: And there was also a strife among them which of them should be held to be [the] greatest.
texts.luk.22.25: And he said to them, The kings of the nations rule over them, and they that exercise authority over them are called benefactors.
texts.luk.22.26: But *ye* [shall] not [be] thus; but let the greater among you be as the younger, and the leader as he that serves.
texts.luk.22.27: For which [is] greater, he that is at table or he that serves? [Is] not he that is at table? But *I* am in the midst of you as the one that serves.
texts.luk.22.28: But *ye* are they who have persevered with me in my temptations.
texts.luk.22.29: And *I* appoint unto you, as my Father has appointed unto me, a kingdom,
texts.luk.22.30: that ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
texts.luk.22.31: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to have you, to sift [you] as wheat;
texts.luk.22.32: but *I* have besought for thee that thy faith fail not; and *thou*, when once thou hast been restored, confirm thy brethren.
texts.luk.22.33: And he said to him, Lord, with thee I am ready to go both to prison and to death.
texts.luk.22.34: And he said, I tell thee, Peter, [the] cock shall not crow to-day before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.
texts.luk.22.35: And he said to them, When I sent you without purse and scrip and sandals, did ye lack anything? And they said, Nothing.
texts.luk.22.36: He said therefore to them, But now he that has a purse let him take [it], in like manner also a scrip, and he that has none let him sell his garment and buy a sword;
texts.luk.22.37: for I say unto you, that this that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned with [the] lawless: for also the things concerning me have an end.
texts.luk.22.38: And they said, Lord, behold here are two swords. And he said to them, It is enough.
texts.luk.22.39: And going forth he went according to his custom to the mount of Olives, and the disciples also followed him.
texts.luk.22.40: And when he was at the place he said to them, Pray that ye enter not into temptation.
texts.luk.22.41: And he was withdrawn from them about a stone's throw, and having knelt down he prayed,
texts.luk.22.42: saying, Father, if thou wilt remove this cup from me: -- but then, not my will, but thine be done.
texts.luk.22.43: And an angel appeared to him from heaven strengthening him.
texts.luk.22.44: And being in conflict he prayed more intently. And his sweat became as great drops of blood, falling down upon the earth.
texts.luk.22.45: And rising up from his prayer, coming to the disciples, he found them sleeping from grief.
texts.luk.22.46: And he said to them, Why sleep ye? rise up and pray that ye enter not into temptation.
texts.luk.22.47: As he was yet speaking, behold, a crowd, and he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went on before them, and drew near to Jesus to kiss him.
texts.luk.22.48: And Jesus said to him, Judas, deliverest thou up the Son of man with a kiss?
texts.luk.22.49: And they who were around him, seeing what was going to follow, said [to him], Lord, shall we smite with [the] sword?
texts.luk.22.50: And a certain one from among them smote the bondman of the high priest and took off his right ear.
texts.luk.22.51: And Jesus answering said, Suffer thus far; and having touched his ear, he healed him.
texts.luk.22.52: And Jesus said to the chief priests and captains of the temple and elders, who were come against him, Have ye come out as against a robber with swords and sticks?
texts.luk.22.53: When I was day by day with you in the temple ye did not stretch out your hands against me; but this is your hour and the power of darkness.
texts.luk.22.54: And having laid hold on him, they led him [away], and they led [him] into the house of the high priest. And Peter followed afar off.
texts.luk.22.55: And they having lit a fire in the midst of the court and sat down together, Peter sat among them.
texts.luk.22.56: And a certain maid, having seen him sitting by the light, and having fixed her eyes upon him, said, And this [man] was with him.
texts.luk.22.57: But he denied [him], saying, Woman, I do not know him.
texts.luk.22.58: And after a short time another seeing him said, And *thou* art of them. But Peter said, Man, I am not.
texts.luk.22.59: And after the lapse of about one hour another stoutly maintained it, saying, In truth this [man] also was with him, for also he is a Galilaean.
texts.luk.22.60: And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he was yet speaking, [the] cock crew.
texts.luk.22.61: And the Lord, turning round, looked at Peter; and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he said to him, Before [the] cock crow thou shalt deny me thrice.
texts.luk.22.62: And Peter, going forth without, wept bitterly.
texts.luk.22.63: And the men who held him mocked him, beating [him];
texts.luk.22.64: and covering him up, asked him saying, Prophesy, who is it that struck thee?
texts.luk.22.65: And they said many other injurious things to him.
texts.luk.22.66: And when it was day, the elderhood of the people, both [the] chief priests and scribes, were gathered together, and led him into their council, saying,
texts.luk.22.67: If *thou* art the Christ, tell us. And he said to them, If I tell you, ye will not at all believe;
texts.luk.22.68: and if I should ask [you], ye would not answer me at all, nor let me go;
texts.luk.22.69: but henceforth shall the Son of man be sitting on the right hand of the power of God.
texts.luk.22.70: And they all said, *Thou* then art the Son of God? And he said to them, *Ye* say that I am.
texts.luk.22.71: And they said, What need have we any more of witness, for we have heard ourselves out of his mouth?
texts.luk.23.1: And the whole multitude of them, rising up, led him to Pilate.
texts.luk.23.2: And they began to accuse him, saying, We have found this [man] perverting our nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ, a king.
texts.luk.23.3: And Pilate demanded of him saying, Art *thou* the king of the Jews? And he answering him said, Thou sayest.
texts.luk.23.4: And Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, I find no guilt in this man.
texts.luk.23.5: But they insisted, saying, He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judaea, beginning from Galilee even on to here.
texts.luk.23.6: But Pilate, having heard Galilee [named], demanded if the man were a Galilaean;
texts.luk.23.7: and having learned that he was of Herod's jurisdiction, remitted him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem in those days.
texts.luk.23.8: And when Herod saw Jesus he greatly rejoiced, for he had been a long while desirous of seeing him, because of hearing many things concerning him, and he hoped to see some sign done by him;
texts.luk.23.9: and he questioned him in many words, but *he* answered him nothing.
texts.luk.23.10: And the chief priests and the scribes stood and accused him violently.
texts.luk.23.11: And Herod with his troops having set him at nought and mocked him, having put a splendid robe upon him, sent him back to Pilate.
texts.luk.23.12: And Pilate and Herod became friends with one another the same day, for they had been at enmity before between themselves.
texts.luk.23.13: And Pilate, having called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
texts.luk.23.14: said to them, Ye have brought to me this man as turning away the people [to rebellion], and behold, I, having examined him before you, have found nothing criminal in this man as to the things of which ye accuse him;
texts.luk.23.15: nor Herod either, for I remitted you to him, and behold, nothing worthy of death is done by him.
texts.luk.23.16: Having chastised him therefore, I will release him.
texts.luk.23.17: ( Now he was obliged to release one for them at the feast.)
texts.luk.23.18: But they cried out in a mass saying, Away with this [man] and release Barabbas to us;
texts.luk.23.19: who was one who, for a certain tumult which had taken place in the city, and [for] murder, had been cast into prison.
texts.luk.23.20: Pilate therefore, desirous to release Jesus, again addressed [them].
texts.luk.23.21: But they cried out in reply saying, Crucify, crucify him.
texts.luk.23.22: And he said the third time to them, What evil then has this [man] done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will chastise him therefore and release him.
texts.luk.23.23: But they were urgent with loud voices, begging that he might be crucified. And their voices [and those of the chief priests] prevailed.
texts.luk.23.24: And Pilate adjudged that what they begged should take place.
texts.luk.23.25: And he released him who, for tumult and murder, had been cast into prison, whom they begged for, and Jesus he delivered up to their will.
texts.luk.23.26: And as they led him away, they laid hold on a certain Simon, a Cyrenian, coming from the field, and put the cross upon him to bear it behind Jesus.
texts.luk.23.27: And a great multitude of the people, and of women who wailed and lamented him, followed him.
texts.luk.23.28: And Jesus turning round to them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over me, but weep over yourselves and over your children;
texts.luk.23.29: for behold, days are coming in which they will say, Blessed [are] the barren, and wombs that have not borne, and breasts that have not given suck.
texts.luk.23.30: Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall upon us; and to the hills, Cover us:
texts.luk.23.31: for if these things are done in the green tree, what shall take place in the dry?
texts.luk.23.32: Now two others also, malefactors, were led with him to be put to death.
texts.luk.23.33: And when they came to the place which is called Skull, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, the other on the left.
texts.luk.23.34: And Jesus said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do. And, parting out his garments, they cast lots.
texts.luk.23.35: And the people stood beholding, and the rulers also [with them] sneered, saying, He has saved others; let him save himself if this is the Christ, the chosen one of God.
texts.luk.23.36: And the soldiers also made game of him, coming up offering him vinegar,
texts.luk.23.37: and saying, If *thou* be the king of the Jews, save thyself.
texts.luk.23.38: And there was also an inscription [written] over him in Greek, and Roman, and Hebrew letters: This is the King of the Jews.
texts.luk.23.39: Now one of the malefactors who had been hanged spoke insultingly to him, saying, Art not thou the Christ? save thyself and us.
texts.luk.23.40: But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost *thou* too not fear God, thou that art under the same judgment?
texts.luk.23.41: and *we* indeed justly, for we receive the just recompense of what we have done; but this [man] has done nothing amiss.
texts.luk.23.42: And he said to Jesus, Remember me, [Lord,] when thou comest in thy kingdom.
texts.luk.23.43: And Jesus said to him, Verily I say to thee, To-day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
texts.luk.23.44: And it was about [the] sixth hour, and there came darkness over the whole land until [the] ninth hour.
texts.luk.23.45: And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple rent in the midst.
texts.luk.23.46: And Jesus, having cried with a loud voice, said, Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit. And having said this, he expired.
texts.luk.23.47: Now the centurion, seeing what took place, glorified God, saying, In very deed this man was just.
texts.luk.23.48: And all the crowds who had come together to that sight, having seen the things that took place, returned, beating [their] breasts.
texts.luk.23.49: And all those who knew him stood afar off, the women also who had followed him from Galilee, beholding these things.
texts.luk.23.50: And behold, a man named Joseph, who was a councillor, a good man and a just
texts.luk.23.51: (this [man] had not assented to their counsel and deed), of Arimathaea, a city of the Jews, who also waited, [himself also,] for the kingdom of God
texts.luk.23.52: -- he having gone to Pilate begged the body of Jesus;
texts.luk.23.53: and having taken it down, wrapped it in fine linen and placed him in a tomb hewn in the rock, where no one had ever been laid.
texts.luk.23.54: And it was preparation day, and [the] sabbath twilight was coming on.
texts.luk.23.55: And women, who had come along with him out of Galilee, having followed, saw the sepulchre and how his body was placed.
texts.luk.23.56: And having returned they prepared aromatic spices and ointments, and remained quiet on the sabbath, according to the commandment.
texts.luk.24.1: But on the morrow of the sabbath, very early indeed in the morning, they came to the tomb, bringing the aromatic spices which they had prepared.
texts.luk.24.2: And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre.
texts.luk.24.3: And when they had entered they found not the body of the Lord Jesus.
texts.luk.24.4: And it came to pass as they were in perplexity about it, that behold, two men suddenly stood by them in shining raiment.
texts.luk.24.5: And as they were filled with fear and bowed their faces to the ground, they said to them, Why seek ye the living one among the dead?
texts.luk.24.6: He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spoke to you, being yet in Galilee,
texts.luk.24.7: saying, The Son of man must be delivered up into the hands of sinners, and be crucified, and rise the third day.
texts.luk.24.9: and, returning from the sepulchre, related all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
texts.luk.24.10: Now it was Mary of Magdala, and Johanna, and Mary the [mother] of James, and the others with them, who told these things to the apostles.
texts.luk.24.11: And their words appeared in their eyes as an idle tale, and they disbelieved them.
texts.luk.24.12: But Peter, rising up, ran to the sepulchre, and stooping down he sees the linen clothes lying there alone, and went away home, wondering at what had happened.
texts.luk.24.13: And behold, two of them were going on the same day to a village distant sixty stadia from Jerusalem, called Emmaus;
texts.luk.24.14: and they conversed with one another about all these things which had taken place.
texts.luk.24.15: And it came to pass as they conversed and reasoned, that Jesus himself drawing nigh, went with them;
texts.luk.24.16: but their eyes were holden so as not to know him.
texts.luk.24.17: And he said to them, What discourses are these which pass between you as ye walk, and are downcast?
texts.luk.24.18: And one [of them], named Cleopas, answering said to him, Thou sojournest alone in Jerusalem, and dost not know what has taken place in it in these days?
texts.luk.24.19: And he said to them, What things? And they said to him, The things concerning Jesus the Nazaraean, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people;
texts.luk.24.20: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him up to [the] judgment of death and crucified him.
texts.luk.24.21: But *we* had hoped that *he* was [the one] who is about to redeem Israel. But then, besides all these things, it is now, to-day, the third day since these things took place.
texts.luk.24.22: And withal, certain women from amongst us astonished us, having been very early at the sepulchre,
texts.luk.24.23: and, not having found his body, came, saying that they also had seen a vision of angels, who say that he is living.
texts.luk.24.24: And some of those with us went to the sepulchre, and found it so, as the women also had said, but him they saw not.
texts.luk.24.25: And *he* said to them, O senseless and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
texts.luk.24.26: Ought not the Christ to have suffered these things and to enter into his glory?
texts.luk.24.27: And having begun from Moses and from all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
texts.luk.24.28: And they drew near to the village where they were going, and *he* made as though he would go farther.
texts.luk.24.29: And they constrained him, saying, Stay with us, for it is toward evening and the day is declining. And he entered in to stay with them.
texts.luk.24.30: And it came to pass as he was at table with them, having taken the bread, he blessed, and having broken it, gave it to them.
texts.luk.24.31: And their eyes were opened, and they recognised him. And he disappeared from them.
texts.luk.24.32: And they said to one another, Was not our heart burning in us as he spoke to us on the way, [and] as he opened the scriptures to us?
texts.luk.24.33: And rising up the same hour, they returned to Jerusalem. And they found the eleven, and those with them, gathered together,
texts.luk.24.34: saying, The Lord is indeed risen and has appeared to Simon.
texts.luk.24.35: And they related what [had happened] on the way, and how he was made known to them in the breaking of bread.
texts.luk.24.36: And as they were saying these things, he himself stood in their midst, and says to them, Peace [be] unto you.
texts.luk.24.37: But they, being confounded and being frightened, supposed they beheld a spirit.
texts.luk.24.38: And he said to them, Why are ye troubled? and why are thoughts rising in your hearts?
texts.luk.24.39: behold my hands and my feet, that it is *I* myself. Handle me and see, for a spirit has not flesh and bones as ye see me having.
texts.luk.24.40: And having said this he shewed them his hands and his feet.
texts.luk.24.41: But while they yet did not believe for joy, and were wondering, he said to them, Have ye anything here to eat?
texts.luk.24.42: And they gave him part of a broiled fish and of a honeycomb;
texts.luk.24.43: and he took it and ate before them.
texts.luk.24.44: And he said to them, These [are] the words which I spoke to you while I was yet with you, that all that is written concerning me in the law of Moses and prophets and psalms must be fulfilled.
texts.luk.24.45: Then he opened their understanding to understand the scriptures,
texts.luk.24.46: and said to them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved the Christ to suffer, and to rise from among the dead the third day;
texts.luk.24.47: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations beginning at Jerusalem.
texts.luk.24.48: And *ye* are witnesses of these things.
texts.luk.24.49: And behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you; but do ye remain in the city till ye be clothed with power from on high.
texts.luk.24.50: And he led them out as far as Bethany, and having lifted up his hands, he blessed them.
texts.luk.24.51: And it came to pass as he was blessing them, he was separated from them and was carried up into heaven.
texts.luk.24.52: And *they*, having done him homage, returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
texts.luk.24.53: and were continually in the temple praising and blessing God.

texts.luk.1.1: Seeing that many did take in hand to set in order a narration of the matters that have been fully assured among us,
texts.luk.1.2: as they did deliver to us, who from the beginning became eye-witnesses, and officers of the Word, --
texts.luk.1.3: it seemed good also to me, having followed from the first after all things exactly, to write to thee in order, most noble Theophilus,
texts.luk.1.4: that thou mayest know the certainty of the things wherein thou wast instructed.
texts.luk.1.5: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest, by name Zacharias, of the course of Abijah, and his wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elisabeth;
texts.luk.1.6: and they were both righteous before God, going on in all the commands and righteousnesses of the Lord blameless,
texts.luk.1.7: and they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days.
texts.luk.1.8: And it came to pass, in his acting as priest, in the order of his course before God,
texts.luk.1.9: according to the custom of the priesthood, his lot was to make perfume, having gone into the sanctuary of the Lord,
texts.luk.1.10: and all the multitude of the people were praying without, at the hour of the perfume.
texts.luk.1.11: And there appeared to him a messenger of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of the perfume,
texts.luk.1.12: and Zacharias, having seen, was troubled, and fear fell on him;
texts.luk.1.13: and the messenger said unto him, `Fear not, Zacharias, for thy supplication was heard, and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear a son to thee, and thou shalt call his name John,
texts.luk.1.14: and there shall be joy to thee, and gladness, and many at his birth shall joy,
texts.luk.1.15: for he shall be great before the Lord, and wine and strong drink he may not drink, and of the Holy Spirit he shall be full, even from his mother's womb;
texts.luk.1.16: and many of the sons of Israel he shall turn to the Lord their God,
texts.luk.1.17: and he shall go before Him, in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn hearts of fathers unto children, and disobedient ones to the wisdom of righteous ones, to make ready for the Lord, a people prepared.'
texts.luk.1.18: And Zacharias said unto the messenger, `Whereby shall I know this? for I am aged, and my wife is advanced in her days?'
texts.luk.1.19: And the messenger answering said to him, `I am Gabriel, who have been standing near before God, and I was sent to speak unto thee, and to proclaim these good news to thee,
texts.luk.1.20: and lo, thou shalt be silent, and not able to speak, till the day that these things shall come to pass, because thou didst not believe my words, that shall be fulfilled in their season.'
texts.luk.1.21: And the people were waiting for Zacharias, and wondering at his tarrying in the sanctuary,
texts.luk.1.22: and having come out, he was not able to speak to them, and they perceived that a vision he had seen in the sanctuary, and he was beckoning to them, and did remain dumb.
texts.luk.1.23: And it came to pass, when the days of his service were fulfilled, he went away to his house,
texts.luk.1.24: and after those days, his wife Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months, saying --
texts.luk.1.25: `Thus hath the Lord done to me, in days in which He looked upon [me], to take away my reproach among men.'
texts.luk.1.26: And in the sixth month was the messenger Gabriel sent by God, to a city of Galilee, the name of which [is] Nazareth,
texts.luk.1.27: to a virgin, betrothed to a man, whose name [is] Joseph, of the house of David, and the name of the virgin [is] Mary.
texts.luk.1.28: And the messenger having come in unto her, said, `Hail, favoured one, the Lord [is] with thee; blessed [art] thou among women;'
texts.luk.1.29: and she, having seen, was troubled at his word, and was reasoning of what kind this salutation may be.
texts.luk.1.30: And the messenger said to her, `Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found favour with God;
texts.luk.1.31: and lo, thou shalt conceive in the womb, and shalt bring forth a son, and call his name Jesus;
texts.luk.1.32: he shall be great, and Son of the Highest he shall be called, and the Lord God shall give him the throne of David his father,
texts.luk.1.33: and he shall reign over the house of Jacob to the ages; and of his reign there shall be no end.'
texts.luk.1.34: And Mary said unto the messenger, `How shall this be, seeing a husband I do not know?'
texts.luk.1.35: And the messenger answering said to her, `The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee, therefore also the holy-begotten thing shall be called Son of God;
texts.luk.1.36: and lo, Elisabeth, thy kinswoman, she also hath conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month to her who was called barren;
texts.luk.1.37: because nothing shall be impossible with God.'
texts.luk.1.38: And Mary said, `Lo, the maid-servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to thy saying,' and the messenger went away from her.
texts.luk.1.39: And Mary having arisen in those days, went to the hill-country, with haste, to a city of Judea,
texts.luk.1.40: and entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elisabeth.
texts.luk.1.41: And it came to pass, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe did leap in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit,
texts.luk.1.42: and spake out with a loud voice, and said, `Blessed [art] thou among women, and blessed [is] the fruit of thy womb;
texts.luk.1.43: and whence [is] this to me, that the mother of my Lord might come unto me?
texts.luk.1.44: for, lo, when the voice of thy salutation came to my ears, leap in gladness did the babe in my womb;
texts.luk.1.45: and happy [is] she who did believe, for there shall be a completion to the things spoken to her from the Lord.'
texts.luk.1.46: And Mary said, `My soul doth magnify the Lord,
texts.luk.1.47: And my spirit was glad on God my Saviour,
texts.luk.1.48: Because He looked on the lowliness of His maid-servant, For, lo, henceforth call me happy shall all the generations,
texts.luk.1.49: For He who is mighty did to me great things, And holy [is] His name,
texts.luk.1.50: And His kindness [is] to generations of generations, To those fearing Him,
texts.luk.1.51: He did powerfully with His arm, He scattered abroad the proud in the thought of their heart,
texts.luk.1.52: He brought down the mighty from thrones, And He exalted the lowly,
texts.luk.1.53: The hungry He did fill with good, And the rich He sent away empty,
texts.luk.1.54: He received again Israel His servant, To remember kindness,
texts.luk.1.55: As He spake unto our fathers, To Abraham and to his seed -- to the age.'
texts.luk.1.56: And Mary remained with her about three months, and turned back to her house.
texts.luk.1.57: And to Elisabeth was the time fulfilled for her bringing forth, and she bare a son,
texts.luk.1.58: and the neighbours and her kindred heard that the Lord was making His kindness great with her, and they were rejoicing with her.
texts.luk.1.59: And it came to pass, on the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child, and they were calling him by the name of his father, Zacharias,
texts.luk.1.60: and his mother answering said, `No, but he shall be called John.'
texts.luk.1.61: And they said unto her -- `There is none among thy kindred who is called by this name,'
texts.luk.1.62: and they were making signs to his father, what he would wish him to be called,
texts.luk.1.63: and having asked for a tablet, he wrote, saying, `John is his name;' and they did all wonder;
texts.luk.1.64: and his mouth was opened presently, and his tongue, and he was speaking, praising God.
texts.luk.1.65: And fear came upon all those dwelling around them, and in all the hill-country of Judea were all these sayings spoken of,
texts.luk.1.66: and all who heard did lay them up in their hearts, saying, `What then shall this child be?' and the hand of the Lord was with him.
texts.luk.1.67: And Zacharias his father was filled with the Holy Spirit, and did prophesy, saying,
texts.luk.1.68: `Blessed [is] the Lord, the God of Israel, Because He did look upon, And wrought redemption for His people,
texts.luk.1.69: And did raise an horn of salvation to us, In the house of David His servant,
texts.luk.1.70: As He spake by the mouth of His holy prophets, Which have been from the age;
texts.luk.1.71: Salvation from our enemies, And out of the hand of all hating us,
texts.luk.1.72: To do kindness with our fathers, And to be mindful of His holy covenant,
texts.luk.1.73: An oath that He sware to Abraham our father,
texts.luk.1.74: To give to us, without fear, Out of the hand of our enemies having been delivered,
texts.luk.1.75: To serve Him, in holiness and righteousness Before Him, all the days of our life.
texts.luk.1.76: And thou, child, Prophet of the Highest Shalt thou be called; For thou shalt go before the face of the Lord, To prepare His ways.
texts.luk.1.77: To give knowledge of salvation to His people In remission of their sins,
texts.luk.1.78: Through the tender mercies of our God, In which the rising from on high did look upon us,
texts.luk.1.79: To give light to those sitting in darkness and death-shade, To guide our feet to a way of peace.'
texts.luk.1.80: And the child grew, and was strengthened in spirit, and he was in the deserts till the day of his shewing unto Israel.
texts.luk.2.1: And it came to pass in those days, there went forth a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world be enrolled --
texts.luk.2.2: this enrollment first came to pass when Cyrenius was governor of Syria --
texts.luk.2.3: and all were going to be enrolled, each to his proper city,
texts.luk.2.4: and Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, that is called Bethlehem, because of his being of the house and family of David,
texts.luk.2.5: to enroll himself with Mary his betrothed wife, being with child.
texts.luk.2.6: And it came to pass, in their being there, the days were fulfilled for her bringing forth,
texts.luk.2.7: and she brought forth her son -- the first-born, and wrapped him up, and laid him down in the manger, because there was not for them a place in the guest-chamber.
texts.luk.2.8: And there were shepherds in the same region, lodging in the field, and keeping the night-watches over their flock,
texts.luk.2.9: and lo, a messenger of the Lord stood over them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they feared a great fear.
texts.luk.2.10: And the messenger said to them, `Fear not, for lo, I bring you good news of great joy, that shall be to all the people --
texts.luk.2.11: because there was born to you to-day a Saviour -- who is Christ the Lord -- in the city of David,
texts.luk.2.12: and this [is] to you the sign: Ye shall find a babe wrapped up, lying in the manger.'
texts.luk.2.13: And suddenly there came with the messenger a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God, and saying,
texts.luk.2.14: `Glory in the highest to God, and upon earth peace, among men -- good will.'
texts.luk.2.15: And it came to pass, when the messengers were gone away from them to the heavens, that the men, the shepherds, said unto one another, `We may go over indeed unto Bethlehem, and see this thing that hath come to pass, that the Lord did make known to us.'
texts.luk.2.16: And they came, having hasted, and found both Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in the manger,
texts.luk.2.17: and having seen, they made known abroad concerning the saying spoken to them concerning the child.
texts.luk.2.18: And all who heard, did wonder concerning the things spoken by the shepherds unto them;
texts.luk.2.19: and Mary was preserving all these things, pondering in her heart;
texts.luk.2.20: and the shepherds turned back, glorifying and praising God, for all those things they heard and saw, as it was spoken unto them.
texts.luk.2.21: And when eight days were fulfilled to circumcise the child, then was his name called Jesus, having been so called by the messenger before his being conceived in the womb.
texts.luk.2.22: And when the days of their purification were fulfilled, according to the law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem, to present to the Lord,
texts.luk.2.23: as it hath been written in the Law of the Lord, -- `Every male opening a womb shall be called holy to the Lord,'
texts.luk.2.24: and to give a sacrifice, according to that said in the Law of the Lord, `A pair of turtle-doves, or two young pigeons.'
texts.luk.2.25: And lo, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name [is] Simeon, and this man is righteous and devout, looking for the comforting of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him,
texts.luk.2.26: and it hath been divinely told him by the Holy Spirit -- not to see death before he may see the Christ of the Lord.
texts.luk.2.27: And he came in the Spirit to the temple, and in the parents bringing in the child Jesus, for their doing according to the custom of the law regarding him,
texts.luk.2.28: then he took him in his arms, and blessed God, and he said,
texts.luk.2.29: `Now Thou dost send away Thy servant, Lord, according to Thy word, in peace,
texts.luk.2.30: because mine eyes did see Thy salvation,
texts.luk.2.31: which Thou didst prepare before the face of all the peoples,
texts.luk.2.32: a light to the uncovering of nations, and the glory of Thy people Israel.'
texts.luk.2.33: And Joseph and his mother were wondering at the things spoken concerning him,
texts.luk.2.34: and Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, `Lo, this [one] is set for the falling and rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign spoken against --
texts.luk.2.35: (and also thine own soul shall a sword pass through) -- that the reasonings of many hearts may be revealed.'
texts.luk.2.36: And there was Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, she was much advanced in days, having lived with an husband seven years from her virginity,
texts.luk.2.37: and she [is] a widow of about eighty-four years, who did depart not from the temple, with fasts and supplications serving, night and day,
texts.luk.2.38: and she, at that hour, having come in, was confessing, likewise, to the Lord, and was speaking concerning him, to all those looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
texts.luk.2.39: And when they finished all things, according to the Law of the Lord, they turned back to Galilee, to their city Nazareth;
texts.luk.2.40: and the child grew and was strengthened in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
texts.luk.2.41: And his parents were going yearly to Jerusalem, at the feast of the passover,
texts.luk.2.42: and when he became twelve years old, they having gone up to Jerusalem, according to the custom of the feast,
texts.luk.2.43: and having finished the days, in their returning the child Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and Joseph and his mother did not know,
texts.luk.2.44: and, having supposed him to be in the company, they went a day's journey, and were seeking him among the kindred and among the acquaintances,
texts.luk.2.45: and not having found him, they turned back to Jerusalem seeking him.
texts.luk.2.46: And it came to pass, after three days, they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both hearing them and questioning them,
texts.luk.2.47: and all those hearing him were astonished at his understanding and answers.
texts.luk.2.48: And, having seen him, they were amazed, and his mother said unto him, `Child, why didst thou thus to us? lo, thy father and I, sorrowing, were seeking thee.'
texts.luk.2.49: And he said unto them, `Why [is it] that ye were seeking me? did ye not know that in the things of my Father it behoveth me to be?'
texts.luk.2.50: and they did not understand the saying that he spake to them,
texts.luk.2.51: and he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and he was subject to them, and his mother was keeping all these sayings in her heart,
texts.luk.2.52: and Jesus was advancing in wisdom, and in stature, and in favour with God and men.
texts.luk.3.1: And in the fifteenth year of the government of Tiberius Caesar -- Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod tetrarch of Galilee, and Philip his brother, tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene --
texts.luk.3.2: Annas and Caiaphas being chief priests -- there came a word of God unto John the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness,
texts.luk.3.3: and he came to all the region round the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of reformation -- to remission of sins,
texts.luk.3.4: as it hath been written in the scroll of the words of Isaiah the prophet, saying, `A voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, straight make ye His paths;
texts.luk.3.5: every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be made low, and the crooked shall become straightness, and the rough become smooth ways;
texts.luk.3.6: and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.'
texts.luk.3.7: Then said he to the multitudes coming forth to be baptised by him, `Brood of vipers! who did prompt you to flee from the coming wrath?
texts.luk.3.8: make, therefore, fruits worthy of the reformation, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have a father -- Abraham; for I say to you, that God is able out of these stones to raise children to Abraham;
texts.luk.3.9: and already also the axe unto the root of the trees is laid, every tree, therefore, not making good fruit is cut down, and to fire it is cast.'
texts.luk.3.10: And the multitudes were questioning him, saying, `What, then, shall we do?'
texts.luk.3.11: and he answering saith to them, `He having two coats -- let him impart to him having none, and he having victuals -- in like manner let him do.'
texts.luk.3.12: And there came also tax-gatherers to be baptised, and they said unto him, `Teacher, what shall we do?'
texts.luk.3.13: and he said unto them, `Exact no more than that directed you.'
texts.luk.3.14: And questioning him also were those warring, saying, `And we, what shall we do?' and he said unto them, `Do violence to no one, nor accuse falsely, and be content with your wages.'
texts.luk.3.15: And the people are looking forward, and all are reasoning in their hearts concerning John, whether or not he may be the Christ;
texts.luk.3.16: John answered, saying to all, `I indeed with water do baptise you, but he cometh who is mightier than I, of whom I am not worthy to loose the latchet of his sandals -- he shall baptise you with the Holy Spirit and with fire;
texts.luk.3.17: whose winnowing shovel [is] in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor, and will gather the wheat to his storehouse, and the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.'
texts.luk.3.18: And, therefore, indeed with many other things, exhorting, he was proclaiming good news to the people,
texts.luk.3.19: and Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him concerning Herodias the wife of Philip his brother, and concerning all the evils that Herod did,
texts.luk.3.20: added also this to all, that he shut up John in the prison.
texts.luk.3.21: And it came to pass, in all the people being baptised, Jesus also being baptised, and praying, the heaven was opened,
texts.luk.3.22: and the Holy Spirit came down in a bodily appearance, as if a dove, upon him, and a voice came out of heaven, saying, `Thou art My Son -- the Beloved, in thee I did delight.'
texts.luk.3.23: And Jesus himself was beginning to be about thirty years of age, being, as was supposed, son of Joseph,
texts.luk.3.24: the [son] of Eli, the [son] of Matthat, the [son] of Levi, the [son] of Melchi, the [son] of Janna, the [son] of Joseph,
texts.luk.3.25: the [son] of Mattathias, the [son] of Amos, the [son] of Naum, the [son] of Esli,
texts.luk.3.26: the [son] of Naggai, the [son] of Maath, the [son] of Mattathias, the [son] of Semei, the [son] of Joseph, the [son] of Juda,
texts.luk.3.27: the [son] of Joanna, the [son] of Rhesa, the [son] of Zerubbabel, the [son] of Shealtiel,
texts.luk.3.28: the [son] of Neri, the [son] of Melchi, the [son] of Addi, the [son] of Cosam, the [son] of Elmodam, the [son] of Er,
texts.luk.3.29: the [son] of Jose, the [son] of Eliezer, the [son] of Jorim, the [son] of Matthat,
texts.luk.3.30: the [son] of Levi, the [son] of Simeon, the [son] of Juda, the [son] of Joseph, the [son] of Jonan, the [son] of Eliakim,
texts.luk.3.31: the [son] of Melea, the [son] of Mainan, the [son] of Mattatha, the [son] of Nathan,
texts.luk.3.32: the [son] of David, the [son] of Jesse, the [son] of Obed, the [son] of Booz, the [son] of Salmon, the [son] of Nahshon,
texts.luk.3.33: the [son] of Amminadab, the [son] of Aram, the [son] of Esrom, the [son] of Pharez,
texts.luk.3.34: the [son] of Judah, the [son] of Jacob, the [son] of Isaac, the [son] of Abraham, the [son] of Terah, the [son] of Nahor,
texts.luk.3.35: the [son] of Serug, the [son] of Reu, the [son] of Peleg, the [son] of Eber,
texts.luk.3.36: the [son] of Salah, the [son] of Cainan, the [son] of Arphaxad, the [son] of Shem, the [son] of Noah, the [son] of Lamech,
texts.luk.3.37: the [son] of Methuselah, the [son] of Enoch, the [son] of Jared, the [son] of Mahalaleel,
texts.luk.3.38: the [son] of Cainan, the [son] of Enos, the [son] of Seth, the [son] of Adam, the [son] of God.
texts.luk.4.1: And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, turned back from the Jordan, and was brought in the Spirit to the wilderness,
texts.luk.4.2: forty days being tempted by the Devil, and he did not eat anything in those days, and they having been ended, he afterward hungered,
texts.luk.4.3: and the Devil said to him, `If Son thou art of God, speak to this stone that it may become bread.'
texts.luk.4.4: And Jesus answered him, saying, `It hath been written, that, not on bread only shall man live, but on every saying of God.'
texts.luk.4.5: And the Devil having brought him up to an high mountain, shewed to him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time,
texts.luk.4.6: and the Devil said to him, `To thee I will give all this authority, and their glory, because to me it hath been delivered, and to whomsoever I will, I do give it;
texts.luk.4.7: thou, then, if thou mayest bow before me -- all shall be thine.'
texts.luk.4.8: And Jesus answering him said, `Get thee behind me, Adversary, for it hath been written, Thou shalt bow before the Lord thy God, and Him only thou shalt serve.'
texts.luk.4.9: And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, `If the Son thou art of God, cast thyself down hence,
texts.luk.4.10: for it hath been written -- To His messengers He will give charge concerning thee, to guard over thee,
texts.luk.4.11: and -- On hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou mayest dash against a stone thy foot.'
texts.luk.4.12: And Jesus answering said to him -- `It hath been said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.'
texts.luk.4.13: And having ended all temptation, the Devil departed from him till a convenient season.
texts.luk.4.14: And Jesus turned back in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and a fame went forth through all the region round about concerning him,
texts.luk.4.15: and he was teaching in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
texts.luk.4.16: And he came to Nazareth, where he hath been brought up, and he went in, according to his custom, on the sabbath-day, to the synagogue, and stood up to read;
texts.luk.4.17: and there was given over to him a roll of Isaiah the prophet, and having unfolded the roll, he found the place where it hath been written:
texts.luk.4.18: `The Spirit of the Lord [is] upon me, Because He did anoint me; To proclaim good news to the poor, Sent me to heal the broken of heart, To proclaim to captives deliverance, And to blind receiving of sight, To send away the bruised with deliverance,
texts.luk.4.19: To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.'
texts.luk.4.20: And having folded the roll, having given [it] back to the officer, he sat down, and the eyes of all in the synagogue were gazing on him.
texts.luk.4.21: And he began to say unto them -- `To-day hath this writing been fulfilled in your ears;'
texts.luk.4.22: and all were bearing testimony to him, and were wondering at the gracious words that are coming forth out of his mouth, and they said, `Is not this the son of Joseph?'
texts.luk.4.23: And he said unto them, `Certainly ye will say to me this simile, Physician, heal thyself; as great things as we heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country;'
texts.luk.4.24: and he said, `Verily I say to you -- No prophet is accepted in his own country;
texts.luk.4.25: and of a truth I say to you, Many widows were in the days of Elijah, in Israel, when the heaven was shut for three years and six months, when great famine came on all the land,
texts.luk.4.26: and unto none of them was Elijah sent, but -- to Sarepta of Sidon, unto a woman, a widow;
