texts.luk.4.27: and many lepers were in the time of Elisha the prophet, in Israel, and none of them was cleansed, but -- Naaman the Syrian.'
texts.luk.4.28: And all in the synagogue were filled with wrath, hearing these things,
texts.luk.4.29: and having risen, they put him forth without the city, and brought him unto the brow of the hill on which their city had been built -- to cast him down headlong,
texts.luk.4.30: and he, having gone through the midst of them, went away.
texts.luk.4.31: And he came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and was teaching them on the sabbaths,
texts.luk.4.32: and they were astonished at his teaching, because his word was with authority.
texts.luk.4.33: And in the synagogue was a man, having a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a great voice,
texts.luk.4.34: saying, `Away, what -- to us and to thee, Jesus, O Nazarene? thou didst come to destroy us; I have known thee who thou art -- the Holy One of God.'
texts.luk.4.35: And Jesus did rebuke him, saying, `Be silenced, and come forth out of him;' and the demon having cast him into the midst, came forth from him, having hurt him nought;
texts.luk.4.36: and amazement came upon all, and they were speaking together, with one another, saying, `What [is] this word, that with authority and power he doth command the unclean spirits, and they come forth?'
texts.luk.4.37: and there was going forth a fame concerning him to every place of the region round about.
texts.luk.4.38: And having risen out of the synagogue, he entered into the house of Simon, and the mother-in-law of Simon was pressed with a great fever, and they did ask him about her,
texts.luk.4.39: and having stood over her, he rebuked the fever, and it left her, and presently, having risen, she was ministering to them.
texts.luk.4.40: And at the setting of the sun, all, as many as had any ailing with manifold sicknesses, brought them unto him, and he on each one of them [his] hands having put, did heal them.
texts.luk.4.41: And demons also were coming forth from many, crying out and saying -- `Thou art the Christ, the Son of God;' and rebuking, he did not suffer them to speak, because they knew him to be the Christ.
texts.luk.4.42: And day having come, having gone forth, he went on to a desert place, and the multitudes were seeking him, and they came unto him, and were staying him -- not to go on from them,
texts.luk.4.43: and he said unto them -- `Also to the other cities it behoveth me to proclaim good news of the reign of God, because for this I have been sent;'
texts.luk.4.44: and he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
texts.luk.5.1: And it came to pass, in the multitude pressing on him to hear the word of God, that he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret,
texts.luk.5.2: and he saw two boats standing beside the lake, and the fishers, having gone away from them, were washing the nets,
texts.luk.5.3: and having entered into one of the boats, that was Simon's, he asked him to put back a little from the land, and having sat down, was teaching the multitudes out of the boat.
texts.luk.5.4: And when he left off speaking, he said unto Simon, `Put back to the deep, and let down your nets for a draught;'
texts.luk.5.5: and Simon answering said to him, `Master, through the whole night, having laboured, we have taken nothing, but at thy saying I will let down the net.'
texts.luk.5.6: And having done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fishes, and their net was breaking,
texts.luk.5.7: and they beckoned to the partners, who [are] in the other boat, having come, to help them; and they came, and filled both the boats, so that they were sinking.
texts.luk.5.8: And Simon Peter having seen, fell down at the knees of Jesus, saying, `Depart from me, because I am a sinful man, O lord;'
texts.luk.5.9: for astonishment seized him, and all those with him, at the draught of the fishes that they took,
texts.luk.5.10: and in like manner also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon; and Jesus said unto Simon, `Fear not, henceforth thou shalt be catching men;'
texts.luk.5.11: and they, having brought the boats upon the land, having left all, did follow him.
texts.luk.5.12: And it came to pass, in his being in one of the cities, that lo, a man full of leprosy, and having seen Jesus, having fallen on [his] face, he besought him, saying, `Sir, if thou mayest will, thou art able to cleanse me;'
texts.luk.5.13: and having stretched forth [his] hand, he touched him, having said, `I will; be thou cleansed;' and immediately the leprosy went away from him.
texts.luk.5.14: And he charged him to tell no one, `But, having gone away, shew thyself to the priest, and bring near for thy cleansing according as Moses directed, for a testimony to them;'
texts.luk.5.15: but the more was the report going abroad concerning him, and great multitudes were coming together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities,
texts.luk.5.16: and he was withdrawing himself in the desert places and was praying.
texts.luk.5.17: And it came to pass, on one of the days, that he was teaching, and there were sitting by Pharisees and teachers of the Law, who were come out of every village of Galilee, and Judea, and Jerusalem, and the power of the Lord was -- to heal them.
texts.luk.5.18: And lo, men bearing upon a couch a man, who hath been struck with palsy, and they were seeking to bring him in, and to place before him,
texts.luk.5.19: and not having found by what way they may bring him in because of the multitude, having gone up on the house-top, through the tiles they let him down, with the little couch, into the midst before Jesus,
texts.luk.5.20: and he having seen their faith, said to him, `Man, thy sins have been forgiven thee.'
texts.luk.5.21: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, `Who is this that doth speak evil words? who is able to forgive sins, except God only?'
texts.luk.5.22: And Jesus having known their reasonings, answering, said unto them, `What reason ye in your hearts?
texts.luk.5.23: which is easier -- to say, Thy sins have been forgiven thee? or to say, Arise, and walk?
texts.luk.5.24: `And that ye may know that the Son of Man hath authority upon the earth to forgive sins -- (he said to the one struck with palsy) -- I say to thee, Arise, and having taken up thy little couch, be going on to thy house.'
texts.luk.5.25: And presently having risen before them, having taken up [that] on which he was lying, he went away to his house, glorifying God,
texts.luk.5.26: and astonishment took all, and they were glorifying God, and were filled with fear, saying -- `We saw strange things to-day.'
texts.luk.5.27: And after these things he went forth, and beheld a tax-gatherer, by name Levi, sitting at the tax-office, and said to him, `Be following me;'
texts.luk.5.28: and he, having left all, having arisen, did follow him.
texts.luk.5.29: And Levi made a great entertainment to him in his house, and there was a great multitude of tax-gatherers and others who were with them reclining (at meat),
texts.luk.5.30: and the scribes and the Pharisees among them were murmuring at his disciples, saying, `Wherefore with tax-gatherers and sinners do ye eat and drink?'
texts.luk.5.31: And Jesus answering said unto them, `They who are well have no need of a physician, but they that are ill:
texts.luk.5.32: I came not to call righteous men, but sinners, to reformation.'
texts.luk.5.33: And they said unto him, `Wherefore do the disciples of John fast often, and make supplications -- in like manner also those of the Pharisees -- but thine do eat and drink?'
texts.luk.5.34: And he said unto them, `Are ye able to make the sons of the bride-chamber -- in the bridegroom being with them -- to fast?
texts.luk.5.35: but days will come, and, when the bridegroom may be taken away from them, then they shall fast in those days.'
texts.luk.5.36: And he spake also a simile unto them -- `No one a patch of new clothing doth put on old clothing, and if otherwise, the new also doth make a rent, and with the old the patch doth not agree, that [is] from the new.
texts.luk.5.37: `And no one doth put new wine into old skins, and if otherwise, the new wine will burst the skins, and itself will be poured out, and the skins will be destroyed;
texts.luk.5.38: but new wine into new skins is to be put, and both are preserved together;
texts.luk.5.39: and no one having drunk old [wine], doth immediately wish new, for he saith, The old is better.'
texts.luk.6.1: And it came to pass, on the second-first sabbath, as he is going through the corn fields, that his disciples were plucking the ears, and were eating, rubbing with the hands,
texts.luk.6.2: and certain of the Pharisees said to them, `Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbaths?'
texts.luk.6.3: And Jesus answering said unto them, `Did ye not read even this that David did, when he hungered, himself and those who are with him,
texts.luk.6.4: how he went into the house of God, and the loaves of the presentation did take, and did eat, and gave also to those with him, which it is not lawful to eat, except only to the priests?'
texts.luk.6.5: and he said to them, -- `The Son of Man is lord also of the sabbath.'
texts.luk.6.6: And it came to pass also, on another sabbath, that he goeth into the synagogue, and teacheth, and there was there a man, and his right hand was withered,
texts.luk.6.7: and the scribes and the Pharisees were watching him, if on the sabbath he will heal, that they might find an accusation against him.
texts.luk.6.8: And he himself had known their reasonings, and said to the man having the withered hand, `Rise, and stand in the midst;' and he having risen, stood.
texts.luk.6.9: Then said Jesus unto them, `I will question you something: Is it lawful on the sabbaths to do good, or to do evil? life to save or to kill?'
texts.luk.6.10: And having looked round on them all, he said to the man, `Stretch forth thy hand;' and he did so, and his hand was restored whole as the other;
texts.luk.6.11: and they were filled with madness, and were speaking with one another what they might do to Jesus.
texts.luk.6.12: And it came to pass in those days, he went forth to the mountain to pray, and was passing the night in the prayer of God,
texts.luk.6.13: and when it became day, he called near his disciples, and having chosen from them twelve, whom also he named apostles,
texts.luk.6.14: (Simon, whom also he named Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
texts.luk.6.15: Matthew and Thomas, James of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes,
texts.luk.6.16: Judas of James, and Judas Iscariot, who also became betrayer;)
texts.luk.6.17: and having come down with them, he stood upon a level spot, and a crowd of his disciples, and a great multitude of the people from all Judea, and Jerusalem, and the maritime Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him, and to be healed of their sicknesses,
texts.luk.6.18: and those harassed by unclean spirits, and they were healed,
texts.luk.6.19: and all the multitude were seeking to touch him, because power from him was going forth, and he was healing all.
texts.luk.6.20: And he, having lifted up his eyes to his disciples, said: `Happy the poor -- because yours is the reign of God.
texts.luk.6.21: `Happy those hungering now -- because ye shall be filled. `Happy those weeping now -- because ye shall laugh.
texts.luk.6.22: `Happy are ye when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you, and shall reproach, and shall cast forth your name as evil, for the Son of Man's sake --
texts.luk.6.23: rejoice in that day, and leap, for lo, your reward [is] great in the heaven, for according to these things were their fathers doing to the prophets.
texts.luk.6.24: `But wo to you -- the rich, because ye have got your comfort.
texts.luk.6.25: `Wo to you who have been filled -- because ye shall hunger. `Wo to you who are laughing now -- because ye shall mourn and weep.
texts.luk.6.26: `Wo to you when all men shall speak well of you -- for according to these things were their fathers doing to false prophets.
texts.luk.6.27: `But I say to you who are hearing, Love your enemies, do good to those hating you,
texts.luk.6.28: bless those cursing you, and pray for those accusing you falsely;
texts.luk.6.29: and to him smiting thee upon the cheek, give also the other, and from him taking away from thee the mantle, also the coat thou mayest not keep back.
texts.luk.6.30: `And to every one who is asking of thee, be giving; and from him who is taking away thy goods, be not asking again;
texts.luk.6.31: and as ye wish that men may do to you, do ye also to them in like manner;
texts.luk.6.32: and -- if ye love those loving you, what grace have ye? for also the sinful love those loving them;
texts.luk.6.33: and if ye do good to those doing good to you, what grace have ye? for also the sinful do the same;
texts.luk.6.34: and if ye lend [to those] of whom ye hope to receive back, what grace have ye? for also the sinful lend to sinners -- that they may receive again as much.
texts.luk.6.35: `But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again, and your reward will be great, and ye shall be sons of the Highest, because He is kind unto the ungracious and evil;
texts.luk.6.36: be ye therefore merciful, as also your Father is merciful.
texts.luk.6.37: `And judge not, and ye may not be judged; condemn not, and ye may not be condemned; release, and ye shall be released.
texts.luk.6.38: `Give, and it shall be given to you; good measure, pressed, and shaken, and running over, they shall give into your bosom; for with that measure with which ye measure, it shall be measured to you again.'
texts.luk.6.39: And he spake a simile to them, `Is blind able to lead blind? shall they not both fall into a pit?
texts.luk.6.40: A disciple is not above his teacher, but every one perfected shall be as his teacher.
texts.luk.6.41: `And why dost thou behold the mote that is in thy brother's eye, and the beam that [is] in thine own eye dost not consider?
texts.luk.6.42: or how art thou able to say to thy brother, Brother, suffer, I may take out the mote that [is] in thine eye -- thyself the beam in thine own eye not beholding? Hypocrite, take first the beam out of thine own eye, and then thou shalt see clearly to take out the mote that [is] in thy brother's eye.
texts.luk.6.43: `For there is not a good tree making bad fruit, nor a bad tree making good fruit;
texts.luk.6.44: for each tree from its own fruit is known, for not from thorns do they gather figs, nor from a bramble do they crop a grape.
texts.luk.6.45: `The good man out of the good treasure of his heart doth bring forth that which [is] good; and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart doth bring forth that which [is] evil; for out of the abounding of the heart doth his mouth speak.
texts.luk.6.46: `And why do ye call me, Lord, Lord, and do not what I say?
texts.luk.6.47: Every one who is coming unto me, and is hearing my words, and is doing them, I will shew you to whom he is like;
texts.luk.6.48: he is like to a man building a house, who did dig, and deepen, and laid a foundation upon the rock, and a flood having come, the stream broke forth on that house, and was not able to shake it, for it had been founded upon the rock.
texts.luk.6.49: `And he who heard and did not, is like to a man having builded a house upon the earth, without a foundation, against which the stream brake forth, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house became great.'
texts.luk.7.1: And when he completed all his sayings in the ears of the people, he went into Capernaum;
texts.luk.7.2: and a certain centurion's servant being ill, was about to die, who was much valued by him,
texts.luk.7.3: and having heard about Jesus, he sent unto him elders of the Jews, beseeching him, that having come he might thoroughly save his servant.
texts.luk.7.4: And they, having come near unto Jesus, were calling upon him earnestly, saying -- `He is worthy to whom thou shalt do this,
texts.luk.7.5: for he doth love our nation, and the synagogue he did build to us.'
texts.luk.7.6: And Jesus was going on with them, and now when he is not far distant from the house the centurion sent unto him friends, saying to him, `Sir, be not troubled, for I am not worthy that under my roof thou mayest enter;
texts.luk.7.7: wherefore not even myself thought I worthy to come unto thee, but say in a word, and my lad shall be healed;
texts.luk.7.8: for I also am a man placed under authority, having under myself soldiers, and I say to this [one], Go, and he goeth; and to another, Be coming, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doth [it].'
texts.luk.7.9: And having heard these things Jesus wondered at him, and having turned to the multitude following him, he said, `I say to you, not even in Israel so much faith did I find;'
texts.luk.7.10: and those sent, having turned back to the house, found the ailing servant in health.
texts.luk.7.11: And it came to pass, on the morrow, he was going on to a city called Nain, and there were going with him many of his disciples, and a great multitude,
texts.luk.7.12: and as he came nigh to the gate of the city, then, lo, one dead was being carried forth, an only son of his mother, and she a widow, and a great multitude of the city was with her.
texts.luk.7.13: And the Lord having seen her, was moved with compassion towards her, and said to her, `Be not weeping;'
texts.luk.7.14: and having come near, he touched the bier, and those bearing [it] stood still, and he said, `Young man, to thee I say, Arise;'
texts.luk.7.15: and the dead sat up, and began to speak, and he gave him to his mother;
texts.luk.7.16: and fear took hold of all, and they were glorifying God, saying -- `A great prophet hath risen among us,' and -- `God did look upon His people.'
texts.luk.7.17: And the account of this went forth in all Judea about him, and in all the region around.
texts.luk.7.18: And the disciples of John told him about all these things,
texts.luk.7.19: and John having called near a certain two of his disciples, sent unto Jesus, saying, `Art thou he who is coming, or for another do we look?'
texts.luk.7.20: And having come near to him, the men said, `John the Baptist sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he who is coming, or for another do we look?'
texts.luk.7.21: And in that hour he cured many from sicknesses, and plagues, and evil spirits, and to many blind he granted sight.
texts.luk.7.22: And Jesus answering said to them, `Having gone on, report to John what ye saw and heard, that blind men do see again, lame do walk, lepers are cleansed, deaf do hear, dead are raised, poor have good news proclaimed;
texts.luk.7.23: and happy is he whoever may not be stumbled in me.'
texts.luk.7.24: And the messengers of John having gone away, he began to say unto the multitudes concerning John: `What have ye gone forth to the wilderness to look on? a reed by the wind shaken?
texts.luk.7.25: but what have ye gone forth to see? a man in soft garments clothed? lo, they in splendid apparellings, and living in luxury, are in the houses of kings!
texts.luk.7.26: `But what have ye gone forth to see? a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and much more than a prophet:
texts.luk.7.27: this is he concerning whom it hath been written, Lo, I send my messenger before thy face, who shall prepare thy way before thee;
texts.luk.7.28: for I say to you, a greater prophet, among those born of women, than John the Baptist there is not; but the least in the reign of God is greater than he.'
texts.luk.7.29: And all the people having heard, and the tax-gatherers, declared God righteous, having been baptized with the baptism of John,
texts.luk.7.30: but the Pharisees, and the lawyers, the counsel of God did put away for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
texts.luk.7.31: And the Lord said, `To what, then, shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?
texts.luk.7.32: they are like to children, to those sitting in a market-place, and calling one to another, and saying, We piped to you, and ye did not dance, we mourned to you, and ye did not weep!
texts.luk.7.33: `For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and ye say, He hath a demon;
texts.luk.7.34: the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and ye say, Lo, a man, a glutton, and a wine drinker, a friend of tax-gatherers and sinners;
texts.luk.7.35: and the wisdom was justified from all her children.'
texts.luk.7.36: And a certain one of the Pharisees was asking him that he might eat with him, and having gone into the house of the Pharisee he reclined (at meat),
texts.luk.7.37: and lo, a woman in the city, who was a sinner, having known that he reclineth (at meat) in the house of the Pharisee, having provided an alabaster box of ointment,
texts.luk.7.38: and having stood behind, beside his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with the tears, and with the hairs of her head she was wiping, and was kissing his feet, and was anointing with the ointment.
texts.luk.7.39: And the Pharisee who did call him, having seen, spake within himself, saying, `This one, if he were a prophet, would have known who and of what kind [is] the woman who doth touch him, that she is a sinner.'
texts.luk.7.40: And Jesus answering said unto him, `Simon, I have something to say to thee;' and he saith, `Teacher, say on.'
texts.luk.7.41: `Two debtors were to a certain creditor; the one was owing five hundred denaries, and the other fifty;
texts.luk.7.42: and they not having [wherewith] to give back, he forgave both; which then of them, say thou, will love him more?'
texts.luk.7.43: And Simon answering said, `I suppose that to whom he forgave the more;' and he said to him, `Rightly thou didst judge.'
texts.luk.7.44: And having turned unto the woman, he said to Simon, `Seest thou this woman? I entered into thy house; water for my feet thou didst not give, but this woman with tears did wet my feet, and with the hairs of her head did wipe;
texts.luk.7.45: a kiss to me thou didst not give, but this woman, from what [time] I came in, did not cease kissing my feet;
texts.luk.7.46: with oil my head thou didst not anoint, but this woman with ointment did anoint my feet;
texts.luk.7.47: therefore I say to thee, her many sins have been forgiven, because she did love much; but to whom little is forgiven, little he doth love.'
texts.luk.7.48: And he said to her, `Thy sins have been forgiven;'
texts.luk.7.49: and those reclining with him (at meat) began to say within themselves, `Who is this, who also doth forgive sins?'
texts.luk.7.50: and he said unto the woman, `Thy faith have saved thee, be going on to peace.'
texts.luk.8.1: And it came to pass thereafter, that he was going through every city and village, preaching and proclaiming good news of the reign of God, and the twelve [are] with him,
texts.luk.8.2: and certain women, who were healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary who is called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone forth,
texts.luk.8.3: and Joanna wife of Chuza, steward of Herod, and Susanna, and many others, who were ministering to him from their substance.
texts.luk.8.4: And a great multitude having gathered, and those who from city and city were coming unto him, he spake by a simile:
texts.luk.8.5: `The sower went forth to sow his seed, and in his sowing some indeed fell beside the way, and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the heaven did devour it.
texts.luk.8.6: `And other fell upon the rock, and having sprung up, it did wither, through not having moisture.
texts.luk.8.7: `And other fell amidst the thorns, and the thorns having sprung up with it, did choke it.
texts.luk.8.8: `And other fell upon the good ground, and having sprung up, it made fruit an hundred fold.' These things saying, he was calling, `He having ears to hear -- let him hear.'
texts.luk.8.9: And his disciples were questioning him, saying, `What may this simile be?'
texts.luk.8.10: And he said, `To you it hath been given to know the secrets of the reign of God, and to the rest in similes; that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
texts.luk.8.11: `And this is the simile: The seed is the word of God,
texts.luk.8.12: and those beside the way are those hearing, then cometh the Devil, and taketh up the word from their heart, lest having believed, they may be saved.
texts.luk.8.13: `And those upon the rock: They who, when they may hear, with joy do receive the word, and these have no root, who for a time believe, and in time of temptation fall away.
texts.luk.8.14: `And that which fell to the thorns: These are they who have heard, and going forth, through anxieties, and riches, and pleasures of life, are choked, and bear not to completion.
texts.luk.8.15: `And that in the good ground: These are they, who in an upright and good heart, having heard the word, do retain [it], and bear fruit in continuance.
texts.luk.8.16: `And no one having lighted a lamp doth cover it with a vessel, or under a couch doth put [it]; but upon a lamp-stand he doth put [it], that those coming in may see the light,
texts.luk.8.17: for nothing is secret, that shall not become manifest, nor hid, that shall not be known, and become manifest.
texts.luk.8.18: `See, therefore, how ye hear, for whoever may have, there shall be given to him, and whoever may not have, also what he seemeth to have, shall be taken from him.'
texts.luk.8.19: And there came unto him his mother and brethren, and they were not able to get to him because of the multitude,
texts.luk.8.20: and it was told him, saying, `Thy mother and thy brethren do stand without, wishing to see thee;'
texts.luk.8.21: and he answering said unto them, `My mother and my brethren! they are those who the word of God are hearing, and doing.'
texts.luk.8.22: And it came to pass, on one of the days, that he himself went into a boat with his disciples, and he said unto them, `We may go over to the other side of the lake;' and they set forth,
texts.luk.8.23: and as they are sailing he fell deeply asleep, and there came down a storm of wind to the lake, and they were filling, and were in peril.
texts.luk.8.24: And having come near, they awoke him, saying, `Master, master, we perish;' and he, having arisen, rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they ceased, and there came a calm,
texts.luk.8.25: and he said to them, `Where is your faith?' and they being afraid did wonder, saying unto one another, `Who, then, is this, that even the winds he doth command, and the water, and they obey him?'
texts.luk.8.26: And they sailed down to the region of the Gadarenes, that is over-against Galilee,
texts.luk.8.27: and he having gone forth upon the land, there met him a certain man, out of the city, who had demons for a long time, and with a garment was not clothed, and in a house was not abiding, but in the tombs,
texts.luk.8.28: and having seen Jesus, and having cried out, he fell before him, and with a loud voice, said, `What -- to me and to thee, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I beseech thee, mayest thou not afflict me!'
texts.luk.8.29: For he commanded the unclean spirit to come forth from the man, for many times it had caught him, and he was being bound with chains and fetters -- guarded, and breaking asunder the bonds he was driven by the demons to the deserts.
texts.luk.8.30: And Jesus questioned him, saying, `What is thy name?' and he said, `Legion,' (because many demons were entered into him,)
texts.luk.8.31: and he was calling on him, that he may not command them to go away to the abyss,
texts.luk.8.32: and there was there a herd of many swine feeding in the mountain, and they were calling on him, that he might suffer them to enter into these, and he suffered them,
texts.luk.8.33: and the demons having gone forth from the man, did enter into the swine, and the herd rushed down the steep to the lake, and were choked.
texts.luk.8.34: And those feeding [them], having seen what was come to pass, fled, and having gone, told [it] to the city, and to the fields;
texts.luk.8.35: and they came forth to see what was come to pass, and they came unto Jesus, and found the man sitting, out of whom the demons had gone forth, clothed, and right-minded, at the feet of Jesus, and they were afraid;
texts.luk.8.36: and those also having seen [it], told them how the demoniac was saved.
texts.luk.8.37: And the whole multitude of the region of the Gadarenes round about asked him to go away from them, because with great fear they were pressed, and he having entered into the boat, did turn back.
texts.luk.8.38: And the man from whom the demons had gone forth was beseeching of him to be with him, and Jesus sent him away, saying,
texts.luk.8.39: `Turn back to thy house, and tell how great things God did to thee;' and he went away through all the city proclaiming how great things Jesus did to him.
texts.luk.8.40: And it came to pass, in the turning back of Jesus, the multitude received him, for they were all looking for him,
texts.luk.8.41: and lo, there came a man, whose name [is] Jairus, and he was a chief of the synagogue, and having fallen at the feet of Jesus, was calling on him to come to his house;
texts.luk.8.42: because he had an only daughter about twelve years [old], and she was dying. And in his going away, the multitudes were thronging him,
texts.luk.8.43: and a woman, having an issue of blood for twelve years, who, having spent on physicians all her living, was not able to be healed by any,
texts.luk.8.44: having come near behind, touched the fringe of his garment, and presently the issue of her blood stood.
texts.luk.8.45: And Jesus said, `Who [is] it that touched me?' and all denying, Peter and those with him said, `Master, the multitudes press thee, and throng [thee], and thou dost say, Who [is] it that touched me!'
texts.luk.8.46: And Jesus said, `Some one did touch me, for I knew power having gone forth from me.'
texts.luk.8.47: And the woman, having seen that she was not hid, trembling, came, and having fallen before him, for what cause she touched him declared to him before all the people, and how she was healed presently;
texts.luk.8.48: and he said to her, `Take courage, daughter, thy faith hath saved thee, be going on to peace.'
texts.luk.8.49: While he is yet speaking, there doth come a certain one from the chief of the synagogue's [house], saying to him -- `Thy daughter hath died, harass not the Teacher;'
texts.luk.8.50: and Jesus having heard, answered him, saying, `Be not afraid, only believe, and she shall be saved.'
texts.luk.8.51: And having come to the house, he suffered no one to go in, except Peter, and James, and John, and the father of the child, and the mother;
texts.luk.8.52: and they were all weeping, and beating themselves for her, and he said, `Weep not, she did not die, but doth sleep;
texts.luk.8.53: and they were deriding him, knowing that she did die;
texts.luk.8.54: and he having put all forth without, and having taken hold of her hand, called, saying, `Child, arise;'
texts.luk.8.55: and her spirit came back, and she arose presently, and he directed that there be given to her to eat;
texts.luk.8.56: and her parents were amazed, but he charged them to say to no one what was come to pass.
texts.luk.9.1: And having called together his twelve disciples, he gave them power and authority over all the demons, and to cure sicknesses,
texts.luk.9.2: and he sent them to proclaim the reign of God, and to heal the ailing.
texts.luk.9.3: And he said unto them, `Take nothing for the way, neither staff, nor scrip, nor bread, nor money; neither have two coats each;
texts.luk.9.4: and into whatever house ye may enter, there remain, and thence depart;
texts.luk.9.5: and as many as may not receive you, going forth from that city, even the dust from your feet shake off, for a testimony against them.'
texts.luk.9.6: And going forth they were going through the several villages, proclaiming good news, and healing everywhere.
texts.luk.9.7: And Herod the tetrarch heard of all the things being done by him, and was perplexed, because it was said by certain, that John hath been raised out of the dead;
texts.luk.9.8: and by certain, that Elijah did appear, and by others, that a prophet, one of the ancients, was risen;
texts.luk.9.9: and Herod said, `John I did behead, but who is this concerning whom I hear such things?' and he was seeking to see him.
texts.luk.9.10: And the apostles having turned back, declared to him how great things they did, and having taken them, he withdrew by himself to a desert place of a city called Bethsaida,
texts.luk.9.11: and the multitudes having known did follow him, and having received them, he was speaking to them concerning the reign of God, and those having need of service he cured.
texts.luk.9.12: And the day began to decline, and the twelve having come near, said to him, `Let away the multitude, that having gone to the villages and the fields round about, they may lodge and may find provision, because here we are in a desert place.'
texts.luk.9.13: And he said unto them, `Give ye them to eat;' and they said, `We have no more than five loaves, and two fishes: except, having gone, we may buy for all this people victuals;'
texts.luk.9.14: for they were about five thousand men. And he said unto his disciples, `Cause them to recline in companies, in each fifty;'
texts.luk.9.15: and they did so, and made all to recline;
texts.luk.9.16: and having taken the five loaves, and the two fishes, having looked up to the heaven, he blessed them, and brake, and was giving to the disciples to set before the multitude;
texts.luk.9.17: and they did eat, and were all filled, and there was taken up what was over to them of broken pieces, twelve baskets.
texts.luk.9.18: And it came to pass, as he is praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he questioned them, saying, `Who do the multitudes say me to be?'
texts.luk.9.19: And they answering said, `John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and others, that a prophet, one of the ancients, was risen;'
texts.luk.9.20: and he said to them, `And ye -- who do ye say me to be?' and Peter answering said, `The Christ of God.'
texts.luk.9.21: And having charged them, he commanded [them] to say this to no one,
texts.luk.9.22: saying -- `It behoveth the Son of Man to suffer many things, and to be rejected by the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and to be killed, and the third day to be raised.'
texts.luk.9.23: And he said unto all, `If any one doth will to come after me, let him disown himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me;
texts.luk.9.24: for whoever may will to save his life, shall lose it, and whoever may lose his life for my sake, he shall save it;
texts.luk.9.25: for what is a man profited, having gained the whole world, and having lost or having forfeited himself?
texts.luk.9.26: `For whoever may be ashamed of me, and of my words, of this one shall the Son of Man be ashamed, when he may come in his glory, and the Father's, and the holy messengers';
texts.luk.9.27: and I say to you, truly, there are certain of those here standing, who shall not taste of death till they may see the reign of God.'
texts.luk.9.28: And it came to pass, after these words, as it were eight days, that having taken Peter, and John, and James, he went up to the mountain to pray,
texts.luk.9.29: and it came to pass, in his praying, the appearance of his face became altered, and his garment white -- sparkling.
texts.luk.9.30: And lo, two men were speaking together with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
texts.luk.9.31: who having appeared in glory, spake of his outgoing that he was about to fulfil in Jerusalem,
texts.luk.9.32: but Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep, and having waked, they saw his glory, and the two men standing with him.
texts.luk.9.33: And it came to pass, in their parting from him, Peter said unto Jesus, `Master, it is good to us to be here; and we may make three booths, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah,' not knowing what he saith:
texts.luk.9.34: and as he was speaking these things, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them, and they feared in their entering into the cloud,
texts.luk.9.35: and a voice came out of the cloud saying, `This is My Son -- the Beloved; hear ye him;'
texts.luk.9.36: and when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone; and they were silent, and declared to no one in those days anything of what they have seen.
texts.luk.9.37: And it came to pass on the next day, they having come down from the mount, there met him a great multitude,
texts.luk.9.38: and lo, a man from the multitude cried out, saying, `Teacher, I beseech thee, look upon my son, because he is my only begotten;
texts.luk.9.39: and lo, a spirit doth take him, and suddenly he doth cry out, and it teareth him, with foaming, and it hardly departeth from him, bruising him,
texts.luk.9.40: and I besought thy disciples that they might cast it out, and they were not able.'
texts.luk.9.41: And Jesus answering said, `O generation, unstedfast and perverse, till when shall I be with you, and suffer you? bring near hither thy son;'
texts.luk.9.42: and as he is yet coming near, the demon rent him, and tore [him] sore, and Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the youth, and gave him back to his father.
texts.luk.9.43: And they were all amazed at the greatness of God, and while all are wondering at all things that Jesus did, he said unto his disciples,
texts.luk.9.44: `Lay ye to your ears these words, for the Son of Man is about to be delivered up to the hands of men.'
texts.luk.9.45: And they were not knowing this saying, and it was veiled from them, that they might not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
texts.luk.9.46: And there entered a reasoning among them, this, Who may be greater of them?
texts.luk.9.47: and Jesus having seen the reasoning of their heart, having taken hold of a child, set him beside himself,
texts.luk.9.48: and said to them, `Whoever may receive this child in my name, doth receive me, and whoever may receive me, doth receive Him who sent me, for he who is least among you all -- he shall be great.'
texts.luk.9.49: And John answering said, `Master, we saw a certain one in thy name casting forth the demons, and we forbade him, because he doth not follow with us;'
texts.luk.9.50: and Jesus said unto him, `Forbid not, for he who is not against us, is for us.'
texts.luk.9.51: And it came to pass, in the completing of the days of his being taken up, that he fixed his face to go on to Jerusalem,
texts.luk.9.52: and he sent messengers before his face, and having gone on, they went into a village of Samaritans, to make ready for him,
texts.luk.9.53: and they did not receive him, because his face was going on to Jerusalem.
texts.luk.9.54: And his disciples James and John having seen, said, `Sir, wilt thou [that] we may command fire to come down from the heaven, and to consume them, as also Elijah did?'
texts.luk.9.55: and having turned, he rebuked them, and said, `Ye have not known of what spirit ye are;
texts.luk.9.56: for the Son of Man did not come to destroy men's lives, but to save;' and they went on to another village.
texts.luk.9.57: And it came to pass, as they are going on in the way, a certain one said unto him, `I will follow thee wherever thou mayest go, sir;'
texts.luk.9.58: and Jesus said to him, `The foxes have holes, and the fowls of the heaven places of rest, but the Son of Man hath not where he may recline the head.'
texts.luk.9.59: And he said unto another, `Be following me;' and he said, `Sir, permit me, having gone away, first to bury my father;'
texts.luk.9.60: and Jesus said to him, `Suffer the dead to bury their own dead, and thou, having gone away, publish the reign of God.'
texts.luk.9.61: And another also said, `I will follow thee, sir, but first permit me to take leave of those in my house;'
texts.luk.9.62: and Jesus said unto him, `No one having put his hand on a plough, and looking back, is fit for the reign of God.'
texts.luk.10.1: And after these things, the Lord did appoint also other seventy, and sent them by twos before his face, to every city and place whither he himself was about to come,
texts.luk.10.2: then said he unto them, `The harvest indeed [is] abundant, but the workmen few; beseech ye then the Lord of the harvest, that He may put forth workmen to His harvest.
texts.luk.10.3: `Go away; lo, I send you forth as lambs in the midst of wolves;
texts.luk.10.4: carry no bag, no scrip, nor sandals; and salute no one on the way;
texts.luk.10.5: and into whatever house ye do enter, first say, Peace to this house;
texts.luk.10.6: and if indeed there may be there the son of peace, rest on it shall your peace; and if not so, upon you it shall turn back.
texts.luk.10.7: `And in that house remain, eating and drinking the things they have, for worthy [is] the workman of his hire; go not from house to house,
texts.luk.10.8: and into whatever city ye enter, and they may receive you, eat the things set before you,
texts.luk.10.9: and heal the ailing in it, and say to them, The reign of God hath come nigh to you.
texts.luk.10.10: `And into whatever city ye do enter, and they may not receive you, having gone forth to its broad places, say,
texts.luk.10.11: And the dust that hath cleaved to us, from your city, we do wipe off against you, but this know ye, that the reign of God hath come nigh to you;
texts.luk.10.12: and I say to you, that for Sodom in that day it shall be more tolerable than for that city.
texts.luk.10.13: `Wo to thee, Chorazin; wo to thee, Bethsaida; for if in Tyre and Sidon had been done the mighty works that were done in you, long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes, they had reformed;
texts.luk.10.14: but for Tyre and Sidon it shall be more tolerable in the judgment than for you.
texts.luk.10.15: `And thou, Capernaum, which unto the heaven wast exalted, unto hades thou shalt be brought down.
texts.luk.10.16: `He who is hearing you, doth hear me; and he who is putting you away, doth put me away; and he who is putting me away, doth put away Him who sent me.'
texts.luk.10.17: And the seventy turned back with joy, saying, `Sir, and the demons are being subjected to us in thy name;'
texts.luk.10.18: and he said to them, `I was beholding the Adversary, as lightning from the heaven having fallen;
texts.luk.10.19: lo, I give to you the authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and on all the power of the enemy, and nothing by any means shall hurt you;
texts.luk.10.20: but, in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subjected to you, but rejoice rather that your names were written in the heavens.'
texts.luk.10.21: In that hour was Jesus glad in the Spirit, and said, `I do confess to thee, Father, Lord of the heaven and of the earth, that Thou didst hide these things from wise men and understanding, and didst reveal them to babes; yes, Father, because so it became good pleasure before Thee.
texts.luk.10.22: `All things were delivered up to me by my Father, and no one doth know who the Son is, except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son, and he to whom the Son may wish to reveal [Him].'
texts.luk.10.23: And having turned unto the disciples, he said, by themselves, `Happy the eyes that are perceiving what ye perceive;
texts.luk.10.24: for I say to you, that many prophets and kings did wish to see what ye perceive, and did not see, and to hear what ye hear, and did not hear.'
texts.luk.10.25: And lo, a certain lawyer stood up, trying him, and saying, `Teacher, what having done, life age-during shall I inherit?'
texts.luk.10.26: And he said unto him, `In the law what hath been written? how dost thou read?'
texts.luk.10.27: And he answering said, `Thou shalt love the Lord thy God out of all thy heart, and out of all thy soul, and out of all thy strength, and out of all thy understanding, and thy neighbour as thyself.'
texts.luk.10.28: And he said to him, `Rightly thou didst answer; this do, and thou shalt live.'
texts.luk.10.29: And he, willing to declare himself righteous, said unto Jesus, `And who is my neighbour?'
texts.luk.10.30: and Jesus having taken up [the word], said, `A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among robbers, and having stripped him and inflicted blows, they went away, leaving [him] half dead.
texts.luk.10.31: `And by a coincidence a certain priest was going down in that way, and having seen him, he passed over on the opposite side;
texts.luk.10.32: and in like manner also, a Levite, having been about the place, having come and seen, passed over on the opposite side.
texts.luk.10.33: `But a certain Samaritan, journeying, came along him, and having seen him, he was moved with compassion,
texts.luk.10.34: and having come near, he bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine, and having lifted him up on his own beast, he brought him to an inn, and was careful of him;
texts.luk.10.35: and on the morrow, going forth, taking out two denaries, he gave to the innkeeper, and said to him, Be careful of him, and whatever thou mayest spend more, I, in my coming again, will give back to thee.
texts.luk.10.36: `Who, then, of these three, seemeth to thee to have become neighbour of him who fell among the robbers?'
texts.luk.10.37: and he said, `He who did the kindness with him,' then Jesus said to him, `Be going on, and thou be doing in like manner.'
texts.luk.10.38: And it came to pass, in their going on, that he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman, by name Martha, did receive him into her house,
texts.luk.10.39: and she had also a sister, called Mary, who also, having seated herself beside the feet of Jesus, was hearing the word,
texts.luk.10.40: and Martha was distracted about much serving, and having stood by him, she said, `Sir, dost thou not care that my sister left me alone to serve? say then to her, that she may partake along with me.'
texts.luk.10.41: And Jesus answering said to her, `Martha, Martha, thou art anxious and disquieted about many things,
texts.luk.10.42: but of one thing there is need, and Mary the good part did choose, that shall not be taken away from her.'
texts.luk.11.1: And it came to pass, in his being in a certain place praying, as he ceased, a certain one of his disciples said unto him, `Sir, teach us to pray, as also John taught his disciples.'
texts.luk.11.2: And he said to them, `When ye may pray, say ye: Our Father who art in the heavens; hallowed be Thy name: Thy reign come; Thy will come to pass, as in heaven also on earth;
texts.luk.11.3: our appointed bread be giving us daily;
texts.luk.11.4: and forgive us our sins, for also we ourselves forgive every one indebted to us; and mayest Thou not bring us into temptation; but do Thou deliver us from the evil.'
texts.luk.11.5: And he said unto them, `Who of you shall have a friend, and shall go on unto him at midnight, and may say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves,
texts.luk.11.6: seeing a friend of mine came out of the way unto me, and I have not what I shall set before him,
texts.luk.11.7: and he from within answering may say, Do not give me trouble, already the door hath been shut, and my children with me are in the bed, I am not able, having risen, to give to thee.
texts.luk.11.8: `I say to you, even if he will not give to him, having risen, because of his being his friend, yet because of his importunity, having risen, he will give him as many as he doth need;
texts.luk.11.9: and I say to you, Ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you;
texts.luk.11.10: for every one who is asking doth receive; and he who is seeking doth find; and to him who is knocking it shall be opened.
texts.luk.11.11: `And of which of you -- the father -- if the son shall ask a loaf, a stone will he present to him? and if a fish, will he instead of a fish, a serpent present to him?
texts.luk.11.12: and if he may ask an egg, will he present to him a scorpion?
texts.luk.11.13: If, then, ye, being evil, have known good gifts to be giving to your children, how much more shall the Father who is from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those asking Him!'
texts.luk.11.14: And he was casting forth a demon, and it was dumb, and it came to pass, the demon having gone forth, the dumb man spake, and the multitudes wondered,
texts.luk.11.15: and certain of them said, `By Beelzeboul, ruler of the demons, he doth cast forth the demons;'
texts.luk.11.16: and others, tempting, a sign out of heaven from him were asking.
texts.luk.11.17: And he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, `Every kingdom having been divided against itself is desolated; and house against house doth fall;
texts.luk.11.18: and if also the Adversary against himself was divided, how shall his kingdom be made to stand? for ye say, by Beelzeboul is my casting forth the demons.
texts.luk.11.19: `But if I by Beelzeboul cast forth the demons -- your sons, by whom do they cast forth? because of this your judges they shall be;
texts.luk.11.20: but if by the finger of God I cast forth the demons, then come unawares upon you did the reign of God.
texts.luk.11.21: `When the strong man armed may keep his hall, in peace are his goods;
texts.luk.11.22: but when the stronger than he, having come upon [him], may overcome him, his whole-armour he doth take away in which he had trusted, and his spoils he distributeth;
texts.luk.11.23: he who is not with me is against me, and he who is not gathering with me doth scatter.
texts.luk.11.24: `When the unclean spirit may go forth from the man it walketh through waterless places seeking rest, and not finding, it saith, I will turn back to my house whence I came forth;
texts.luk.11.25: and having come, it findeth [it] swept and adorned;
texts.luk.11.26: then doth it go, and take to it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having entered, they dwell there, and the last of that man becometh worst than the first.'
texts.luk.11.27: And it came to pass, in his saying these things, a certain woman having lifted up the voice out of the multitude, said to him, `Happy the womb that carried thee, and the paps that thou didst suck!'
texts.luk.11.28: And he said, `Yea, rather, happy those hearing the word of God, and keeping [it]!'
texts.luk.11.29: And the multitudes crowding together upon him, he began to say, `This generation is evil, a sign it doth seek after, and a sign shall not be given to it, except the sign of Jonah the prophet,
texts.luk.11.30: for as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also shall the Son of Man be to this generation.
texts.luk.11.31: `A queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and shall condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and lo, greater than Solomon here!
texts.luk.11.32: `Men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it, because they reformed at the proclamation of Jonah; and lo, greater than Jonah here!
texts.luk.11.33: `And no one having lighted a lamp, doth put [it] in a secret place, nor under the measure, but on the lamp-stand, that those coming in may behold the light.
texts.luk.11.34: `The lamp of the body is the eye, when then thine eye may be simple, thy whole body also is lightened; and when it may be evil, thy body also is darkened;
texts.luk.11.35: take heed, then, lest the light that [is] in thee be darkness;
texts.luk.11.36: if then thy whole body is lightened, not having any part darkened, the whole shall be lightened, as when the lamp by the brightness may give thee light.'
texts.luk.11.37: And in [his] speaking, a certain Pharisee was asking him that he might dine with him, and having gone in, he reclined (at meat),
texts.luk.11.38: and the Pharisee having seen, did wonder that he did not first baptize himself before the dinner.
texts.luk.11.39: And the Lord said unto him, `Now do ye, the Pharisees, the outside of the cup and of the plate make clean, but your inward part is full of rapine and wickedness;
texts.luk.11.40: unthinking! did not He who made the outside also the inside make?
texts.luk.11.41: But what ye have give ye [as] alms, and, lo, all things are clean to you.
texts.luk.11.42: `But wo to you, the Pharisees, because ye tithe the mint, and the rue, and every herb, and ye pass by the judgment, and the love of God; these things it behoveth to do, and those not to be neglecting.
texts.luk.11.43: `Wo to you, the Pharisees, because ye love the first seats in the synagogues, and the salutations in the market-places.
texts.luk.11.44: `Wo to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because ye are as the unseen tombs, and the men walking above have not known.'
texts.luk.11.45: And one of the lawyers answering, saith to him, `Teacher, these things saying, us also thou dost insult;'
texts.luk.11.46: and he said, `And to you, the lawyers, wo! because ye burden men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves with one of your fingers do not touch the burdens.
texts.luk.11.47: `Wo to you, because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
texts.luk.11.48: Then do ye testify, and are well pleased with the works of your fathers, because they indeed killed them, and ye do build their tombs;
texts.luk.11.49: because of this also the wisdom of God said: I will send to them prophets, and apostles, and some of them they shall kill and persecute,
texts.luk.11.50: that the blood of all the prophets, that is being poured forth from the foundation of the world, may be required from this generation;
texts.luk.11.51: from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, who perished between the altar and the house; yes, I say to you, It shall be required from this generation.
texts.luk.11.52: `Wo to you, the lawyers, because ye took away the key of the knowledge; yourselves ye did not enter; and those coming in, ye did hinder.'
texts.luk.11.53: And in his speaking these things unto them, the scribes and the Pharisees began fearfully to urge and to press him to speak about many things,
texts.luk.11.54: laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him.
texts.luk.12.1: At which time the myriads of the multitude having been gathered together, so as to tread upon one another, he began to say unto his disciples, first, `Take heed to yourselves of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy;
texts.luk.12.2: and there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known;
texts.luk.12.3: because whatever in the darkness ye said, in the light shall be heard: and what to the ear ye spake in the inner-chambers, shall be proclaimed upon the house-tops.
texts.luk.12.4: `And I say to you, my friends, be not afraid of those killing the body, and after these things are not having anything over to do;
texts.luk.12.5: but I will show to you, whom ye may fear; Fear him who, after the killing, is having authority to cast to the gehenna; yes, I say to you, Fear ye Him.
texts.luk.12.6: `Are not five sparrows sold for two assars? and one of them is not forgotten before God,
texts.luk.12.7: but even the hairs of your head have been all numbered; therefore fear ye not, than many sparrows ye are of more value.
texts.luk.12.8: `And I say to you, Every one -- whoever may confess with me before men, the Son of Man also shall confess with him before the messengers of God,
texts.luk.12.9: and he who hath denied me before men, shall be denied before the messengers of God,
texts.luk.12.10: and every one whoever shall say a word to the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven to him, but to him who to the Holy Spirit did speak evil, it shall not be forgiven.
texts.luk.12.11: `And when they bring you before the synagogues, and the rulers, and the authorities, be not anxious how or what ye may reply, or what ye may say,
texts.luk.12.12: for the Holy Spirit shall teach you in that hour what it behoveth [you] to say.'
texts.luk.12.13: And a certain one said to him, out of the multitude, `Teacher, say to my brother to divide with me the inheritance.'
texts.luk.12.14: And he said to him, `Man, who set me a judge or a divider over you?'
texts.luk.12.15: And he said unto them, `Observe, and beware of the covetousness, because not in the abundance of one's goods is his life.'
texts.luk.12.16: And he spake a simile unto them, saying, `Of a certain rich man the field brought forth well;
texts.luk.12.17: and he was reasoning within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have not where I shall gather together my fruits?
texts.luk.12.18: and he said, This I will do, I will take down my storehouses, and greater ones I will build, and I will gather together there all my products and my good things,
texts.luk.12.19: and I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast many good things laid up for many years, be resting, eat, drink, be merry.
texts.luk.12.20: `And God said to him, Unthinking one! this night thy soul they shall require from thee, and what things thou didst prepare -- to whom shall they be?
texts.luk.12.21: so [is] he who is treasuring up to himself, and is not rich toward God.'
texts.luk.12.22: And he said unto his disciples, `Because of this, to you I say, Be not anxious for your life, what ye may eat; nor for the body, what ye may put on;
texts.luk.12.23: the life is more than the nourishment, and the body than the clothing.
texts.luk.12.24: `Consider the ravens, that they sow not, nor reap, to which there is no barn nor storehouse, and God doth nourish them; how much better are ye than the fowls?
texts.luk.12.25: and who of you, being anxious, is able to add to his age one cubit?
texts.luk.12.26: If, then, ye are not able for the least -- why for the rest are ye anxious?
texts.luk.12.27: `Consider the lilies, how do they grow? they labour not, nor do they spin, and I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed as one of these;
texts.luk.12.28: and if the herbage in the field, that to-day is, and to-morrow into an oven is cast, God doth so clothe, how much more you -- ye of little faith?
texts.luk.12.29: `And ye -- seek not what ye may eat, or what ye may drink, and be not in suspense,
texts.luk.12.30: for all these things do the nations of the world seek after, and your Father hath known that ye have need of these things;
texts.luk.12.31: but, seek ye the reign of God, and all these things shall be added to you.
texts.luk.12.32: `Fear not, little flock, because your Father did delight to give you the reign;
texts.luk.12.33: sell your goods, and give alms, make to yourselves bags that become not old, a treasure unfailing in the heavens, where thief doth not come near, nor moth destroy;
texts.luk.12.34: for where your treasure is, there also your heart will be.
texts.luk.12.35: `Let your loins be girded, and the lamps burning,
texts.luk.12.36: and ye like to men waiting for their lord, when he shall return out of the wedding feasts, that he having come and knocked, immediately they may open to him.
texts.luk.12.37: `Happy those servants, whom the lord, having come, shall find watching; verily I say to you, that he will gird himself, and will cause them to recline (at meat), and having come near, will minister to them;
texts.luk.12.38: and if he may come in the second watch, and in the third watch he may come, and may find [it] so, happy are those servants.
texts.luk.12.39: `And this know, that if the master of the house had known what hour the thief doth come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken through;
texts.luk.12.40: and ye, then, become ye ready, because at the hour ye think not, the Son of Man doth come.'
texts.luk.12.41: And Peter said to him, `Sir, unto us this simile dost thou speak, or also unto all?'
texts.luk.12.42: And the Lord said, `Who, then, is the faithful and prudent steward whom the lord shall set over his household, to give in season the wheat measure?
texts.luk.12.43: Happy that servant, whom his lord, having come, shall find doing so;
texts.luk.12.44: truly I say to you, that over all his goods he will set him.
texts.luk.12.45: `And if that servant may say in his heart, My lord doth delay to come, and may begin to beat the men-servants and the maid-servants, to eat also, and to drink, and to be drunken;
texts.luk.12.46: the lord of that servant will come in a day in which he doth not look for [him], and in an hour that he doth not know, and will cut him off, and his portion with the unfaithful he will appoint.
texts.luk.12.47: `And that servant, who having known his lord's will, and not having prepared, nor having gone according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes,
texts.luk.12.48: and he who, not having known, and having done things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few; and to every one to whom much was given, much shall be required from him; and to whom they did commit much, more abundantly they will ask of him.
texts.luk.12.49: `Fire I came to cast to the earth, and what will I if already it was kindled?
texts.luk.12.50: but I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how am I pressed till it may be completed!
texts.luk.12.51: `Think ye that peace I came to give in the earth? no, I say to you, but rather division;
texts.luk.12.52: for there shall be henceforth five in one house divided -- three against two, and two against three;
texts.luk.12.53: a father shall be divided against a son, and a son against a father, a mother against a daughter, and a daughter against a mother, a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.'
texts.luk.12.54: And he said also to the multitudes, `When ye may see the cloud rising from the west, immediately ye say, A shower doth come, and it is so;
texts.luk.12.55: and when -- a south wind blowing, ye say, that there will be heat, and it is;
texts.luk.12.56: hypocrites! the face of the earth and of the heaven ye have known to make proof of, but this time -- how do ye not make proof of [it]?
texts.luk.12.57: `And why, also, of yourselves, judge ye not what is righteous?
texts.luk.12.58: for, as thou art going away with thy opponent to the ruler, in the way give diligence to be released from him, lest he may drag thee unto the judge, and the judge may deliver thee to the officer, and the officer may cast thee into prison;
texts.luk.12.59: I say to thee, thou mayest not come forth thence till even the last mite thou mayest give back.'
texts.luk.13.1: And there were present certain at that time, telling him about the Galileans, whose blood Pilate did mingle with their sacrifices;
texts.luk.13.2: and Jesus answering said to them, `Think ye that these Galileans became sinners beyond all the Galileans, because they have suffered such things?
texts.luk.13.3: No -- I say to you, but, if ye may not reform, all ye even so shall perish.
texts.luk.13.4: `Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them; think ye that these became debtors beyond all men who are dwelling in Jerusalem?
texts.luk.13.5: No -- I say to you, but, if ye may not reform, all ye in like manner shall perish.'
texts.luk.13.6: And he spake this simile: `A certain one had a fig-tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit in it, and he did not find;
texts.luk.13.7: and he said unto the vine-dresser, Lo, three years I come seeking fruit in this fig-tree, and do not find, cut it off, why also the ground doth it render useless?
texts.luk.13.8: `And he answering saith to him, Sir, suffer it also this year, till that I may dig about it, and cast in dung;
texts.luk.13.9: and if indeed it may bear fruit --; and if not so, thereafter thou shalt cut it off.'
texts.luk.13.10: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath,
texts.luk.13.11: and lo, there was a woman having a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and she was bowed together, and not able to bend back at all,
texts.luk.13.12: and Jesus having seen her, did call [her] near, and said to her, `Woman, thou hast been loosed from thy infirmity;'
texts.luk.13.13: and he laid on her [his] hands, and presently she was set upright, and was glorifying God.
texts.luk.13.14: And the chief of the synagogue answering -- much displeased that on the sabbath Jesus healed -- said to the multitude, `Six days there are in which it behoveth [us] to be working; in these, then, coming, be healed, and not on the sabbath-day.'
texts.luk.13.15: Then the Lord answered him and said, `Hypocrite, doth not each of you on the sabbath loose his ox or ass from the stall, and having led away, doth water [it]?
texts.luk.13.16: and this one, being a daughter of Abraham, whom the Adversary bound, lo, eighteen years, did it not behove to be loosed from this bond on the sabbath-day?'
texts.luk.13.17: And he saying these things, all who were opposed to him were being ashamed, and all the multitude were rejoicing over all the glorious things that are being done by him.
texts.luk.13.18: And he said, `To what is the reign of God like? and to what shall I liken it?
texts.luk.13.19: It is like to a grain of mustard, which a man having taken, did cast into his garden, and it increased, and came to a great tree, and the fowls of the heavens did rest in its branches.'
texts.luk.13.20: And again he said, `To what shall I liken the reign of God?
texts.luk.13.21: It is like leaven, which a woman, having taken, did hide in three measures of meal, till that all was leavened.'
texts.luk.13.22: And he was going through cities and villages, teaching, and making progress toward Jerusalem;
texts.luk.13.23: and a certain one said to him, `Sir, are those saved few?' and he said unto them,
texts.luk.13.24: `Be striving to go in through the straight gate, because many, I say to you, will seek to go in, and shall not be able;
texts.luk.13.25: from the time the master of the house may have risen up, and may have shut the door, and ye may begin without to stand, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, lord, open to us, and he answering shall say to you, I have not known you whence ye are,
texts.luk.13.26: then ye may begin to say, We did eat before thee, and did drink, and in our broad places thou didst teach;
texts.luk.13.27: and he shall say, I say to you, I have not known you whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of the unrighteousness.
texts.luk.13.28: `There shall be there the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth, when ye may see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the reign of God, and yourselves being cast out without;
texts.luk.13.29: and they shall come from east and west, and from north and south, and shall recline in the reign of God,
texts.luk.13.30: and lo, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who shall be last.'
texts.luk.13.31: On that day there came near certain Pharisees, saying to him, `Go forth, and be going on hence, for Herod doth wish to kill thee;'
texts.luk.13.32: and he said to them, `Having gone, say to this fox, Lo, I cast forth demons, and perfect cures to-day and to-morrow, and the third [day] I am being perfected;
texts.luk.13.33: but it behoveth me to-day, and to-morrow, and the [day] following, to go on, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish out of Jerusalem.
texts.luk.13.34: `Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that is killing the prophets, and stoning those sent unto her, how often did I will to gather together thy children, as a hen her brood under the wings, and ye did not will.
texts.luk.13.35: `Lo, your house is being left to you desolate, and verily I say to you -- ye may not see me, till it may come, when ye may say, Blessed [is] he who is coming in the name of the Lord.'
texts.luk.14.1: And it came to pass, on his going into the house of a certain one of the chiefs of the Pharisees, on a sabbath, to eat bread, that they were watching him,
texts.luk.14.2: and lo, there was a certain dropsical man before him;
texts.luk.14.3: and Jesus answering spake to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, `Is it lawful on the sabbath-day to heal?'
texts.luk.14.4: and they were silent, and having taken hold of [him], he healed him, and let [him] go;
texts.luk.14.5: and answering them he said, `Of which of you shall an ass or ox fall into a pit, and he will not immediately draw it up on the sabbath-day?'
texts.luk.14.6: and they were not able to answer him again unto these things.
texts.luk.14.7: And he spake a simile unto those called, marking how they were choosing out the first couches, saying unto them,
texts.luk.14.8: `When thou mayest be called by any one to marriage-feasts, thou mayest not recline on the first couch, lest a more honourable than thou may have been called by him,
texts.luk.14.9: and he who did call thee and him having come shall say to thee, Give to this one place, and then thou mayest begin with shame to occupy the last place.
texts.luk.14.10: `But, when thou mayest be called, having gone on, recline in the last place, that when he who called thee may come, he may say to thee, Friend, come up higher; then thou shalt have glory before those reclining with thee;
texts.luk.14.11: because every one who is exalting himself shall be humbled, and he who is humbling himself shall be exalted.'
texts.luk.14.12: And he said also to him who did call him, `When thou mayest make a dinner or a supper, be not calling thy friends, nor thy brethren, nor thy kindred, nor rich neighbours, lest they may also call thee again, and a recompense may come to thee;
texts.luk.14.13: but when thou mayest make a feast, be calling poor, maimed, lame, blind,
texts.luk.14.14: and happy thou shalt be, because they have not to recompense thee, for it shall be recompensed to thee in the rising again of the righteous.'
texts.luk.14.15: And one of those reclining with him, having heard these things, said to him, `Happy [is] he who shall eat bread in the reign of God;'
texts.luk.14.16: and he said to him, `A certain man made a great supper, and called many,
texts.luk.14.17: and he sent his servant at the hour of the supper to say to those having been called, Be coming, because now are all things ready.
texts.luk.14.18: `And they began with one consent all to excuse themselves: The first said to him, A field I bought, and I have need to go forth and see it; I beg of thee, have me excused.
texts.luk.14.19: `And another said, Five yoke of oxen I bought, and I go on to prove them; I beg of thee, have me excused:
texts.luk.14.20: and another said, A wife I married, and because of this I am not able to come.
texts.luk.14.21: `And that servant having come, told to his lord these things, then the master of the house, having been angry, said to his servant, Go forth quickly to the broad places and lanes of the city, and the poor, and maimed, and lame, and blind, bring in hither.
texts.luk.14.22: `And the servant said, Sir, it hath been done as thou didst command, and still there is room.
texts.luk.14.23: `And the lord said unto the servant, Go forth to the ways and hedges, and constrain to come in, that my house may be filled;
texts.luk.14.24: for I say to you, that none of those men who have been called shall taste of my supper.'
texts.luk.14.25: And there were going on with him great multitudes, and having turned, he said unto them,
texts.luk.14.26: `If any one doth come unto me, and doth not hate his own father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and yet even his own life, he is not able to be my disciple;
texts.luk.14.27: and whoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, is not able to be my disciple.
texts.luk.14.28: `For who of you, willing to build a tower, doth not first, having sat down, count the expense, whether he have the things for completing?
texts.luk.14.29: lest that he having laid a foundation, and not being able to finish, all who are beholding may begin to mock him,
texts.luk.14.30: saying -- This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
texts.luk.14.31: `Or what king going on to engage with another king in war, doth not, having sat down, first consult if he be able with ten thousand to meet him who with twenty thousand is coming against him?
texts.luk.14.32: and if not so -- he being yet a long way off -- having sent an embassy, he doth ask the things for peace.
texts.luk.14.33: `So, then, every one of you who doth not take leave of all that he himself hath, is not able to be my disciple.
texts.luk.14.34: `The salt [is] good, but if the salt doth become tasteless, with what shall it be seasoned?
texts.luk.14.35: neither for land nor for manure is it fit -- they cast it without. He who is having ears to hear -- let him hear.'
texts.luk.15.1: And all the tax-gatherers and the sinners were coming nigh to him, to hear him,
texts.luk.15.2: and the Pharisees and the scribes were murmuring, saying -- This one doth receive sinners, and doth eat with them.'
texts.luk.15.3: And he spake unto them this simile, saying,
texts.luk.15.4: `What man of you having a hundred sheep, and having lost one out of them, doth not leave behind the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go on after the lost one, till he may find it?
texts.luk.15.5: and having found, he doth lay [it] on his shoulders rejoicing,
texts.luk.15.6: and having come to the house, he doth call together the friends and the neighbours, saying to them, Rejoice with me, because I found my sheep -- the lost one.
texts.luk.15.7: `I say to you, that so joy shall be in the heaven over one sinner reforming, rather than over ninety-nine righteous men, who have no need of reformation.
texts.luk.15.8: `Or what woman having ten drachms, if she may lose one drachm, doth not light a lamp, and sweep the house, and seek carefully till that she may find?
texts.luk.15.9: and having found, she doth call together the female friends and the neighbours, saying, Rejoice with me, for I found the drachm that I lost.
texts.luk.15.10: `So I say to you, joy doth come before the messengers of God over one sinner reforming.'
texts.luk.15.11: And he said, `A certain man had two sons,
texts.luk.15.12: and the younger of them said to the father, Father, give me the portion of the substance falling to [me], and he divided to them the living.
texts.luk.15.13: `And not many days after, having gathered all together, the younger son went abroad to a far country, and there he scattered his substance, living riotously;
texts.luk.15.14: and he having spent all, there came a mighty famine on that country, and himself began to be in want;
texts.luk.15.15: and having gone on, he joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him to the fields to feed swine,
texts.luk.15.16: and he was desirous to fill his belly from the husks that the swine were eating, and no one was giving to him.
texts.luk.15.17: `And having come to himself, he said, How many hirelings of my father have a superabundance of bread, and I here with hunger am perishing!
texts.luk.15.18: having risen, I will go on unto my father, and will say to him, Father, I did sin -- to the heaven, and before thee,
texts.luk.15.19: and no more am I worthy to be called thy son; make me as one of thy hirelings.
texts.luk.15.20: `And having risen, he went unto his own father, and he being yet far distant, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and having ran he fell upon his neck and kissed him;
texts.luk.15.21: and the son said to him, Father, I did sin -- to the heaven, and before thee, and no more am I worthy to be called thy son.
texts.luk.15.22: `And the father said unto his servants, Bring forth the first robe, and clothe him, and give a ring for his hand, and sandals for the feet;
texts.luk.15.23: and having brought the fatted calf, kill [it], and having eaten, we may be merry,
texts.luk.15.24: because this my son was dead, and did live again, and he was lost, and was found; and they began to be merry.
texts.luk.15.25: `And his elder son was in a field, and as, coming, he drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing,
texts.luk.15.26: and having called near one of the young men, he was inquiring what these things might be,
texts.luk.15.27: and he said to him -- Thy brother is arrived, and thy father did kill the fatted calf, because in health he did receive him back.
texts.luk.15.28: `And he was angry, and would not go in, therefore his father, having come forth, was entreating him;
texts.luk.15.29: and he answering said to the father, Lo, so many years I do serve thee, and never thy command did I transgress, and to me thou didst never give a kid, that with my friends I might make merry;
texts.luk.15.30: but when thy son -- this one who did devour thy living with harlots -- came, thou didst kill to him the fatted calf.
texts.luk.15.31: `And he said to him, Child, thou art always with me, and all my things are thine;
texts.luk.15.32: but to be merry, and to be glad, it was needful, because this thy brother was dead, and did live again, he was lost, and was found.'
texts.luk.16.1: And he said also unto his disciples, `A certain man was rich, who had a steward, and he was accused to him as scattering his goods;
texts.luk.16.2: and having called him, he said to him, What [is] this I hear about thee? render the account of thy stewardship, for thou mayest not any longer be steward.
texts.luk.16.3: `And the steward said in himself, What shall I do, because my lord doth take away the stewardship from me? to dig I am not able, to beg I am ashamed: --
texts.luk.16.4: I have known what I shall do, that, when I may be removed from the stewardship, they may receive me to their houses.
texts.luk.16.5: `And having called near each one of his lord's debtors, he said to the first, How much dost thou owe to my lord?
texts.luk.16.6: and he said, A hundred baths of oil; and he said to him, Take thy bill, and having sat down write fifty.
texts.luk.16.7: `Afterward to another he said, And thou, how much dost thou owe? and he said, A hundred cors of wheat; and he saith to him, Take thy bill, and write eighty.
texts.luk.16.8: `And the lord commended the unrighteous steward that he did prudently, because the sons of this age are more prudent than the sons of the light, in respect to their generation.
texts.luk.16.9: and I say to you, Make to yourselves friends out of the mammon of unrighteousness, that when ye may fail, they may receive you to the age-during tabernacles.
texts.luk.16.10: `He who is faithful in the least, [is] also faithful in much; and he who in the least [is] unrighteous, is also unrighteous in much;
texts.luk.16.11: if, then, in the unrighteous mammon ye became not faithful -- the true who will entrust to you?
texts.luk.16.12: and if in the other's ye became not faithful -- your own, who shall give to you?
texts.luk.16.13: `No domestic is able to serve two lords, for either the one he will hate, and the other he will love; or one he will hold to, and of the other he will be heedless; ye are not able to serve God and mammon.'
texts.luk.16.14: And also the Pharisees, being lovers of money, were hearing all these things, and were deriding him,
texts.luk.16.15: and he said to them, `Ye are those declaring yourselves righteous before men, but God doth know your hearts; because that which among men is high, [is] abomination before God;
texts.luk.16.16: the law and the prophets [are] till John; since then the reign of God is proclaimed good news, and every one doth press into it;
texts.luk.16.17: and it is easier to the heaven and the earth to pass away, than of the law one tittle to fall.
texts.luk.16.18: `Every one who is sending away his wife, and marrying another, doth commit adultery; and every one who is marrying her sent away from a husband doth commit adultery.
