texts.luk.7.19: And, calling unto him certain two of his disciples, John sent unto the Lord, saying—Art, thou, the Coming One, or, a different one, are we to expect?
texts.luk.7.20: And, coming near unto him, the men said—John the Immerser, hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art, thou, the Coming One, or, another, are we to expect?
texts.luk.7.21: In that very hour, he cured many from diseases, and plagues, and wicked spirits; and, unto many blind, gave he the favour to see.
texts.luk.7.22: And, answering, he said unto them—Go and bear tidings unto John, as to what ye have seen and heard: The blind, are receiving sight, the lame, walk, lepers, are cleansed, and, the deaf, hear, the dead, are raised, the destitute, are told the glad-message;
texts.luk.7.23: And, happy, is he, whosoever shall not find occasion of stumbling in me!
texts.luk.7.24: And, the messengers of John having departed, he began to say unto the multitudes, concerning John—What went ye forth into the desert to gaze at? A reed, by a wind, shaken?
texts.luk.7.25: But what went ye forth to see? A man, in soft garments, arrayed? Lo! they who in splendid apparel and luxury are found, are, in the kingly courts.
texts.luk.7.26: But what went ye forth to see? A prophet? Yea! I say unto you,—and abundantly more than a prophet.
texts.luk.7.27: This, is he concerning whom it is written—Lo! I am sending forth my messenger before thy face, who shall prepare thy way before thee.
texts.luk.7.28: I say unto you—A greater, among them that are born of women, than John, is there none; but, he that is least in the kingdom of God, is greater than he.
texts.luk.7.29: And, all the people, when they heard, and the tax-collectors, justified God, having been immersed with the immersion of John;
texts.luk.7.30: but, the Pharisees and the lawyers, had set aside, the counsel of God against themselves, not being immersed by him.
texts.luk.7.31: Unto what, then, shall I liken the men of this generation? And unto what are they like?
texts.luk.7.32: They are like unto the children sitting, in a market-place, and calling one to another, who say—We played the flute for you, and ye danced not, We wailed, and ye wept not.
texts.luk.7.33: For John the Immerser hath come, neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and ye say—A demon, he hath:
texts.luk.7.34: The Son of Man hath come, eating and drinking, and ye say—Lo! a man, gluttonous and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax-collectors and sinners.
texts.luk.7.35: And yet wisdom hath been justified by all her children.
texts.luk.7.36: And a certain one of the Pharisees was requesting him, that he would eat with him; and, entering into the house of the Pharisee, he reclined.
texts.luk.7.37: And, lo! a woman, who indeed was in the city a sinner; and, when she found out that he was reclining in the house of the Pharisee, providing an alabaster-jar of perfume,
texts.luk.7.38: and standing behind, near his feet, weeping, with the tears, began she to be wetting his feet, and, with the hair of her head, was wiping off [the tears], and was tenderly kissing his feet, and anointing them with the perfume.
texts.luk.7.39: But the Pharisee who had invited him, seeing it, spake within himself, saying, This one, if he were the prophet, would have been taking note, who and of what sort, is the woman, who is even touching him, that she is, a sinner.
texts.luk.7.40: And, making answer, Jesus said unto him—Simon! I have, unto thee, something to say. He, then—Teacher, speak!—saith he.
texts.luk.7.41: Two debtors, there were, to a certain creditor,—the one, owed five hundred denaries, and, the other, fifty.
texts.luk.7.42: they not having wherewith to pay, he forgave, both. Which of them, therefore, will love him, more?
texts.luk.7.43: Making answer, Simon said—I suppose, that he to whom, the more, he forgave. And, he, said unto him—Rightly, hast thou judged.
texts.luk.7.44: And, turning towards the woman, unto Simon, he said—Seest thou this woman? I entered into thy house: water to me, on my feet, thou didst not give,—but, she, with her tears, hath wetted my feet, and, with her hair, wiped off [the tears].
texts.luk.7.45: A kiss, to me, thou didst not give,—but, she, from the time I came in, hath not ceased tenderly kissing my feet.
texts.luk.7.46: With oil, my head, thou didst not anoint,—but, she, with perfume, hath anointed, my feet.
texts.luk.7.47: For which cause, I say unto thee—Her many sins, have been forgiven, because she hath loved, much: but, he to whom little is forgiven, little, loveth.
texts.luk.7.48: And he said unto her—Thy sins have been forgiven.
texts.luk.7.49: And they who were reclining together, began to be saying within themselves—Who is, this, that, even forgiveth sins?
texts.luk.7.50: But he said unto the woman—Thy faith, hath saved thee,—Go thy way into peace.
texts.luk.8.1: And it came to pass, in due course, that he was passing through, city by city and village by village, proclaiming, and delivering the glad-message of the kingdom of God,—and, the twelve, were with him;
texts.luk.8.2: and certain women, who had been cured from evil spirits and infirmities,—Mary, the one called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone forth,
texts.luk.8.3: and Joana, wife of Chuza steward of Herod, and Susanna, and many others,—who indeed were ministering unto them out of their possessions.
texts.luk.8.4: And, seeing that a great multitude were coming together, and they who from every city were journeying forth unto him, he spake through means of a parable:—
texts.luk.8.5: The sower went forth to sow his seed,—and, as he sowed, some, indeed, fell beside the pathway, and was trodden down; and, the birds of heaven, devoured it.
texts.luk.8.6: And, other, fell down upon the rock; and, growing, was withered, because it had not moisture.
texts.luk.8.7: And, other, fell and thorns; and, growing together, the thorns, choked it.
texts.luk.8.8: And, other, fell into good ground; and, growing, brought forth fruit, a hundredfold. These things, saying, he went on to cry aloud—He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.luk.8.9: But his disciples began to question him—What might, this very, parable be?
texts.luk.8.10: And, he, said—Unto you, hath it been given, to get to know the sacred secrets of the kingdom of God; but, unto the rest, in parables,—in order that, seeing, they may not see, and, hearing, they may not understand.
texts.luk.8.11: Now the parable, is this—The seed, is, the word of God.
texts.luk.8.12: And, those beside the pathway, are they who have heard; afterwards, cometh the adversary, and catcheth away the word from their heart, lest, believing, they should, be saved.
texts.luk.8.13: And, those upon the rock, are they who, as soon as they hear, with joy, welcome the word; and, these, not having, root, are they who, for a season, believe,—and, in a season of testing, draw back.
texts.luk.8.14: And, that which in among the thorns fell, these, are they who have heard; and, by anxieties and wealth and pleasures of life being borne along, are choked up, and bear not to perfection.
texts.luk.8.15: But, that in the good ground, these, are they who, indeed, in a noble and good heart having heard the word, hold fast, and bear fruit with endurance.
texts.luk.8.16: And, no one having lit a lamp, covereth it up with a vessel, or, beneath a couch, putteth it; but, upon a lamp-stand, putteth it, that, they who come in, may see the light.
texts.luk.8.17: For there is no secret, which shall not be made, manifest; neither a hidden thing, which shall in anywise not be made known, or not come, where it can be seen.
texts.luk.8.18: Be taking heed therefore how ye hear; for, whosoever shall have, it shall be given unto him; and, whosoever shall not have, even what he seemeth to have, shall be taken from him.
texts.luk.8.19: And his mother and brethren came near unto him, and were unable to reach him, because of the multitude.
texts.luk.8.20: And it was reported to him—Thy mother and thy brethren, are standing outside, desiring, to see, thee.
texts.luk.8.21: But, he, answering, said unto them—My mother and my brethren, are, these—they who, the word of God, are hearing and doing.
texts.luk.8.22: And it came to pass, on one of the days, that, he, entered into a boat, and his disciples; and he said unto them—Let us pass over unto the other side of the lake. And they set sail.
texts.luk.8.23: Now, as they were sailing, he fell asleep. And there came down a hurricane of wind upon the lake, and they began to be filled, and to be in peril.
texts.luk.8.24: And, coming near, they roused him up, saying—Master! Master! we perish! And, he, roused up, rebuked the wind, and the surging of the water; and they ceased, and it became a calm.
texts.luk.8.25: And he said unto them—Where was your faith? But, struck with fear, they marvelled, saying one to another—Who then is, this,—that, even unto the winds, he giveth orders, and unto the water, and they hearken unto him.
texts.luk.8.26: And they sailed down into the country of the Gerasenes, the which is over against Galilee.
texts.luk.8.27: And, when he went forth upon the land, there met him a certain man, out of the city, having demons; and, for a considerable time, he had put on no garment, and, in a house, would not abide, but among the tombs.
texts.luk.8.28: But, seeing Jesus, he cried out aloud, and fell down before him, and, with a loud voice, said—What have I in common with thee, O Jesus, Son of [God] the Most High? I beg of thee—Do not torment me!—
texts.luk.8.29: for he was about to charge the impure spirit to come out from the man. For, many times, had it snatched him away; and he used to be bound with chains and fetters, for a safe-guard, and was wont to break in pieces the bonds, and to be driven by the demon into the deserts.
texts.luk.8.30: And Jesus questioned him—What name hast thou? And, he, said—Legion! because many demons had entered into him.
texts.luk.8.31: And they were beseeching him that he would not order them, into the abyss, to depart.
texts.luk.8.32: Now there was there, a herd of a good many swine, feeding in the mountain; and they besought him, that he would suffer them, into those, to enter; and he suffered them.
texts.luk.8.33: And the demons, going forth from the man entered into the swine; and the herd rushed down the cliff, into the lake, and were choked.
texts.luk.8.34: And they who had been feeding them, seeing what had happened, fled, and carried tidings into the city, and into the country-places.
texts.luk.8.35: And they went forth to see what had happened; and came unto Jesus, and found the man from whom the demons had gone forth, sitting, clothed, and of sound mind, near the feet of Jesus,—and they were struck with fear.
texts.luk.8.36: And they who had seen it, reported unto them, how the demonized man was saved.
texts.luk.8.37: And one and all of the throng of the surrounding country of the Gerasenes, requested him, to depart from them; because, with a great fear, were they oppressed. And, he, entering into a boat, returned.
texts.luk.8.38: And the man from whom the demons had gone forth, began to beg of him, that he might be with him; but he dismissed him, saying—
texts.luk.8.39: Be returning unto thy house, and telling forth what great things, God, for thee, hath done. And he departed, through all the city, proclaiming what great things, Jesus, had done for him.
texts.luk.8.40: Now, when Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him back, for they were all expecting him.
texts.luk.8.41: And lo! there came a man, whose name was Jairus, and, the same, was, a ruler of the synagogue,—and, falling down near the feet of Jesus, he began beseeching him to enter into his house;
texts.luk.8.42: because he had, an only-begotten daughter, about twelve years old, and, she, was dying. Now, as he withdrew, the multitudes, were hemming him in.
texts.luk.8.43: And, a woman, with a flow of blood of twelve years standing, who indeed could, from no one, be cured,
texts.luk.8.44: coming near behind, touched the fringe of his mantle; and, instantly, was stayed the flow of her blood.
texts.luk.8.45: And Jesus said—Who, is it that touched me? And, when all were denying, Peter said—Master! the multitudes, are hemming thee in, and pressing along.
texts.luk.8.46: But, Jesus, said—Some one touched me, for, I, took note of power, gone out from me.
texts.luk.8.47: And, the woman seeing that she had not escaped notice, trembling, came, and, falling down before him, reported before all the people, for what cause she had touched him, and how she was healed instantly!
texts.luk.8.48: And, he, said to her—Daughter! thy faith, hath saved thee: Go thy way into peace.
texts.luk.8.49: While yet he is speaking, there cometh one from the synagogue ruler’s, saying—Thy daughter, is dead: No further, be troubling the teacher.
texts.luk.8.50: But, Jesus, hearing, answered him—Do not fear! Only believe, and she shall be saved.
texts.luk.8.51: And, when he came into the house, he suffered no one to enter with him, save Peter and John and James, and the father of the girl, and the mother.
texts.luk.8.52: And they were all weeping, and beating themselves, for her. And he said—Be not weeping; for she died not, but is sleeping.
texts.luk.8.53: And they were deriding him, knowing that she died.
texts.luk.8.54: But, he, grasping her hand, called aloud, saying—O girl! arise!
texts.luk.8.55: And her spirit returned, and she rose up instantly, and he ordered that something should be given her to eat.
texts.luk.8.56: And her parents were beside themselves. But, he, charged them to tell, no one, what had happened.
texts.luk.9.1: And, calling together the twelve, he gave them power and authority over all the demons, and to be curing, diseases;
texts.luk.9.2: and sent them forth, to be proclaiming the kingdom of God, and to be healing;
texts.luk.9.3: and said unto them—Nothing, take ye for the journey,—neither staff, nor satchel, nor bread, nor silver, nor to have, two tunics.
texts.luk.9.4: And, into whatsoever house ye enter, there, abide, and, thence, be going forth.
texts.luk.9.5: And, as many soever as shall not welcome you, in going forth from that city, the dust of your feet, shake ye off, for a witness against them.
texts.luk.9.6: And they went forth, and were passing through, along the villages,—delivering the glad-message, and effecting cures in every direction.
texts.luk.9.7: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all the things which were coming to pass, and was utterly at a loss, because of its being said, by some, that, John, had been raised from the dead;
texts.luk.9.8: and, by some, that, Elijah, had appeared; and, by others, that, some prophet of the ancients, had arisen.
texts.luk.9.9: But Herod said—John, I myself, beheaded; but, who is this, concerning whom I am hearing such things as these? And he was seeking to see him.
texts.luk.9.10: And the Apostles, returning, related to him what great things they had done. And, taking them aside, he retired privately, into a city called Bethsaida.
texts.luk.9.11: But, the multitudes, getting to know, followed him; and, giving them welcome, he began speaking unto them concerning the kingdom of God,—and, them that had need of cure, he healed,
texts.luk.9.12: And, the day, began to decline; and the twelve, coming near, said to him—Dismiss the multitude, that, going into the surrounding villages and hamlets, they may lodge, and find provisions; because, here, in a desert place, are we.
texts.luk.9.13: But he said unto them—Give, ye, them to eat. They, however, said—We have not more than five loaves, and two fishes,—unless perhaps, we, should go, and buy food, for all this people.
texts.luk.9.14: For there were about five thousand men. And he said unto his disciples—Make them recline, in companies of about fifty each.
texts.luk.9.15: And they did so,—and made, one and all, recline.
texts.luk.9.16: And, taking the five loaves, and the two fishes, looking up into heaven, he blessed them, and brake [them] up, and went on giving to the disciples, to set before the multitude;
texts.luk.9.17: and they did all eat and were filled. And that which remained over to them, was taken up,—of broken pieces, twelve baskets.
texts.luk.9.18: And, it came to pass, when he was praying in solitude, the disciples, were with him. And he questioned them, saying—Who do the multitudes say that I am?
texts.luk.9.19: And they, answering, said John the Immerser; But some, Elijah, and others, that, some prophet of the ancients, hath arisen.
texts.luk.9.20: And he said to them—But who say, ye, that I am? And, Peter, answering, said—The Christ of God!
texts.luk.9.21: He, however, sternly admonishing them, gave charge that, unto no one, should they be telling this;
texts.luk.9.22: saying—The Son of Man must needs suffer, many things, and be rejected by the Elders and High priests and Scribes, and be slain,—and, on the third day, arise.
texts.luk.9.23: And he was saying, unto all—If any one intendeth after me to come, Let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily,—and be following me.
texts.luk.9.24: For, whosoever intendeth, his life, to save, shall lose it; but, whosoever shall lose his life for my sake, the same, shall save it?
texts.luk.9.25: For what doth a man profit, who hath gained the whole world, but hath lost, or been made to forfeit, himself?
texts.luk.9.26: For, whosoever shall be ashamed of me, and of my words, of him, the Son of Man, will be ashamed, whensoever he shall come in his glory, and that of the Father, and of the holy messengers.
texts.luk.9.27: But I tell you of a truth—There, are, some of those, here, standing, who shall in nowise taste of death, until they see the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.9.28: And it came to pass, after these words, about eight days, taking with him Peter and John and James, he went up into the mountain to pray.
texts.luk.9.29: And it came to pass, while he was praying, that, the appearance of his face, was changed, and, his clothing, became white, effulgent.
texts.luk.9.30: And lo! two men, were conversing with him, who, indeed, were Moses and Elijah,—
texts.luk.9.31: who, appearing in glory, were speaking as to his departure, which he was about to fulfil in Jerusalem.
texts.luk.9.32: Now, Peter, and they who were with him, had become heavy with sleep; but, waking up, they saw his glory, and the two men who were standing with him.
texts.luk.9.33: And it came to pass, when they were being parted from him, Peter said unto Jesus—Master! it is, delightful, for us to be, here: Let us, therefore, make three tents, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah:—not knowing what he said.
texts.luk.9.34: Now, while he was saying these things, there came a cloud, and it began to overshadow them,—and they were overcome with fear as they entered into the cloud.
texts.luk.9.35: And, a voice, came out of the cloud, saying—This, is my Son, the Chosen One: Unto him, be hearkening.
texts.luk.9.36: And, when the voice came, there was found, Jesus alone. And they held their peace, and, unto no one, reported they, in those days, any of the things which they had seen.
texts.luk.9.37: And it came to pass, on the next day, when they came down from the mountain, that there met him a great multitude.
texts.luk.9.38: And lo! a man from the multitude, uttered a cry, saying—Teacher! I beg of thee, to look upon my son, because, my only begotten, he is.
texts.luk.9.39: And lo! a spirit, taketh him, and, suddenly, he crieth out,—and it convulseth him—with foaming, and with difficulty departeth from him, sorely bruising him.
texts.luk.9.40: And I begged of thy disciples, that they would cast it out, and they could not.
texts.luk.9.41: And, making answer, Jesus said—O faithless and perverted generation! how long shall I be with you, and bear with you? Bring, hither, thy son.
texts.luk.9.42: And, while yet he was coming, the demon tare him, and mangled him. But Jesus rebuked the impure spirit, and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
texts.luk.9.43: And they were all being struck with astonishment, at the majesty of God. And, while all were marvelling at all things which he was doing, he said unto his disciples:
texts.luk.9.44: Lay, ye, up in your ears, these words; for, the Son of Man, is about to be delivered up, into the hands of men.
texts.luk.9.45: But, they, understood not this saying, and it had become veiled from them, that they might not grasp it,—and they were afraid to question him, concerning this saying.
texts.luk.9.46: But there entered a reasoning among them, as to who of them should be greatest.
texts.luk.9.47: And, Jesus, perceiving the reasoning of their heart, taking a child, placed it near himself,—
texts.luk.9.48: and said unto them—Whosoever shall give welcome unto this child, on my name, unto me, giveth welcome; and, whosoever, unto me, giveth welcome, giveth welcome unto him that sent me forth. For, he who is least among you all, the same, is, great.
texts.luk.9.49: But John, answering, said—Master! we saw some one, in thy name, casting out demons,—and we forbade him, because he followeth not with us.
texts.luk.9.50: And Jesus said unto him—Do not forbid; for, whosoever is not against you, is, for you.
texts.luk.9.51: And it came to pass, when the days for taking him up were on the point of being fulfilled, even he himself, set, his face, to be journeying unto Jerusalem;
texts.luk.9.52: and he sent messengers before his face,—and, taking their journey, they entered into a village of Samaritans, so as to prepare for him.
texts.luk.9.53: And they welcomed him not, because, his face, was for journeying unto Jerusalem.
texts.luk.9.54: And the disciples James and John, seeing it, said—Lord! wilt thou, that we bid fire come down from heaven, and destroy them?
texts.luk.9.56: And they journeyed into a different village.
texts.luk.9.57: And, as they were journeying on the road, one said unto him—I will follow thee, whithersoever thou shalt depart.
texts.luk.9.58: And Jesus said unto him—the foxes, have, dens, and, the birds of heaven, nests; but, the Son of Man, hath not where, his head, he may recline.
texts.luk.9.59: And he said unto another—Be following me! But, he, said—Suffer me, first, to depart, and bury my father.
texts.luk.9.60: And he said unto him—Leave, the dead, to bury their own dead; but, thou, departing, be declaring the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.9.61: And, yet another, said—I will follow thee, Lord; But, first, suffer me to bid adieu to them that are in my house.
texts.luk.9.62: But Jesus said [unto him] —No one, laying the hand on a plough and looking unto the things behind, is, fit, for the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.10.1: And, after these things, the Lord appointed seventy two others, and sent them forth, two and two before his face, into every city and place whither, he himself, was about to come.
texts.luk.10.2: And he was saying unto them—The harvest, indeed, is, great, but, the labourers, few; beg ye, therefore, of the Lord of the harvest, that he would thrust forth, labourers, into his harvest.
texts.luk.10.3: Withdraw! Lo! I send you forth as lambs amid wolves.
texts.luk.10.4: Be not carrying purse, or satchel, or sandals, and, no one along the road, salute ye;
texts.luk.10.5: And, into whatsoever house ye enter, First, say, Peace to this house!
texts.luk.10.6: And, if the son of peace be, there, your peace, shall rest upon it; but, otherwise, at least, unto you, shall it return.
texts.luk.10.7: And, in the self-same house, abide ye, eating and drinking such things as they have; for, worthy, is the labourer, of his hire: be not removing from house to house.
texts.luk.10.8: And, into whatsoever city ye shall enter, and they bid you welcome, be eating such things as are set before you;
texts.luk.10.9: And be curing the sick that are, therein, and be saying unto them—The kingdom of God hath drawn nigh upon you.
texts.luk.10.10: But, into whatsoever city ye shall enter, and they do not welcome you, going forth into the broadways thereof, say ye:
texts.luk.10.11: Even the dust that cleaveth unto us, out of your city, unto our feet, do we wipe off against you; nevertheless, of this, be taking notice—The kingdom of God hath drawn near.
texts.luk.10.12: I tell you, for them of Sodom, in that day, more tolerable, will it be, than for that city.
texts.luk.10.13: Alas for thee, Chorazin! Alas for thee, Bethsaida! Because, if, in Tyre and Zidon, had been done the works of power which have been down in you, of old, in sackcloth and ashes sitting, they would have repented.
texts.luk.10.14: Moreover, for Tyre and Zidon, more tolerable, will it be, in the judgment, than, for you.
texts.luk.10.15: And, thou, Capernaum,—Unto heaven, shalt thou be uplifted? …Unto hades, thou shalt be brought down!
texts.luk.10.16: He that hearkeneth unto you, unto me, doth hearken, and, he that setteth you aside, doth set, me, aside; and, he that setteth, me, aside, doth set aside, him that sent me.
texts.luk.10.17: And the seventy [-two] returned, with joy, saying—Lord! even the demons, submit themselves unto us, in thy name!
texts.luk.10.18: And he said unto them—I was beholding Satan, when, like lightning, out of heaven, he fell!
texts.luk.10.19: Lo! I have given you the authority—to be treading upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and, nothing, unto you, shall in anywise do harm;
texts.luk.10.20: Notwithstanding, in this, be not rejoicing—that, the spirits, unto you submit themselves; but be rejoicing—that, your names, are inscribed in the heavens!
texts.luk.10.21: In the self-same hour, exulted he in the Holy Spirit, and said—I openly give praise unto thee, Father! Lord of heaven and earth! in that thou hast hid these things from the wise and discerning, and hast revealed them unto babes,—Yea, O Father! that, so, hath it become, a delight, before thee.
texts.luk.10.22: All things, unto me, have been delivered up by my Father; and, no one, knoweth, who the Son is, save the Father,—and who the Father is, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son may be minded to reveal him.
texts.luk.10.23: And, turning unto his disciples, privately, he said—Happy, the eyes, that see what ye see!
texts.luk.10.24: For I tell you, Many prophets and kings, have desired to see what, ye, see, and they saw not, and to hear what ye hear, and they heard not.
texts.luk.10.25: And lo! a certain lawyer, arose, putting him to the test, saying—Teacher! by doing what, shall I inherit, life age-abiding?
texts.luk.10.26: And, he, said unto him—In the law, what is written? how dost thou read?
texts.luk.10.27: And, he, answering, said—Thou shalt love the Lord thy God, out of all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might, and with all thine intention; and thy neighbour, as thyself?
texts.luk.10.28: And he said unto him—Rightly, hast thou answered: This, do, and thou shalt live.
texts.luk.10.29: But, he, wishing to justify himself, said unto Jesus—And, who is, my, neighbour?
texts.luk.10.30: And taking up [the question], Jesus said—A certain man, was going down from Jerusalem unto Jericho, and, with robbers, fell in,—who, stripping him, and inflicting, wounds, upon him, departed, leaving him, half dead.
texts.luk.10.31: And, by chance, a certain priest, was coming down by that road, and, seeing him, passed by, on the opposite side.
texts.luk.10.32: And, in like manner, a Levite also, coming down to the place, and seeing him, passed by, on the opposite side.
texts.luk.10.33: But, a certain Samaritan, going on his journey, came down to him, and, seeing him, was moved with compassion;
texts.luk.10.34: and, coming near, bound up his bruises, pouring thereon oil and wine,—and, setting him on his own beast, brought him into an inn, and took care of him.
texts.luk.10.35: And, on the morrow, throwing out two denaries, he gave them to the inn-keeper, and said—Take care of him, and, whatsoever thou shall further spend, I, when on my way back, will duly pay thee.
texts.luk.10.36: Which of these three, seemeth unto thee to have become, neighbour, unto him who fell among the robbers?
texts.luk.10.37: And, he, said—He who dealt mercifully with him. And Jesus said unto him—Be taking thy journey, and, thou, be doing, in like manner.
texts.luk.10.38: And, as they were journeying, he, entered into a certain village; and, a certain woman, named Martha, welcomed him into her house.
texts.luk.10.39: And, she, had a sister, called Mary, who also, seating herself at the feet of the Lord, was hearing his word.
texts.luk.10.40: But, Martha, was distracted about much ministering, and, coming near, said—Lord! carest thou not that, my sister, hath left me to be ministering, alone? Speak to her, then, that she help me.
texts.luk.10.41: But the Lord, answering, said to her—Martha! Martha! thou art anxious and troubled about many things:
texts.luk.10.42: Of few things, is there need, or, of one; Mary, in fact, hath chosen, the good part,—one which shall not be taken away from her.
texts.luk.11.1: And it came to pass, when he was in a certain place praying, as he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him—Lord! teach us to pray, as, John also, taught his disciples.
texts.luk.11.2: And he said unto them—Whensoever ye are praying, say—Father! Hallowed be thy name, Come may thy kingdom,
texts.luk.11.3: Our needful bread, be giving us, day by day;
texts.luk.11.4: And forgive us our sins, for, even we ourselves, forgive every one indebted to us; And bring us not into temptation.
texts.luk.11.5: And he said unto them—Who from among you, shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say unto him—Friend! supply me with three loaves,
texts.luk.11.6: forasmuch as, a friend of mine, hath come off a journey unto me, and I have not what I can set before him;
texts.luk.11.7: and, he, from within, shall answer, and say—Be not disturbing me,—already, the door hath been fastened, and, my children, with me, are, in bed: I cannot rise and give thee?
texts.luk.11.8: I say unto you—Even though he will not give him, rising because of his being a friend of his, because, at least, of his importunity, he will rouse himself, and give him as many as he needeth.
texts.luk.11.9: I, therefore, unto you, say—Be asking, and it shall be given to you, Be seeking, and ye shall find,—Be knocking, and it shall be opened unto you.
texts.luk.11.10: For, whosoever asketh, receiveth, and, he that seeketh, findeth,—and, to him that knocketh, shall it be opened.
texts.luk.11.11: But which is the father, from among yourselves, whom the son will ask for, a fish, who, instead of a fish, will give him, a serpent?
texts.luk.11.12: Or shall also ask, an egg, who will give him, a scorpion?
texts.luk.11.13: If therefore, ye, being, evil, know how to be giving, good gifts, unto your children, how much rather, will, the heavenly Father, give Holy Spirit unto them that ask him!
texts.luk.11.14: And he was casting out a demon that was dumb; and it came to pass, when the demon went out, the dumb began speaking. And the multitudes marvelled;
texts.luk.11.15: but, some from among them, said—In Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, is he casting out the demons;
texts.luk.11.16: and, others, putting him to the test, a sign out of heaven, were seeking from him.
texts.luk.11.17: But, he, knowing their thoughts, said unto them—Every kingdom, against itself divided, is laid waste, and, a house, against a house, [divided], falleth;
texts.luk.11.18: And, if, even Satan, against himself hath become divided, how shall his kingdom stand? because ye are saying that, in Beelzebul, am I casting out the demons.
texts.luk.11.19: But, if, I, in Beelzebul, am casting out the demons, In whom are, your sons, casting them out? Wherefore, they, shall be, your judges.
texts.luk.11.20: But, if, with the finger of God, I, am casting out the demons, then doubtless unawares hath come upon you, the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.11.21: Whensoever, the mighty one, armed, may be guarding his own dwelling, in peace, are his goods;
texts.luk.11.22: But, whensoever, a mightier than he, shall come upon and vanquish him, his panoply, he taketh away, wherein he was trusting, and, his spoils, he distributeth.
texts.luk.11.23: He that is not with me, is, against me; and, he that gathereth not with me, scattereth.
texts.luk.11.24: Whensoever, the impure spirit, goeth out from the man, it passeth through waterless places, seeking rest; and, not finding it, [then,] it saith, I will return unto my house, whence I came out;—
texts.luk.11.25: and, coming, findeth it, [empty,] swept, and adorned.
texts.luk.11.26: Then, goeth it, and taketh along with itself, other spirits, more wicked than itself—seven, and, entering in, fixeth its dwelling there; and, the last state of that man, becometh, worse than the first.
texts.luk.11.27: Now it came to pass, while he was saying these things, that a certain woman out of the multitude, lifting up her voice, said unto him—Happy the womb that bare thee! And the breasts which thou didst suck!
texts.luk.11.28: But, he, said—Yea rather!—Happy they who hear the word of God, and observe it!
texts.luk.11.29: And, as the multitudes were thronging together, he began to be saying—This generation, is, a wicked generation: A sign, it is seeking, and, a sign, shall not be given it, save the sign of Jonah.
texts.luk.11.30: For, according as, Jonah, became, unto the Ninevites, a sign, so, shall be, the Son of Man also, unto this generation.
texts.luk.11.31: The queen of the south, will rise up, in the judgment, with the men of this generation, and will condemn them; because she came out of the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon,—and lo! something more than Solomon, here.
texts.luk.11.32: Men of Nineveh, will rise up, in the judgment, with this generation, and will condemn it; because they repented into the proclamation of Jonah,—and lo! something more than Jonah, here.
texts.luk.11.33: No one, having lighted, a lamp, into a covered place, a putteth it, nor, under the measure; but upon the lampstand, that they who enter may see, the light.
texts.luk.11.34: The lamp of thy body, is thine eye: Whensoever, thine eye, may be, single, even the whole of thy body, is, lighted up; but, whensoever it may be, useless, even thy body, is darkened.
texts.luk.11.35: Be looking to it, therefore, lest, the light that is in thee, be, darkness.
texts.luk.11.36: If, therefore, thy whole body, is lighted up, not having any part darkened, the whole, shall be lighted up, as whensoever, the lamp, with its radiance, may be giving thee light.
texts.luk.11.37: And, when he had spoken, a Pharisee was requesting him that he would dine with him; and, entering, he reclined.
texts.luk.11.38: And, the Pharisee, beholding, marvelled that he was not, first, immersed, before the dinner.
texts.luk.11.39: And the Lord said unto him: Now, ye, the Pharisees, the outside of the cup and of the tray, do make pure; but, your inward part, is full of plunder and wickedness.
texts.luk.11.40: Simple ones! Did not, he who made the outside, the inside also, make?
texts.luk.11.41: Notwithstanding, as to the things within, give alms, and lo! everything, is, pure unto you.
texts.luk.11.42: But alas for you, the Pharisees! because ye tithe the mint, and the rue, and every garden herb, and pass by justice, and the love of God. But, these things, it was binding to do, and, those, not to pass by.
texts.luk.11.43: Alas for you, the Pharisees! because ye love the first seats in the synagogues, and the salutations in the market-places!
texts.luk.11.44: Alas for you! because ye are as the secret tombs: even the men that are walking above them, know it not.
texts.luk.11.45: And, making answer, one of the Lawyers saith unto him, Teacher! these things, saying, us also, dost thou insult!
texts.luk.11.46: And, he, said—And, for you, the lawyers, alas! because ye lade men with burdens hard to be borne, and, yourselves, with one of your fingers, touch not the burdens.
texts.luk.11.47: Alas for you! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers slew them!
texts.luk.11.48: Hence, witnesses, are ye, and find consenting pleasure in the works of your fathers: because, they, indeed, slew them, and, ye, are building, [their tombs].
texts.luk.11.49: For this cause, the Wisdom of God hath said—I will send forth, unto them, prophets and apostles,—and, some from among them, will they slay, and, [some] persecute:
texts.luk.11.50: That the blood of all the prophets which hath been shed from the foundation of the world, may be sought out, from this generation,—
texts.luk.11.51: From the blood of Abel, unto the blood of Zachariah who was destroyed betwixt the altar and the house; Yea! I say unto you—It shall be sought out from this generation.
texts.luk.11.52: Alas for you, the lawyers! because ye took away the key of knowledge: yourselves, entered not, and, them who were entering, ye hindered.
texts.luk.11.53: And, when, from thence, he came out, the Scribes and the Pharisees began, with vehemence, to be hemming him in, and trying to make him speak off-hand concerning many things,—
texts.luk.11.54: lying in wait for him, to catch something out of his mouth.
texts.luk.12.1: Amongst which things, when the ten thousands of the multitude were gathered together, so that they were treading one upon another, he began to be saying, unto his disciples, first—Be keeping yourselves free from the leaven of the Pharisees, the which is, hypocrisy.
texts.luk.12.2: But, nothing, hath been, covered up, which shall not be uncovered, and hidden, which shall not be made known.
texts.luk.12.3: Because, as many things as, in the darkness, ye have said, in the light, shall be heard; and, what to the ear ye spake, in the chambers, shall be proclaimed on the housetops.
texts.luk.12.4: And I say unto you, my friends—Do not be put in fear of them who kill the body, and, after these things, have nothing more uncommon which they can do.
texts.luk.12.5: But I will suggest to you, whom ye should fear—Fear him who, after killing, hath authority to cast into gehenna,—Yea, I say unto you—Him, fear ye.
texts.luk.12.6: Are not, five sparrows, sold for two farthings? and, not one from among them, hath been forgotten before God.
texts.luk.12.7: But, even the hairs of your head, have all been numbered: Be not afraid: many sparrows, ye excel.
texts.luk.12.8: And I say unto you—Whosoever shall confess me before men, even the Son of Man, will confess him, before the messengers of God;
texts.luk.12.9: But, he who denied me before men, shall be denied before the messengers of God.
texts.luk.12.10: And, whosoever shall say a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him; but, unto him who, against the Holy Spirit, speaketh profanely, it shall not be forgiven.
texts.luk.12.11: But, whensoever they shall be bringing you in before the synagogues, and the rulers, and the authorities, do not be anxious how, [or what] ye shall answer, or what ye shall say;
texts.luk.12.12: For, the Holy Spirit, shall teach you, in that very hour, what ye ought to say.
texts.luk.12.13: And one from amongst the multitude said unto him—Teacher! bid my brother divide with me the inheritance.
texts.luk.12.14: But, he, said unto him—Man! who hath appointed me a judge or divider over you?
texts.luk.12.15: And he said unto them—Mind and be guarding yourselves from all covetousness; for not, in one’s abundance, doth his life spring out of his possessions.
texts.luk.12.16: And he spake a parable unto them, saying—A certain rich man’s estate, bare well.
texts.luk.12.17: And he began to deliberate within himself, saying—What shall I do? because I have not where I can gather my fruits.
texts.luk.12.18: And he said—This, will I do,—I will pull down my barns, and, greater ones, build, and gather, there, all my wheat and good things;
texts.luk.12.19: and will say to my soul—Soul! thou hast many good things [lying by for many years: be taking thy rest, eat, drink,] be making merry!
texts.luk.12.20: But God said unto him—Simple one! on this very night, they are asking, thy soul, from thee; The things, then, which thou hast prepared, whose shall they be?
texts.luk.12.21: [So, is he that is laying up treasure for himself, and is not rich, towards God.]
texts.luk.12.22: And he said unto his disciples—For this cause, I say unto you,—Be not anxious for the life, what ye shall eat, nor yet for [your] body, what ye shall put on;
texts.luk.12.23: For, the life, is more, than the food, and, the body, than, the clothing.
texts.luk.12.24: Consider well the ravens—That they sow nor, neither do they reap, which have neither chamber nor barn,—and, God, feedeth, them! By how much do, ye, excel, the birds?
texts.luk.12.25: And, who from among you, though anxious, can, unto his stature, add a cubit?
texts.luk.12.26: If then, not even the least thing, ye can do, why, concerning the rest, are ye anxious?
texts.luk.12.27: Consider well the lilies, how they grow: they toil not, neither do they spin, and yet I say unto you—Not even Solomon, in all his glory, was arrayed like one of these.
texts.luk.12.28: But, if God thus adorneth, the grass, which is, in a field, to-day, and, to-morrow, into an oven, is cast, how much rather you, O little-of-faith?
texts.luk.12.29: Ye, therefore, be not seeking what ye shall eat and what ye shall drink, and be not held in suspense;
texts.luk.12.30: For, after all these things, do, the nations of the world, seek,—but, your Father, knoweth that ye need these things.
texts.luk.12.31: Notwithstanding, be seeking his kingdom,—and, these things, shall be added unto you.
texts.luk.12.32: Be not afraid, the dear little flock! for your Father delighteth to give you, the kingdom.
texts.luk.12.33: Sell your possessions, and give alms, make for yourselves purses that wax not old,—treasure unfailing, in the heavens, where, thief, doth not draw near, and, moth, doth not spoil.
texts.luk.12.34: For, where your treasure is, there, will your heart he also.
texts.luk.12.35: Let your loins be girded, and your lamps burning,
texts.luk.12.36: And, ye yourselves, like unto men awaiting their own lord, once he may break up out of the marriage-feast,—that, when he cometh and knocketh, straightway, they may open unto him.
texts.luk.12.37: Happy those servants, whom the lord, when he cometh, shall find watching! Verily, I say unto you—he will gird himself, and make them recline, and, coming near, will minister unto them.
texts.luk.12.38: And, if, in the second, or if, in the third, watch, he come and find, thus, happy, are, they!
texts.luk.12.39: But, of this, be taking note—Had the householder known, in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched, and not suffered his house, to be digged through.
texts.luk.12.40: Ye, therefore, be getting ready, because, in what hour ye are not thinking, The Son of Man cometh!
texts.luk.12.41: But Peter said—Lord! unto us, this parable, speakest thou? or, even unto all?
texts.luk.12.42: And the Lord said—Who then is the faithful steward, the prudent one, whom the lord will appoint over his body of attendants, to be giving, in due season, the measured allowance of wheat?
texts.luk.12.43: Happy, that servant, whom the lord, when he cometh shall find doing, thus!
texts.luk.12.44: Of a truth, I say unto you—Over all his possessions, will he appoint him.
texts.luk.12.45: But, if that servant should say in his heart—My lord delayeth to come! and should begin to be striking the youths and the maidens,—to be eating also, and drinking, and making himself drunk,
texts.luk.12.46: The lord of that servant, will have come—on a day when he is not expecting, and in an hour when he is not taking note,—and will cut him asunder, and, his part, with the unfaithful, will appoint.
texts.luk.12.47: And, that servant, who had come to know the will of his lord, and neither prepared, nor wrought unto his will, shall be beaten with many stripes;
texts.luk.12.48: Whereas, he who had not come to know, and did things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. And, every one to whom was given much, much, shall be sought from him; and, he to whom they committed much, for more than common, will they ask him.
texts.luk.12.49: Fire, came I to cast upon the earth,—and what can I wish, if, already, it hath been, kindled?
texts.luk.12.50: But, an immersion, have I, to be immersed with, and how am I distressed, until it be ended!
texts.luk.12.51: Suppose ye, that, peace, I am come to give in the earth? Nay, I tell you, but rather division.
texts.luk.12.52: For there shall be, henceforth, five in one house, divided,—three against two, and two against three:
texts.luk.12.53: There shall be divided—Father against son, and son against father, mother against daughter, and daughter against the mother,—mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against the mother-in-law.
texts.luk.12.54: And he went on to say, even unto the multitudes,—Whensoever ye see a cloud springing up from the west, straightway, ye are saying—A thunderstorm is coming! and it happeneth thus.
texts.luk.12.55: And, whensoever a south wind, blowing, ye say—A scorching heat, will there be! and it cometh to pass.
texts.luk.12.56: Hypocrites! the face of the earth and of the heaven, ye know how to scan; but, this season, how know ye not to scan;
texts.luk.12.57: Why, moreover, even from yourselves, judge ye not what is just?
texts.luk.12.58: For, as thou art going along with thine adversary unto a ruler, on the way, take pains to get a release from him; lest once he drag thee along unto the judge, and, the judge, deliver thee up to the punisher,—and, the punisher, cast thee into prison:
texts.luk.12.59: I tell thee—In nowise shalt thou come out from thence, until, even the last fraction, thou pay!
texts.luk.13.1: Now there were present some, in that very season, bringing tidings to him, concerning the Galilaeans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
texts.luk.13.2: And, answering, he said unto them—Suppose ye, that, these Galilaeans, had become, sinners beyond all the Galilaeans, because, these things, they have suffered?
texts.luk.13.3: Nay! I tell you, but, except ye repent, ye, all, in like manner, shall perish.
texts.luk.13.4: Or, those eighteen, upon whom fell the tower in Siloam, and slew them, suppose ye that, they, had become, debtors, beyond all the men who were dwelling in Jerusalem?
texts.luk.13.5: Nay! I tell you, but, except ye repent, ye, all, in the same way, shall perish.
texts.luk.13.6: And he went on to speak this parable:—A certain man had, a fig-tree, planted in his vineyard, and he canto seeking fruit therein, and found none.
texts.luk.13.7: And he said unto the vine-dresser—Lo! three years, I come, seeking fruit in this fig-tree, and find none. Cut it down! Why doth it make, even the round useless?
texts.luk.13.8: And, he, answering, saith unto him—Sir! let it alone this year also, until such time as I dig about it, and throw in manure,—
texts.luk.13.9: and if it may bear fruit for the future; …but, otherwise, certainly, thou shalt cut it down.
texts.luk.13.10: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues, on the Sabbath.
texts.luk.13.11: And lo! a woman, having a spirit of weakness eighteen years,—and was bowed together, and unable to lift herself up, at all.
texts.luk.13.12: And, seeing her, Jesus called her and said to her—Woman! thou art loosed from thy weakness,—
texts.luk.13.13: and laid on her his hands; and, instantly, she was made straight again, and began glorifying God.
texts.luk.13.14: But the synagogue-ruler, answering, being greatly displeased that, on the Sabbath, Jesus had healed, began saying unto the multitude—Six days, there are, in which men ought to get their work done; On them, therefore, come and be healed, and, not on the day of rest.
texts.luk.13.15: The Lord answered him, and said—Hypocrites! Doth not, each one of you, on the Sabbath, loose his ox or ass from the manger, and, leading it away, give it drink?
texts.luk.13.16: But, this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound, lo! eighteen years, was there not a needs-be that she should be loosed from this bond, on the day of rest?
texts.luk.13.17: And, as he was saying, these, things, all who had been setting themselves against him were being put to shame; and, all the multitude, were rejoicing over all the glorious things which were being brought to pass by him.
texts.luk.13.18: He went on to say, therefore—Whereunto, is the kingdom of God, like? And, whereunto, shall I liken it?
texts.luk.13.19: It is, like, unto a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and cast into his own garden; and it grew, and became a tree, and, the birds of heaven, lodged amongst its branches.
texts.luk.13.20: And, again, he said—Whereunto, shall I liken the kingdom of God?
texts.luk.13.21: It is, like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until, the whole, was leavened.
texts.luk.13.22: And he was journeying on, city by city and village by village, and making, progress, unto Jerusalem.
texts.luk.13.23: And one said unto him—Lord! are they, few, who are being saved? And, he, said unto them—
texts.luk.13.24: Be striving to enter through the narrow door; for, many, I say unto you, will seek to enter, and will not be able,—
texts.luk.13.25: when once the householder shall rouse himself, and lock the door, and ye begin to stand, outside, and to knock at the door, saying—Lord! open to us; and he shall answer and say unto you—I know you not, whence ye are.
texts.luk.13.26: Then, will ye begin to say—We did eat and drink in thy presence, and, in our broadways, thou didst, teach;
texts.luk.13.27: And he will speak, saying unto you—I know not whence ye are; Depart from me, all workers of unrighteous—
texts.luk.13.28: There, will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, as soon as ye see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and, yourselves, being thrust forth outside.
texts.luk.13.29: And they shall have come from east and west, and from north and south, and be made recline in the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.13.30: And lo! there are, last, who shall be, first, and there are, first, who shall be, last;
texts.luk.13.31: In that very hour, came near certain Pharisees, saying unto him, Go forth, and be journeying hence, because, Herod, desireth to slay thee.
texts.luk.13.32: And he said unto them—Go and tell this fox, Lo! I am casting out demons, and, cures, am I finishing, to-day, and to-morrow,—
texts.luk.13.33: and, on the third, I am to be made perfect. Nevertheless, I must needs, to-day, and tomorrow, and the following, be journeying on, because it is impossible that a prophet perish, outside Jerusalem.
texts.luk.13.34: Jerusalem! Jerusalem! she that slayeth the prophets, and stoneth them that are sent unto her! How often, have I desired to gather together thy children, like as a hen, her own brood, under her wings,—and ye did not desire!
texts.luk.13.35: Lo! your house is left to you. [And] I say unto you—In nowise shall ye see me, until ye say,—Blessed, is he that cometh in the name of the Lord!
texts.luk.14.1: And it came to pass, when he entered into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees, on a Sabbath, to eat bread, that, they, were narrowly watching him.
texts.luk.14.2: And lo! there was, a certain man, who had the dropsy, before him.
texts.luk.14.3: And Jesus, answering, spake unto the Lawyers and Pharisees, saying—Is it allowed, on the Sabbath, to cure, or not? But, they, held their peace.
texts.luk.14.4: And taking hold [of him] he healed and dismissed him,—
texts.luk.14.5: and, unto them, said—Which of you, shall have a son or an ox that, into a pit, shall fall, and will not straightway pull him up, on the day of rest?
texts.luk.14.6: And they could not return an answer unto these things.
texts.luk.14.7: And he went on to speak, unto the invited, a parable,—observing how, the first couches, they were choosing; saying unto them—
texts.luk.14.8: Whensoever thou hast been invited by anyone unto a marriage feast, do not recline on the first couch; lest once, a more honourable than thou, have been invited by him,
texts.luk.14.9: and he that invited both thee and him should come, and say unto thee—Give, unto this one, place! and, then, thou shouldst begin, with shame, the last place, to occupy.
texts.luk.14.10: But, whensoever thou hast been invited, pass on and fall back into the last place, that, whensoever he that hath invited thee shall come, he may say unto thee—Friend! come close up, higher. Then, shalt thou have honour before all who are reclining together with thee.
texts.luk.14.11: Because, everyone who exalteth himself, shall be abased; and, he that abaseth himself, shall be exalted?
texts.luk.14.12: Moreover he went on to say, unto him also who had invited him,—Whensoever thou mayest be making a dinner or a supper, do not call thy friends, or thy brothers, or thy kinsfolk, or rich neighbours,—lest once, they also, invite thee in return, and it become a recompense unto thee.
texts.luk.14.13: But, whensoever, an entertainment, thou mayest be making, invite the destitute, the tried, the lame, the blind;
texts.luk.14.14: and, happy, shalt thou be, that they have not wherewith to recompense thee, for it shall be recompensed unto thee, in the resurrection of the righteous.
texts.luk.14.15: And one of those reclining together, hearing these things, said unto him—Happy, whoever shall eat bread in the kingdom of God!
texts.luk.14.16: But, he, said unto him—A certain man, was making a great supper, and invited many;
texts.luk.14.17: and he sent out his servant, at the hour of the supper, to say unto the invited—Be coming! because, even now, is it, ready.
texts.luk.14.18: And they all began, one after another to excuse themselves. The first, said unto him—A field, have I bought, and have need to go out and see it: I request thee, hold me excused.
texts.luk.14.19: And, another, said—Five yoke of oxen, have I bought, and am going my way to prove them; I request thee, hold me excused.
texts.luk.14.20: And, another, said—A wife, have I married, and, for this cause, I cannot come!
texts.luk.14.21: And, going near, the servant reported unto his lord these things. Then, provoked to anger, the master of the house said unto his servant—Go out quickly, into the broadways and streets of the city,—and, the destitute, and tried, and blind, and lame, bring thou in here.
texts.luk.14.22: And the servant said—Lord! what thou didst order, hath been done; and, yet, there is, room.
texts.luk.14.23: And the lord said unto the servant—Go out among the highways and fences, and compel them to come in; that my house may be filled.
texts.luk.14.24: For, I say unto you—Not one of those men who had been invited, shall taste of my supper.
texts.luk.14.25: And there were journeying together with him many multitudes; and, turning, he said unto them—
texts.luk.14.26: If anyone cometh unto me, and hateth not his own father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, further also, even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.
texts.luk.14.27: Whoever beareth not his own cross, and cometh after me, cannot be my disciple.
texts.luk.14.28: For, who from among you, wishing to build a tower, doth not first sit down and count the cost,—whether he hath sufficient for completion;
texts.luk.14.29: lest once, he having laid a foundation, and not being able to finish, all who are looking on, should begin to mock at him,
texts.luk.14.30: saying—This man, began to build, and was not able to finish!
texts.luk.14.31: Or, what king, moving on to encounter, another king, in battle, will not sit down first and take counsel, whether he is able, with ten thousand, to meet him who, with twenty thousand, is coming against him.
texts.luk.14.32: And, if not, by any means, while he is yet afar off, he sendeth, an embassy, and requesteth the conditions of peace.
texts.luk.14.33: Thus, therefore, everyone from amongst you, who doth not bid adieu unto all his own possessions, cannot be my disciple.
texts.luk.14.34: Good, therefore is the salt; but, if, even the salt, become tasteless, wherewith shall it be seasoned?
texts.luk.14.35: Neither for land nor for manure, is it, fit: outside, they cast it! He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.luk.15.1: But all the tax-collectors and the sinners were, unto him, drawing near, to be hearkening unto him;
texts.luk.15.2: and both the Pharisees and the Scribes were murmuring, saying, This man, unto sinners, giveth welcome, and eateth with them.
texts.luk.15.3: And he spake unto them this parable, saying—
texts.luk.15.4: What man from among you, having a hundred sheep, and losing, from among them, one, doth not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go his way after the lost one, until he find it?
texts.luk.15.5: And, finding it, he layeth it upon his shoulders, rejoicing;
texts.luk.15.6: and, coming unto his house, calleth together the friends and the neighbours, saying unto them—Rejoice with me! because I have found my sheep that was lost!
texts.luk.15.7: I say unto you—Thus, joy in heaven, will there be, over one sinner repenting, rather than over ninety-nine righteous persons, who indeed have, no need, of repentance.
texts.luk.15.8: Or, what woman, having, ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a lamp, and sweep the house, and seek carefully, until she find it?
texts.luk.15.9: And, having found it, she calleth together her female friends and neighbours, saying—Rejoice with me! because I have found the piece of silver which I had lost.
texts.luk.15.10: Thus, I say unto you, there ariseth joy in presence of the messengers of God, over one sinner repenting.
texts.luk.15.11: And he said—A certain man, had two sons.
texts.luk.15.12: And the younger of them said unto the father—Father! give me the share that falleth to me, of what there is. And, he, divided unto them the living.
texts.luk.15.13: And, after not many days, the younger son, gathering all together, left home for a country far away, and, there, squandered his substance with riotous living.
texts.luk.15.14: And, when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine throughout that country,—and, he, began to be in want.
texts.luk.15.15: And he went his way, and joined himself unto one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to be feeding swine.
texts.luk.15.16: And he used to long to be filled with the pods which the swine were eating; and, no man, was giving unto him.
texts.luk.15.17: But coming, to himself, he said—How many hired servants of my father, have bread enough and to spare, whereas, I, with famine, here, am perishing!
texts.luk.15.18: I will arise, and go unto my father, and will say unto him—Father! I have sinned against heaven, and before thee:
texts.luk.15.19: No longer, am I worthy to be called a son of thine,—Make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came unto his own father.
texts.luk.15.20: Now, while yet he was holding afar off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and, running, fell upon his neck, and tenderly kissed him.
texts.luk.15.21: And the son said unto him—Father! I have sinned against heaven, and before thee: No longer, am I worthy to be called a son of thine,— [make me as one of thy hired servants.]
texts.luk.15.22: But the father said unto his servants—Quick! bring forth a robe—the best! and put on him, and get out a ring for his hand, and sandals for his feet.
texts.luk.15.23: And be bringing the fatted calf, sacrifice! and let us eat and make merry:
texts.luk.15.24: Because, this my son, was, dead, and hath come to life again, was lost, and is found. And they began to be making merry.
texts.luk.15.25: But his elder son was in a field; and, as, in coming, he drew near unto the house, he heard music and dancing,—
texts.luk.15.26: and, calling near one of the youths, he inquired what these things, could be.
texts.luk.15.27: And, he, said unto him,—Thy brother, hath come, and thy father hath sacrificed the fatted calf, because, safe and sound, hath he received him back.
texts.luk.15.28: But he was provoked to anger, and would not go in. And, his father, coming out, began to entreat him.
texts.luk.15.29: But, he, answering said unto his father—Lo! so many years as these, do I serve thee, and, at no time, a commandment of thine, have I transgressed,—And, unto me, at no time, hast thou given a kid, that, with my friends, I might make merry;
texts.luk.15.30: But, when, this thy son, who had devoured thy living with harlots, came, thou didst sacrifice, for him, the fatted calf;
texts.luk.15.31: But, he, said unto him—Child! thou, always, art, with me, and, all that is mine, is, thine;
texts.luk.15.32: But, to make merry and rejoice, there was need, because, this thy brother—was, dead, and hath come to life again, and was lost, and is found.
texts.luk.16.1: And he went on to say, unto his disciples also,—There was, a certain rich man, who had a steward, and, the same, was accused to him as squandering his goods.
texts.luk.16.2: And, accosting him, he said unto him—What is this I hear of thee? Render the account of thy stewardship, for thou canst no longer be steward.
texts.luk.16.3: And the steward said within himself—What shall I do, because my lord taketh away the stewardship from me? Dig, I cannot: to beg, I am ashamed.
texts.luk.16.4: I know what I will do, that, when I am removed out of the stewardship, they may welcome me into their own houses.
texts.luk.16.5: And, calling unto him each one of the debtors of his own lord, he was saying unto the first,—How much owest thou my lord?
texts.luk.16.6: And, he, said—A hundred baths of oil. And, he, said unto him—Kindly take thine accounts, and, sitting down, make haste and write—Fifty!
texts.luk.16.7: After that, unto another, he said—And how much owest, thou? And, he, said—A hundred homers of wheat. He saith unto him—Kindly take thine accounts, and write—Eighty!
texts.luk.16.8: And the lord praised the unrighteous steward, in that with forethought he acted:—Because, the sons of this age, have more forethought than the sons of light, respecting their own generation.
texts.luk.16.9: And, I, unto you, say—For yourselves, make ye friends, with the unjust Riches, in order that, as soon as it shall fail, they may welcome you into the age-abiding tents.
texts.luk.16.10: The faithful in least, in much also, is, faithful, and, he that in least is unrighteous, in much also, is, unrighteous.
texts.luk.16.11: If therefore, in the unjust Riches ye proved unfaithful, the true, who, unto you, will entrust?
texts.luk.16.12: And, if, in what was another’s, ye proved unfaithful, your own, who will give unto you?
texts.luk.16.13: No domestic, can, unto two masters, be in service; for either, the one, he will hate, and, the other, love, or, unto the one, he will hold, and, the other, despise: Ye cannot, unto God, be in service, and unto Riches.
texts.luk.16.14: Now the Pharisees, who were, lovers of money, were hearing all these things, and were openly sneering at him.
texts.luk.16.15: And he said unto them—Ye, are they who justify themselves before men, but, God, knoweth your hearts; because, that which amongst men is lofty, is an abomination before God.
texts.luk.16.16: The law and the prophets, were until John,—from that time, the good news of the kingdom of God, is being proclaimed, and, everyone, thereinto, is forcing his way.
texts.luk.16.17: But it is, easier, for heaven and earth to pass away, than that, of the law, one little point, should fail.
texts.luk.16.18: Every one divorcing his wife and marrying another, committeth adultery; and, he that marrieth a woman divorced from a husband, committeth adultery.
texts.luk.16.19: Now, a certain man, was rich, and he used to clothe himself with purple and fine linen, making merry day by day, brilliantly.
texts.luk.16.20: And, a certain beggar, by name Lazarus, used to be cast near his gate, full of sores,
texts.luk.16.21: and to long to be fed from the crumbs that fell from the table of the rich man: nay! even, the dogs, used to come and lick his sores.
texts.luk.16.22: And it came to pass that the beggar died, and was carried away by the messengers, into the bosom of Abraham. And, the rich man also, died, and was buried.
texts.luk.16.23: And, in hades, lifting up his eyes, being in torments, he seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
texts.luk.16.24: And, he, calling out, said—Father Abraham! have mercy upon me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue,—because I am in anguish in this flame.
texts.luk.16.25: But Abraham said—Child! remember—That thou didst duly received thy good things in thy life, and, Lazarus, in like manner, the evil things; but, now, here, he is comforted, and, thou, art in anguish.
texts.luk.16.26: And, besides all these things, betwixt us and you, a great chasm, hath been fixed,—so that, they who might wish to cross over from hence unto you, should not be able, nor any, from thence unto us, be crossing over.
texts.luk.16.27: But he said—I request thee then, father, that thou wouldst send him unto my father’s house,—
texts.luk.16.28: for I have five brethren;—that he may solemnly testify unto them, lest, they also, come into this place of torment.
texts.luk.16.29: But Abraham saith—They have Moses and the Prophets: Let them hearken unto them.
texts.luk.16.30: But, he, said—Nay! father Abraham, but, if one, from the dead, should go unto them, they would repent.
texts.luk.16.31: But he said unto him—If, unto Moses and the Prophets, they do not hearken, neither, if one, from among the dead, should arise, would they be persuaded.
texts.luk.17.1: And he said unto his disciples:—It is, impossible, that occasions of stumbling should not come, notwithstanding, alas! for him through whom they do come:
texts.luk.17.2: It profiteth him, if, a mill-stone, is hung about his neck, and he is cast into the sea, than that he cause, one, of these little ones, to stumble.
texts.luk.17.3: Be taking heed to yourselves,—If thy brother sin, rebuke him, and, if he repent, forgive him;
texts.luk.17.4: Even if, seven times a day, he sin against thee, and, seven times, turn to thee, saying, I repent, thou shalt forgive him.
texts.luk.17.5: And the apostles said unto the Lord—Bestow on us faith!
texts.luk.17.6: And the Lord said—If ye have faith like a grain of mustard-seed, ye should be saying unto [this] mulberry-tree—Be uprooted! and be planted in the sea,—and it should obey you.
texts.luk.17.7: But, who from among you, having, a servant, plowing or keeping sheep, when he hath come in out of the field, will say to him—Straightway, come, and recline;—
texts.luk.17.8: on the contrary, will not say to him—Make somewhat ready, that I may dine,—and, girding thyself, be ministering unto me, until I have eaten and drunk; and, after these things, thou, shalt eat and drink?
texts.luk.17.9: Doth he offer thanks unto the servant, because he hath done the things enjoined?
texts.luk.17.10: Thus, ye also, when ye have done all the things enjoined upon you, say—Unprofitable servants, are we,—What we were bound to do, we have done!
texts.luk.17.11: And it came to pass, during the journey unto Jerusalem, that, he, was going through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
texts.luk.17.12: And, as he was entering into a certain village, there met him ten leprous men, who stood still, afar off;
texts.luk.17.13: and, they, lifted up a voice, saying—Jesus! Master! have mercy on us!
texts.luk.17.14: And, beholding, he said unto them—Go your way, and show yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, as they withdrew, they were cleansed.
texts.luk.17.15: But, one from among them, beholding that he was healed, returned, with a loud voice, glorifying God,—
texts.luk.17.16: and fell prostrate at his feet, giving him thanks; and, he, was a Samaritan.
texts.luk.17.17: And Jesus, answering, said—Were not, the ten, cleansed? [but,] where, are, the nine?
texts.luk.17.18: Have none been found returning to give glory to God, save this one of another race?
texts.luk.17.19: And he said unto him—Arise and go thy way: thy faith, hath saved thee.
texts.luk.17.20: And, being questioned by the Pharisees, When cometh the kingdom of God? he answered them and said—The kingdom of God cometh not with narrow watching;
texts.luk.17.21: Neither shall they say—Lo, here! or, There. For lo! the kingdom of God, is, among you.
texts.luk.17.22: But he said unto the disciples—There will come days—when ye will long to see, one of the days of the Son of Man, and shall not see.
texts.luk.17.23: And they will say unto you, Lo there! or, Lo here! Do not [depart, and do not] pursue.
texts.luk.17.24: For, just as, the lightning, flashing out of the one part under heaven, unto the other part under heaven, shineth, so, shall be, the Son of Man.
texts.luk.17.25: But, first, he must needs suffer, many things, and be rejected by this generation.
texts.luk.17.26: And, as it came to pass in the days of Noah, so, will it be, even in the days of the Son of Man:
texts.luk.17.27: They were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage,—until the day that Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
texts.luk.17.28: In like manner, as it came to pass in the days of Lot, They were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building,—
texts.luk.17.29: But, on the day Lot came out from Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all:—
texts.luk.17.30: According to the same things, will it be on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
texts.luk.17.31: In that day, he that shall be on the housetop, and his utensils in the house, let him not go down, to take them away! And, he that is in the field, in like manner, let him not turn unto the things behind,
texts.luk.17.32: Bear in mind the wife of Lot! Whosoever shall seek to make his life his own, shall lose it,
texts.luk.17.33: But, whosoever shall lose it, shall give it a living birth.
texts.luk.17.34: I say unto you—On the selfsame night, there shall be two men on [one] bed,—the one, shall be taken near, and, the other, left behind;
texts.luk.17.35: There shall be two women grinding together,—the one, shall be taken near, and, the other, left behind.
texts.luk.17.37: And, answering, they say unto him—Where, Lord? And, he, said unto them—Where the body is, there, the vultures also, will be gathered together.
texts.luk.18.1: And he was speaking a parable unto them, as to its being needful for them always to pray, and not be faint-hearted;
texts.luk.18.2: saying—A certain judge, there was in a certain city,—having, for God, no reverence, and, for man, no respect.
texts.luk.18.3: And, a widow, there was, in that city; and she kept coming unto him, saying—Vindicate me from mine adversary!
texts.luk.18.4: And he was unwilling for a time; but, after these things, he said within himself—Although, neither God, I reverence, nor man, I respect,
texts.luk.18.5: Yet, if only because this widow annoyeth me, I will vindicate her,—lest, persistently coming, she wholly wear me out.
texts.luk.18.6: And the Lord said—Hear ye what, the unrighteous judge saith;—
texts.luk.18.7: And shall, God, in any wise not execute the vindication of his chosen ones, who are crying out to him day and night, although he beareth long with regard to them?
texts.luk.18.8: I tell you—He will execute their vindication, quickly! nevertheless, though, the Son of Man, do come, will he, after all, find the faith on the earth?
texts.luk.18.9: And he spake, even unto certain who were confident in themselves that they were righteous, and were despising the rest, this parable:—
texts.luk.18.10: Two men, went up into the temple to pray, one, a Pharisee, and, the other, a tax-collector.
texts.luk.18.11: The Pharisee, taking his stand, these things unto himself was praying: O God! I thank thee, that I am not like the rest of men,—extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or, even as this tax-collector;
texts.luk.18.12: I fast twice in the week, I give a tenth of whatsoever things I gain!
texts.luk.18.13: But, the tax-collector, afar off, standing,—would not so much as lift up, his eyes, unto heaven, but kept smiting his own breast saying—O God! be propitiated unto me, the sinner!
texts.luk.18.14: I tell you—This one went down justified, unto his house, rather than that one; because, every one who exalteth himself, shall be abased, but, he that abaseth himself, shall be exalted?
texts.luk.18.15: And they were bringing unto him, even the babes, that he might touch, them; but the disciples, seeing it, began to rebuke them.
texts.luk.18.16: But, Jesus, called them near, saying—Suffer, the children, to be coming unto me, and do not hinder them; for, of such, is the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.18.17: Verily I say unto you—Whosoever shall not welcome the kingdom of God, as a child, in nowise shall enter thereinto.
texts.luk.18.18: And a certain, ruler, questioned him, saying—Good Teacher! by doing what, shall I inherit life age-abiding?
texts.luk.18.19: But Jesus said to him—Why, callest thou me, good? None, is good, save one—God.
texts.luk.18.20: The commandments, thou knowest:—Do not commit adultery, Do not commit murder, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness,—Honour thy father and mother,
texts.luk.18.21: And, he, said—All these things, have I kept from my youth.
texts.luk.18.22: And Jesus, hearing, said unto him—Yet one thing, unto thee, is lacking: Whatsoever thou hast, sell, and distribute unto the destitute,—and thou shalt have treasure in [the] heavens; and come! be following me.
texts.luk.18.23: But, he, hearing these things, became, encompassed with grief; for he was rich exceedingly.
texts.luk.18.24: And Jesus, beholding him, said—With what difficulty, shall, they who have money, enter, into the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.18.25: For it is, easier, for a camel, to enter, through the eye of a needle, than for, a rich man, to enter, into the kingdom of God.
texts.luk.18.26: And they who heard said—Who, then, can be saved?
texts.luk.18.27: And, he, said—The things impossible with men, are, possible with God.
texts.luk.18.28: And Peter said—Lo! we, have left our own possessions, and followed thee!
texts.luk.18.29: And, he, said unto them—Verily, I say unto you—No one, is there, who hath left—house, or wife, or brethren, or parents, or children,—for the sake of the kingdom of God;
texts.luk.18.30: who shall in anywise not receive manifold in this season, and, in the age that is coming, life age-abiding.
texts.luk.18.31: And, taking aside the twelve, he said unto them—Lo! we are going up unto Jerusalem, and all the things will be finished, which have been written through means of the prophets, respecting the Son of Man;
texts.luk.18.32: For he will be delivered up unto the nations, and be mocked, and insulted, and spit upon,—
texts.luk.18.33: and, having scourged him, they will slay him, and, on the third day, will, he, arise.
texts.luk.18.34: And, they, not one of these things, understood, and this saying was hidden from them, and the could not comprehend the things spoken.
texts.luk.18.35: And it came to pass, as he was drawing near unto Jericho, a certain blind man, was sitting beside the road, begging.
texts.luk.18.36: And. hearkening unto a multitude moving along, he enquired, what this, might be.
texts.luk.18.37: And they told him—Jesus of Nazareth, is passing by!
texts.luk.18.38: And he cried aloud, saying—Jesus, son of David! have mercy upon me!
texts.luk.18.39: And, they that were going before, began to rebuke him, that he might hold his peace. But, he, by so much the more, was crying out—O Son of David! have mercy upon me!
texts.luk.18.40: And, standing still, Jesus commanded him to be led unto him; and, when he had drawn near, he questioned him—
texts.luk.18.41: What desirest thou, I should do unto thee? And, he, said—Lord! …that I may recover sight!
texts.luk.18.42: And, Jesus, said unto him—Recover sight! Thy faith, hath saved thee.
texts.luk.18.43: And, instantly, he recovered sight, and began to follow him, glorifying God. And, all the people, beholding, gave praise unto God.
texts.luk.19.1: And, having entered, he was passing through Jericho;
texts.luk.19.2: and lo! a man, by name called Zacchaeus, and, he, was a chief tax-collector, and [he] was rich.
texts.luk.19.3: And he was seeking to see Jesus, what sort of man he was, and could not for the multitude, because, in stature, he was, small.
texts.luk.19.4: And, running forward unto the front, he got up a sycamore-tree, that he might see him; for, by that way, was he about to pass.
texts.luk.19.5: And, as he came up to the place, looking up, Jesus said unto him—Zacchaeus! make haste, and come down; For, to-day, in thy house, I must needs abide.
texts.luk.19.6: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
texts.luk.19.7: And all, when they beheld, began to murmur, saying—With a sinful man, hath he gone in to lodge!
texts.luk.19.8: But, taking his stand, Zacchaeus said unto the Lord—Lo! the half of my possessions, Lord, unto the destitute, I give; and, if, from anyone, I have taken aught by false accusation, I give back fourfold.
texts.luk.19.9: And Jesus said unto him—This day, salvation, unto this house, hath come,—for that, he too, is, a son of Abraham;
texts.luk.19.10: For the Son of Man came, to seek and to save what was lost.
texts.luk.19.11: And, because they were hearing these things, he added and spake a parable, because of his being near Jerusalem, and their supposing that, instantly, was the kingdom of God to shine forth.
texts.luk.19.12: He said, therefore—A certain man, of noble birth, went into a country far away, to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
texts.luk.19.13: And, calling ten servants of his own, he gave unto them ten minas, and said unto them—Do business, till I come.
texts.luk.19.14: But, his citizens, hated him, and sent off an embassy after him, saying—We desire not, this, man, to be made king over us!
texts.luk.19.15: And it came to pass, when he returned, having received the kingdom, that he bade be called unto him these servants, to whom he had given the silver, that he might take note, what business they had done.
texts.luk.19.16: And the first came near, saying—Lord! thy mina, hath made, ten minas.
texts.luk.19.17: And he said to him—Well done! good servant. Because, in a very small thing, thou hast been, faithful, have thou authority over, ten cities.
texts.luk.19.18: And the second came, saying—Thy mina, lord, hath made five minas.
texts.luk.19.19: And he said, to him also, And, thou, be over five cities.
texts.luk.19.20: And, the other, came, saying—Lord, lo! thy mina, which I kept lying by in a napkin;
texts.luk.19.21: For I was afraid of thee, because, a harsh man, thou art,—Thou takest up, what thou layedst not down, and reapest, what thou sowedst not!
texts.luk.19.22: He saith to him—Out of thy mouth, do I judge thee, O wicked servant! Thou knewest that, I, a harsh man, am,—taking up, what I laid not down, and reaping, what I did not sow;
texts.luk.19.23: Wherefore, then, didst thou not place my silver upon a [money-changer’s] table, and, I, when I came, with interest might have exacted it?
texts.luk.19.24: And, unto the by-standers, he said—Take, from him, the mina, and give unto him that hath, the ten minas;—
texts.luk.19.25: And they said to him, Lord! he hath ten minas;—
texts.luk.19.26: I tell you—Unto everyone that hath, shall be given, whereas, from him that hath not, even what he hath, shall be taken away.
